Measles is one of the most contagious diseases in the world.

It’s also one of the most preventable.

As a doctor, let me be clear up front: Measles can’t be cured or prevented with Vitamin A or cod liver oil. The _only_ reliable way to stop its spread is through vaccination.

So it’s both frustrating and frightening when avoidable public health outbreaks like this occur:

---
This isn’t random. It’s the direct result of stripping away public health programs and funding that used to keep outbreaks like this from happening in the first place — and the dangerous and widespread disinformation about vaccines this administration spreads.

**Bottom line: the record-high measles outbreak happening in our country is the result of putting someone in charge of our public health infrastructure who doesn't understand medicine, and who actively undermines science and experts. **

I care deeply about public health as a physician, as a mom, and as a human being. And I know exactly what vaccine misinformation costs — not in dollars, but in people's lives.

Before the measles vaccine, hundreds of children used to die every year from measles, thousands were hospitalized, and many suffered lifelong consequences. This new outbreak has already tragically cost two unvaccinated school-aged children their lives.

We don’t have to go back to a time when kids were dying from a disease that modern medicine solved decades ago. We just need leaders who trust doctors and believe in science over conspiracy theories.

**I will continue fighting the disinformation coming from Trump and RFK Jr, and I could really use you by my side — because the more voices we can add to the chorus, the more likely it is we will make a real impact.**

Hey friend — Deb here.
I know my team and I have been emailing you a lot lately, but today I am reaching out personally to ask for your input: [**Will you be one of the _FIRST_ to join my official Healthcare Survey and share your thoughts with me?**](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16267?refcode=jtk1219-su-nd&code=jtk1219-su-nd&t=3&akid=11975%2E400544%2Exl2Zk0)

---
Attacks on healthcare are personal to me. I know what it feels like to wonder how you’ll afford a doctor’s appointment, stare down a medical bill you can’t pay, and rely on programs like Planned Parenthood, WIC, and Medicaid to make sure your family gets the care it needs.
Right now, accessible healthcare is under attack. Donald Trump’s policies are dismantling the healthcare system New Mexicans rely on. When his Medicaid cuts take effect in 2027, more than five rural hospitals could close, families could lose coverage, clinics could be forced to cut services, and healthcare workers could lose their jobs. For rural New Mexicans, that could mean driving hours for care that used to be available close to home.

_That’s why New Mexicans need a Governor who will stand up to this agenda, not help bring it here._

My Republican opponent will bring Donald Trump’s dangerous agenda to New Mexico. He’s taking his cues from Trump, who has already made life harder for New Mexicans by cutting healthcare, food assistance, and other programs families rely on. He won’t stand up to Trump or fight to protect these programs — _and he’s even promised to work with extremist Texas Gov. Greg Abbott to restrict reproductive healthcare._ **Meanwhile, I will fight to protect the healthcare New Mexicans rely on.**
As Governor, I’ll fight to protect reproductive freedom, lower healthcare costs, and make sure every New Mexican can get care close to home. But I’ve always believed that good leaders listen first. [**Friend, your perspective is critical to this campaign. Please take two minutes to share your healthcare priorities with me today.**](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16267?refcode=jtk1219-su-nd&code=jtk1219-su-nd&t=6&akid=11975%2E400544%2Exl2Zk0)

When his Medicaid cuts take effect in 2027, more than five rural hospitals could close, families could lose coverage, clinics could be forced to cut services, and healthcare workers could lose their jobs. For rural New Mexicans, that could mean driving hours for care that used to be available close to home. That’s why New Mexicans need a Governor who will stand up to this agenda, not help bring it here. My Republican opponent will bring Donald Trump’s dangerous agenda to New Mexico. He’s taking his cues from Trump, who has already made life harder for New Mexicans by cutting healthcare, food assistance, and other programs families rely on. He won’t stand up to Trump or fight to protect these programs — and he’s even promised to work with extremist Texas Gov. Greg Abbott to restrict reproductive healthcare. Meanwhile, I will fight to protect the healthcare New Mexicans rely on. As Governor, I’ll fight to protect reproductive freedom, lower healthcare costs, and make sure every New Mexican can get care close to home. But I’ve always believed that good leaders listen first. | | Thank you for your valuable input. – Deb | | | | | |

body:
Taking the fight to the next step

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/de2b1cd69aea/breaking-news-citizens-only-voting-amendment-submitted-to-board-of-canvassers-8371916?e=ecf60db114)

| | | | | [DONATE TODAY](https://us.list-manage.com/17qC0Vsf0ZT?e=ecf60db114&c2id=b020b7081f44f277164dc2a0d73e83a2)
---
|

| |

Dear Supporters,
Yesterday was a difficult and deeply disappointing day for Citizen Only Voting Michigan and for the more than 700,000 Michiganders who signed our petition.
Despite the evidence presented in support of certification, the Michigan Board of State Canvassers deadlocked on placing the Michigan Citizen Only Voting Amendment on the November 3 ballot.
Throughout this process, we have maintained that we have the signatures and that every valid petition signature deserves to be fairly considered. That principle became especially important in the cases of 23 Michigan voters who took the extraordinary additional step of submitting notarized affidavits confirming that they personally signed our petition.
Even then, five of those signatures were rejected despite Bureau of Elections staff and all four members of the Board acknowledging on the record that the individuals are registered Michigan voters and that the signatures on their affidavits match signatures contained in the Qualified Voter File.
Think about that for a moment.
These are registered voters who came forward personally, swore under oath that they signed our petition and provided signatures matching their official voter records. We believe that should represent the strongest possible confirmation that a voter signed a petition and intended for his or her voice to be heard.
We are deeply disappointed by the Board's deadlock, but yesterday's meeting does not end the legal process.
Because the Board was unable to certify the petition, we will now take this matter to the Michigan Supreme Court. There, we will continue to defend the validity of these petition signatures and the right of Michigan voters to have their signatures fairly considered.
However, taking this case to the Michigan Supreme Court will require significant legal resources. For those who wish to financially support the costs associated with this legal effort, contributions to Citizen Only Voting Michigan will help cover legal fees and other expenses related to the court proceedings.
Whatever happens next, we want you to know how grateful we are for everyone who has been part of this effort and gotten us this far. More than 700,000 Michiganders put their names on these petitions. Thousands more helped circulate petitions, collected signatures, attended events, contributed resources and followed this process every step of the way.
That extraordinary effort deserves to be recognized.
In the meantime, stay tuned. We will keep you informed as the case moves forward and will share developments as they happen. We will also share tools and resources to help us get our message out. We have the signatures and they should be fairly considered.
Thank you for standing with us and for everything you have done to bring Citizen Only Voting this far.
Sincerely,**Citizen Only Voting Michigan Team**
**P.S. If you can, please consider contributing $1, $5, $10, $25 or more, every dollar helps fund the upcoming legal battle!**

Hey Peter,

If you haven’t already, you’ll likely start seeing MAGA Republicans use my
full name a lot more in the coming weeks: Abdulrahman Mohamed El-Sayed.

Donald Trump has already started using it as if it’s a punchline. ̄\_(
ツ)_/ ̄

Peter, I’ve
spent the majority of my career being someone who’s relatively young,
relatively brown, and relatively Muslim. Something I’ve learned along the
way is that when someone reaches for your name instead of your record,
it's because your record is the thing they can't touch:

* I’ve helped make government agencies actually work for Michiganders —
first by rebuilding Detroit’s Health Department after bankruptcy, and
then restructuring Wayne County’s Department of Health, Human &
Veterans Services.
* As a public servant, I’ve removed lead from elementary schools, taken
on Michigan’s biggest polluters, and made life-saving Narcan
universally accessible.

There’s nothing for them to attack there — so that’s why they’re resorting
to a politics rooted in hatred instead.

Meanwhile, Mike Rogers has a record he'd rather Michiganders never look at
too closely:

* Mike Rogers voted to raise his own pay in Congress.
* He championed a bill that helped create the opioid crisis.
* Then, after spending 15 years in Washington, he left and got $14
million richer working for the very corporations he used to regulate,
then moved to Florida.

And that’s why Mike Rogers needs $51,000,000+ worth of help to have a
chance at beating us in November.

We’re never going to outraise $51 million, but we don’t have to. We just
need folks to pitch in $10 to help us respond to their
attacks and get our message in front of as many Michiganders as possible.
If we do that, we will win. [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260825-3-ak.o_RUNe&amount=10&refcode=em20260825-3014&t=1004&akid=3020%2E251025%2EKAY9m0 ]Can I count on your support,
Peter?

In solidarity,

Abdul

| | | I sat down with _New York Times_ columnist Ezra Klein for one of the longest interviews I've ever done.
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137923915/642426384/724950626?refcode=260825-ezraklein-rs&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NTkyOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlZTVkNjFkZC1mMWEwLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=agDMiIlDPQFeSQYl0zqhERZzuXWmOsRP6OAEqyhDxCA=)
---
It's been a funny experience. People suddenly seem fascinated by this idea that an auto repair and machine shop owner from Skamania County wound up in Congress. _But honestly... I'm not sure I'm all that interesting._ I still wake up in the same house, work at the same shop with my husband, and struggle to find child care. I still worry about whether small businesses can survive. I still believe if the government writes a rule that doesn't make sense, we ought to fix it. The cameras leave. The work continues. Sometimes I think Washington, D.C. forgets that. Politics has become so focused on the next headline that we've stopped asking whether anything actually works. I didn't run for Congress because I wanted to become famous. **I ran for office because I got tired of watching practical problems pile up while everyone argued about them.** That's why I'm still in this fight. _If more people are paying attention now, I hope they're paying attention to that._ Because Congress doesn't need more personalities. It needs more people willing to roll up their sleeves. **[If you think so too, I could use your support. Please chip in $5, $10, or whatever you can afford to help me keep working away at the clunker that is DC.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137923916/642426385/724950626?refcode=260825-ezraklein-rs&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NTkyOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlZTVkNjFkZC1mMWEwLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=agDMiIlDPQFeSQYl0zqhERZzuXWmOsRP6OAEqyhDxCA=) **

We got word about a brand-new poll here in North Carolina, and it’s not
looking good:

Following the millions of dollars the GOP has been pouring into attack ads
against me, a brand-new poll out last week that shows Michael Whatley and
I are statistically tied. If that’s all you need to hear today, please use
this link to split a donation between our campaign and Chris Pappas and
stop them from taking the lead:

this seat, we’ll lose our chance at taking back the U.S. Senate majority.

This new poll only confirms what we’ve known all along: this is going to

I’ve been a top target for national Republicans all cycle. So far, GOP

Fellow Patriot -

I never expected to be running for office. I have never had any desire to be a politician. I am doing this because I am answering President Donald Trump's call to serve and want to stand up for South Carolina and fight for his agenda.

_**Like Lindsey, I am a hard worker with a servant's heart.**_ We grew up in the back of a bar and liquor store, in one room. Our parents worked hard every day to make ends meet - there was no time for sickness and few vacations, because if the doors weren't open, no money was coming in.

What I've spent my life doing is serving South Carolina - including running a state agency with 130 employees and a $90 million budget. We turned it from a struggling organization into a national model helping people find work and live independently. We made sure all spending was reasonable, allowable, and necessary. _I fought against duplication of services, knowing it wasted taxpayers' dollars_.

_**I'm a mother, a grandmother, and a wife, and now South Carolina's first female United States Senator,[who is humbly asking for your support.](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=f8058d593b49445ca3376330cb469d98&_e=ckym_QkG6SZfZ4AuLlXUkcSNVpMlVeJUXA3QKjqvi2moMJaO64VEylRl0otCmnRjllE6t3b0-rkV_erGNKRAofysTqmKm0-ZiHZL4Ld3jOM33zcSQ0T4sRF0cXXW4V3eAIse8iZlGjz7zdvG_1FPNxms5uTmxc18rthnEMXzqfHBpIR1-v7H98blKCfa_pWqVrXeRJwSa4WVaZvyDOtTNWnLP9ihgt-cqc5scYYo7-566UJ7266D7YsXSzBCME-p_M_HNsW9XmL2S00hhjg76sflclZmSUBA18YOBU10haVaCz-CPo28Zze6l5SB10MTRbCrEPiNbym7GL5rS3lQguT5KcPeDpP7pHPwKzX0k0cH4Vca0u9dhsqWX470H37CWHb85RfgM62mTJqFjbgpf_lsGQq8pWUUL7iBxPJdftvdJQujp-zhRidVNZFbkUtbuwyRCuBQp9e6cCsXbu4O4Ms02FBB3VW4FZKLc8MgMeVoFsBs2guv4sCw_fHfsyKGmUYnvcu9Ws1XEdHiATtfSR6BgDuHzi02XL0FChn69Hf2DODv-ReCStxf4d2MjfHZDJBqNBuCwMVHqfPCOH8cRRbAHu_484yUu-700vnAsWhZRI67siRQVsR3iEWMR54OoxsV0aQk4UlvueN0X2Gzn5Ep74PyCGKrj_sFi1H0IGKCpPR6KM0DMr9fVnhLN75tJKHDxEFxH4zAvL-ozznyFA9BVzGLAbCCVVSIsJv7649RwMDE6UPbWjYngAOIBEEQw1svDCY5hKHft5YcS6IspQ%3D%3D)**_

I know how to bargain shop, and I look for the buy-one-get-one-free sales at the grocery store. I just bought a new pair of shoes to walk around the U.S. Capitol off the clearance rack at the Shoe Warehouse. I cut my own grass with a push mower, and yes, I know how to use a weed eater.

I support the Right to Life.
I believe in showing ID to vote to save our country.
I oppose DEI.
I think AOC is C-R-A-Z-Y.
I think Anthony Fauci should stop staring at the floor and answer the questions.
I stand for the national anthem.
I believe our veterans are heroes.
I will always Back the Blue.
**And I know that President Trump and I will Make America Great Again.**
I am the first woman United States senator in South Carolina history. _**My Democratic opponent, Dr. Annie Andrews, must not be the second.**_

clean_body: I never expected to be running for office. I have never had any desire to be a politician. | Peter - I never expected to be running for office. I have never had any desire to be a politician. I am doing this because I am answering President Donald Trump's call to serve and want to stand up for South Carolina and fight for his agenda. Like Lindsey, I am a hard worker with a servant's heart. We grew up in the back of a bar and liquor store, in one room. Our parents worked hard every day to make ends meet - there was no time for sickness and few vacations, because if the doors weren't open, no money was coming in. What I've spent my life doing is serving South Carolina - including running a state agency with 130 employees and a $90 million budget. We turned it from a struggling organization into a national model helping people find work and live independently. We made sure all spending was reasonable, allowable, and necessary. I fought against duplication of services, knowing it wasted taxpayers' dollars. I'm a mother, a grandmother, and a wife, and now South Carolina's first female United States Senator, I know how to bargain shop, and I look for the buy-one-get-one-free sales at the grocery store. I just bought a new pair of shoes to walk around the U.S. Capitol off the clearance rack at the Shoe Warehouse. I cut my own grass with a push mower, and yes, I know how to use a weed eater. I support the Right to Life. I believe in showing ID to vote to save our country. I oppose DEI. I think AOC is C-R-A-Z-Y. I think Anthony Fauci should stop staring at the floor and answer the questions. I stand for the national anthem. I believe our veterans are heroes. I will always Back the Blue. And I know that President Trump and I will Make America Great Again. I am the first woman United States senator in South Carolina history. My Democratic opponent, Dr. Annie Andrews, must not be the second. She supports turning confused little boys into little girls and vice versa. name: Kylie Glatfelter
subject: Greg Ballard’s $2.5 Million Voter Guide Plan Is Redundant Government Waste
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY THE INDIANA REPUBLICAN STATE COMMITTEE
body:
INGOP Press Release No images? [Click here](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-e-ftldtn-hhlljjcji-h/) **For Immediate Release:** August 25, 2026**Contact:** Kylie Glatfelter, Communications Director, **[kglatfelter@indiana.gop](mailto:kglatfelter@indiana.gop)****Greg Ballard's $2.5 Million Voter Guide Plan Is Redundant Government Waste****Indianapolis, IN** - Greg Ballard is proposing a taxpayer-funded voter guide that would be mailed to every registered Indiana voter before each general election, along with a companion smartphone app.There's just one problem: Indiana already provides many of these services.Hoosiers already have access to statewide voter information, candidate lists and personalized ballot information through the Secretary of State's office and IndianaVoters.com. Nonprofit organizations also work to provide voters with election information and resources.Instead of working with nonprofits already providing voter resources or improving the services Indiana already has, Ballard's solution is to balloon state government with another taxpayer-funded program, which he says would cost an average of $2.5 million per year. Despite the $2.5 million annual price tag, Ballard has yet to provide a detailed budget explaining how it would be implemented, funded or sustained.Indiana Republican Party Chairwoman Lana Keesling said Ballard's proposal reflects a broader problem with his campaign: proposing new government programs without explaining what they would cost or whether they are necessary. "Greg Ballard is touting a 'first-of-its-kind' voter guide, but there's nothing innovative about asking Hoosier taxpayers to fund services Indiana already provides."Instead of finding ways to improve existing resources or work with organizations already doing this work, Ballard's answer is more government and more spending, without even providing Hoosiers a detailed budget for how he plans to pay for it."This is becoming a pattern. Greg Ballard and Beau Bayh are campaigning on big promises without explaining whether the Secretary of State's office can actually deliver them. Hoosiers deserve more than campaign promises. They deserve a Secretary of State who understands the office, respects their hard-earned tax dollars and makes government work better, not bigger."### [](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-ftldtn-hhlljjcji-r/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-ftldtn-hhlljjcji-y/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-ftldtn-hhlljjcji-j/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-ftldtn-hhlljjcji-t/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-ftldtn-hhlljjcji-i/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-ftldtn-hhlljjcji-d/) ** PAID FOR BY THE INDIANA REPUBLICAN STATE COMMITTEE. ****NOT AUTHORIZED BY ANY CANDIDATE OR CANDIDATE'S COMMITTEE. ****WWW.INDIANA.GOP.** | Indiana Republican State Committee 101 W. | Maura Healey Hopes We Forgot, But We Didn't!
People are voting with their feet by moving out of Massachusetts because of taxes!
A recent study from the [Massachusetts Opportunity Alliance](https://qgzxgy5ab.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001wOTFuinKY9HL68lr6mv9ELPrJkTp1H8gr9dpQCk74cpUyH2TKJA2--jmAitnXksMqLb7nSDHmUtjOA2jZfKIo4ZROR0JZXbveg6nth7nRAgK9MFvn2qf4OBgmrqjfveBpY79BSG3asZwsTeQb5CZCSgPzYFf9KQ2MsUUBuTMSgQLYhmtVjrZCCFHu_KrB0Ge-hGNW7wViIKgBfUiU0kfMzHcN2J80CRxVDkhT4ZMrOn6xeiK4jUgUg==&c=YNOSSs9AI7zIzZOHDDZn4uP1k1HfYRDdmbWh35rAtGrT4IsXnMbCew==&ch=VQm_2fZNCYJRx0qbNH09VSIGWKOwYFsksbbFvAvBcTQS06C13OPldg==) reports, "More than half said the state's tax burden played a leading role in their decision to move, while more than 80% said taxes are simply too high."
The same study found, "Nearly half of former residents pointed to rent or home prices as their biggest challenge, while roughly 1 in 5 cited utility costs."
Are you ready to make Massachusetts more affordable by electing more Republicans?

name: Jamie Davis
subject: A Black man could never win a statewide Louisiana election
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Jamie Davis for U
body:
Don’t tell me what’s “impossible” in Louisiana. My family worked this Delta land when they were slaves. Today my son and I farm the very same fields together - but now we own it.
| | | | | [](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001O90n5WAAwasUCrnMgNWpNbbU_xNit6RAPuW3_XBFfofcr2nI5H4Zt1UvfjzdhuMUDWRHySnjnFcLCo9fCDwuw7Flyi3Yiz-DJuLnnOlca2XclVxZN150XZUXgY1EAS2xFPq4bBNTXqfUYS3ST_Kh4B18_q1Z5502161PzWTu5nSqqyxlaWRyJ1W6Yi3zeYQCC9KDw2a5OY7y_8Uz2y6nCPcdmsvZTCaBcHXJV3ak30Y=&c=I0z4UFIb16Ox3DLKt0ZvLd72Aa-d-2VvjYgqsooivVqSnWDfQeaU2g==&ch=JgvTfpzBmCNJ9hJhxIlYsgZaTcw1aJQ4HXHpRsd9Pj-VYh85B0l6yw==)
---
| Peter,
Some folks around here still say a Black man can't win a statewide election in Louisiana. I hear it all the time.
We haven't had a black US Senator or statewide elected official since Reconstruction. But I'm a farmer. And I know what grows in this soil.
My family worked this Delta land when they were slaves and then sharecroppers. Today my son and I farm the very same fields together - but now we own it. So don't tell me what's "impossible" in Louisiana.
---
| [](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001O90n5WAAwasUCrnMgNWpNbbU_xNit6RAPuW3_XBFfofcr2nI5H4Zt1UvfjzdhuMUDWRHySnjnFcLCo9fCDwuw7Flyi3Yiz-DJuLnnOlca2XclVxZN150XZUXgY1EAS2xFPq4bBNTXqfUYS3ST_Kh4B18_q1Z5502161PzWTu5nSqqyxlaWRyJ1W6Yi3zeYQCC9KDw2a5OY7y_8Uz2y6nCPitEoXkRwoCtN-zTUfqBR8=&c=I0z4UFIb16Ox3DLKt0ZvLd72Aa-d-2VvjYgqsooivVqSnWDfQeaU2g==&ch=JgvTfpzBmCNJ9hJhxIlYsgZaTcw1aJQ4HXHpRsd9Pj-VYh85B0l6yw==)
---
My son and I on our farm in 2021. The same soil our ancestors worked for free.
This state was built by Black hands. We cleared the land, built the levees, grew the crops, served in uniform, and helped write the laws that shaped this place.
And history proves something most people forget:
We've done this before. Right after the Civil War, Black leaders here in Louisiana were elected statewide. They expanded public education, protected civil rights, and even elected the first Black governor in American history. Not somewhere else. Right here.
So, when people say it can't happen now, what they're really saying is we shouldn't try. I don't accept that. And I know you don't either.
I'm Jamie Davis -- a farmer, a father, and the Democrat running for the U.S. Senate here in Louisiana-- I'm running to prove that working families, rural towns, and everyday Louisianans still matter.
[](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001O90n5WAAwasUCrnMgNWpNbbU_xNit6RAPuW3_XBFfofcr2nI5H4Zt1UvfjzdhuMUjEiFoyYlO73VFs9UzdxY3kASJof72nZkkKCNHfmQW8LTpgtAR2L4eTvmqfFdb1yZWzl-NRCcrIND88iLgmTVUaHLO2cc0z02HDjqnomN3dimPIsvkKxDLk3C8eu7pLurJcBQvJ4Io5UFHCCPS1x2PVx8tjcdg8niGLLPUm8dp0qAca0njzv13CHI_inRghDY&c=I0z4UFIb16Ox3DLKt0ZvLd72Aa-d-2VvjYgqsooivVqSnWDfQeaU2g==&ch=JgvTfpzBmCNJ9hJhxIlYsgZaTcw1aJQ4HXHpRsd9Pj-VYh85B0l6yw==)[But campaigns like ours don't run on corporate checks. clean_body: Don’t tell me what’s “impossible” in Louisiana. My family worked this Delta land when they were slaves. Today my son and I farm the very same fields together - but now we own it. | | | | | == | Peter, Some folks around here still say a Black man can't win a statewide election in Louisiana. I hear it all the time. We haven't had a black US Senator or statewide elected official since Reconstruction. But I'm a farmer. And I know what grows in this soil. My family worked this Delta land when they were slaves and then sharecroppers. Today my son and I farm the very same fields together - but now we own it. So don't tell me what's "impossible" in Louisiana. | == My son and I on our farm in 2021. The same soil our ancestors worked for free. This state was built by Black hands. We cleared the land, built the levees, grew the crops, served in uniform, and helped write the laws that shaped this place. And history proves something most people forget: We've done this before. Right after the Civil War, Black leaders here in Louisiana were elected statewide. They expanded public education, protected civil rights, and even elected the first Black governor in American history. Not somewhere else. Right here. So, when people say it can't happen now, what they're really saying is we shouldn't try. I don't accept that. And I know you don't either. I'm Jamie Davis -- a farmer, a father, and the Democrat running for the U.S. Senate here in Louisiana-- I'm running to prove that working families, rural towns, and everyday Louisianans still matter. == If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | | == | == | == | | | == | == | == | == | Every dollar helps us knock more doors, make more calls, and proves the doubters wrong. name: James O'Keefe
subject: WATCH: The Big Murkowski Ballot Scandal
body:
I gave a name that was not mine at an Alaska polling place. No ID. "Absolutely possible." Now the Senator's office wants me prosecuted.
---

---
| The Big Murkowski Ballot Scandal I gave a name that was not mine at an Alaska polling place. No ID. "Absolutely possible." Now the Senator's office wants me prosecuted. | | [](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5ODB9AAwAAAAAApIpN9v5tv4WL4o6v9QYt9sLYr02XoHdeYq_ZzX_sWUNgzdrrWlk040qZKhPGOU-8neR6K4_xlak6etXZXEnzBfHTaMrFTjQIKD7xhN-BQ)
---
| NEW INVESTIGATION * ALASKA
---
THE BIG
MURKOWSKI
Anchorage. Primary day. No ID required.
This investigation cost **$50,000**. [Help us fund the next one.](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5ODB9AAwAAAAAApIpN9v64jXZAt2KnC82zML9_G9oGi2psW-ZZmMcvipQekL4kuVB0CXqoR8Bxw95LORgLzYkVnk6dMZPt_2PC0N4d5t5m3EdNF9sudDpEw)
Dear Patriot,
Stand at that table with me for a second. Anchorage, Alaska. Primary day. There is a folding table, a laminated binder, and a perfectly nice woman working the poll book the way she probably has for years. I give her a name. It is not my name. The name is **Brian Murkowski**. He is the brother of a sitting United States Senator. He does not live in Alaska. He lives in Texas.
[ ](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5ODB9AAwAAAAAApIpN9v7YGedBXgOF962FqbKoKqexdZoJ4KHxpM3BMtu3JZ1l-7SmIV8ARTcjU9xTvlj4qoJgGIFZ1Ac8-OV4jzTuYeFf5FTd0pZx7CvXA)
Then I tell her the one thing that is supposed to stop all of this cold. I tell her **I do not have my ID.** She looks up at me and says:
| "Absolutely possible."
---
ANCHORAGE POLL WORKER * AUGUST 18, 2026
I want you to watch this one for yourself. And then I want you to help me pay for the next one. **[You can chip in right here.](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5ODB9AAwAAAAAApIpN9v88A4lVV_4o_kqK9ih5kQH5rppUZwvQxOrKKyFRh4B7cXMCG0Cwg-9R2RPBLVooZhoWkB6xHVTV35eO8RSQNJyj5dacAuiDUZKsQ)** I asked her again anyway, because I wanted it recorded and I wanted it to be completely unmistakable to anyone who watched it later. All I have to do is fill out the question ballot, and then I can vote? **" Yes, sir."** We titled the video **" The Big Murkowski,"** and you really do have to laugh a little bit at it, because the only other available option is putting your head through a wall.
The funny part ends fast. **Every single thing I am about to tell you makes the thing before it worse.**
| ONE. A total stranger walked in off the street carrying no identification of any kind and was offered a ballot. TWO. The name on that ballot belongs to a United States Senator's brother who lives roughly three thousand miles away, in another state entirely. THREE. We did it again. Different polling place, same morning. One of my reporters gave the name **Karina Waller** -- Senator Murkowski's own **State Director**. No ID. Same offer. **[Help us keep doing exactly this.](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5ODB9AAwAAAAAApIpN9v95RmijonXDZ6d4lu8WreDWBCwq1anqxznJigL6LUKCrzMhE5_5XAc51kUtL3rr_7RQBkQw_nH154NBhZ_t6etJZ6XlKTVdCSqFg)** FOUR. Alaska law says you show identification to get a ballot, and the one narrow exception written into it is that the poll worker personally knows the person standing in front of them. Nobody in either of those buildings had ever laid eyes on us before in their lives. FIVE. Nobody wrote anything down. Nobody picked up a phone. Nobody flagged a single thing. We asked, we got our answer, and we walked back out the door.
---
Now here is the part that should stop you cold. Senator Murkowski has spent this year fighting the SAVE Act, which her office describes as "an overly burdensome, one-size-fits-all mandate from Washington," and the argument underneath that position has always been the same one we hear everywhere: that the hole we keep describing does not actually exist outside of our imagination. **We just showed her the hole. In her own state. Using her own brother's name.** Before anyone calls this a partisan hit job, let me say it plainly: Senator Murkowski is a Republican, and it does not matter to me even a little, because a hole in the process is a hole in the process and it does not care one bit about which party happens to walk through it. Her office did not say they were going to fix it. Her office said this:
| "Voter impersonation is a crime and should be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law." OFFICE OF SEN. LISA MURKOWSKI
---
Now I want to be precise with you about what we did and did not do, because you fund this operation and you deserve that kind of accounting from me. **I did not vote. I did not sign anyone's name. I never touched a ballot.** I asked a question, I recorded the answer, and I left. That is what reporters do. The response from a sitting United States Senator's office was to start talking about prosecuting me for it. Patriot, this has become a pattern, and I want you to see it as clearly as I have come to see it over the last three weeks. Last week the Secretary of State of Minnesota published a statement accusing my journalists of **" lying, lawbreaking, and disruptions"** and announced that **law enforcement is reviewing** them. He never named a single law we broke. This week the office of a United States Senator is talking about prosecuting a journalist to the fullest extent of the law. Michigan. Minnesota. Alaska. Three states in three weeks, and every single time we have gone looking, we have found the same hole sitting there in plain sight. Nobody ever rushes to close the hole. **They come after the person holding the flashlight.**
[GIVE NOW -- FUND THE NEXT STATE](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5ODB9AAwAAAAAApIpN9v-70GEWPkdagjC-AN1_ifXP6SWChvXsJZVKu7jva5fSixVGZHPDlf0X9YU7guU0t6KI3CySMp0pemFJpFyhE2h22jKKsKyXeLr0w)
Let me tell you what Alaska cost.
| $50,000
---
What this single investigation cost to produce -- so that you could hear two words said out loud at a folding table in Anchorage.
That covered the flights to Anchorage and back, the weeks of preparation before anyone ever got on a plane, the records work, the equipment, and a team standing on the ground at dawn on primary day three thousand miles from our office. It also covered the lawyers who reviewed every frame of that footage before a single second of it went to air, because we understood exactly what was coming the moment it did. I would spend every dollar of it again tomorrow morning without blinking. Here is my problem. **[We do not have another fifty thousand dollars sitting in a drawer waiting for the next state.](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5ODB9AAwAAAAAApIpN9v_P9OGKzDwa_UkB7yTeZJ0ORgUnT5r1Q6qUsyypumCVFV2ghBUDX6Lsm-KFf91QbSp6dUUoHKXUfNndT1HtD_-CbWTP5aq5UVydQ)** And there is a next one. There is always a next one. Alaska is not special. Alaska is simply the state we happened to be standing in on Tuesday, and everything you are about to watch came out of a single morning and one honest question asked out loud at a folding table. **Imagine what is sitting untouched in the other forty-nine.** **In twenty-eight days, the first federal ballots for November go out.** After that date the machine is running, and everything we have not found yet gets voted on anyway. You and your family have to live under whatever comes out of those buildings, and so does mine, and that is the entire reason I keep walking into them with a camera when it would be far easier and considerably safer not to. There is nobody else writing this check, and there never has been. It has always been you.
[YES, JAMES -- I'LL HELP FUND THE NEXT ONE](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5ODB9AAwAAAAAApIpN9wAPeapCWPjBy1pbh5ZaMYaXTOgpbSqYdPpg3YLV2B5x06Ng6dTBsA3EKUJYPWu-tBFCiaGmS-N9YrGq1ULz7UiC6AZznOC9oFzSQ)
Thank you for everything you do. In Truth, James O'Keefe Founder, O'Keefe Media Group
**P.S.** The video is called **" The Big Murkowski,"** and I hope it makes you laugh. Then I hope it makes you furious. A stranger with no ID was offered a United States Senator's brother's ballot, and the Senator's office answered by talking about prosecuting the man who filmed it. **[That is exactly why this cannot stop-- and you are the only reason it does not have to.](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5ODB9AAwAAAAAApIpN9wBOyHWiN7Hu4WtjTeaTV5N2OFNCsUVcrQMpP9Jq5hTl7nZImfBlrcFw7C0hWkB8xR8mUj65IYR_1hr_5xPBEbWqJ1VISA9D9I7rA)**
[RUSH YOUR GIFT NOW](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5ODB9AAwAAAAAApIpN9wCJnJUoTOSdrfCoJLD9buTpfPa0nDqcL-eOHqEQi65N4gmhjTzT3Bjx9votEoM3MbOu7HSd8byre8VR6BnFzu5Qix0z5qDaJwSkA)
| [](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5ODB9AAwAAAAAApIpN9wD8bPkxK4BOmCLW1winb3uL8GA6001kkdcP5Rl9MtsZF-ZvfJoKRwDEdqRPHuRf7wkTeZsNCb0Sav18jJVQN6uwnSqGyt8BGhe2A)

| Peter,
Today, we officially launched our first TV ad of the general election and I wanted you to be among the first to see it.
This ad tells a story that is deeply personal to me.
When my dad was dying from cancer, his treatment cost more than our family could afford. My mom took a second job to help pay for the medicine that could save his life.
I've never forgotten what my family went through, and I know families across Northwest Ohio are facing the same impossible choices because of the rising cost of prescription drugs.
That's why, when I had the opportunity to do something about it, I wrote the law that slashed the cost of life-saving medicine in Ohio.
---

For more than 43 years, Marcy Kaptur has been in Washington while healthcare costs have continued to rise. Northwest Ohio deserves new leadership that understands what working families are going through and will deliver results.
I'm running for Congress to take on Big Pharma, lower prescription drug prices, and fight for families across Northwest Ohio.
Our campaign is building momentum, and this ad marks an important new phase in our race.
Watch the ad, share it with your friends and family, and help us spread the word across Northwest Ohio.

body:
Ten days ago, I laced up my shoes at Rock's Diner in Fort Kent, and started walking south. I told myself I would listen first and talk second.

| | |

Peter, Ten days ago, I laced up my shoes at Rock's Diner in Fort Kent, and started walking south. I told myself I would listen first and talk second. That is exactly what we've been doing. The **For a Better Maine Tour** has brought us from **Fort Kent, Madawaska, Caribou, and Presque Isle** down through **Medway, Millinocket, East Millinocket, Old Town, Orono, and Skowhegan** \- and the response has changed this campaign. [Check out NewsCenter Maine's news coverage from my ](https://www.supportrickbennett.com/r?u=0ZEw3rKCYdU6QDR4jANpCzJgPR1oXz7mjSdU-TTQM5knkPQwhnwTMNs7BsVzdgJm4p_34enJRePYZ0wlFFId4hAeQf-xzfr02ivWd9TJNvj2XTZfledmTiHAtu4EFqBLYniveboMpeDcctldILlC39Yn1Q4KYdWz4AjuNpwnz7Ew_VG0qWtHHpOIg7AvMpQzI9NznGUnEuqThoiTYqVlEHAjPL-1RAD-TwRflwsp0cQkz63QF4NScV98_uGihJbc&e=939e09e235be96b0bea768d960703804&utm_source=bennettforgovernor&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=walking_tour_newscenter_8_26&n=1)time in Skowhegan. What I’m experiencing on the ground is not what you'll see in a poll or a political ad. It's Mainers sitting with me in diner booths and chatting in hardware stores – sharing that they can't afford to live here anymore. It's young people at UMaine wondering whether they can build a life in the state they grew up in. It's small business owners telling me exactly which budget line is going to determine whether they make it to another year. That is what this campaign is about. Not a slogan. **A conversation.** I am running as an **independent** , free of the party bosses in DC and Augusta, and that is landing differently on a porch in [Millinocket than it does in a TV ad](https://www.supportrickbennett.com/r?u=0ZEw3rKCYdU6QDR4jANpCzJgPR1oXz7mjSdU-TTQM5knkPQwhnwTMNs7BsVzdgJm4p_34enJRePYZ0wlFFId4hAeQf-xzfr02ivWd9TJNvj2XTZfledmTiHAtu4EFqBLYniveboMpeDcctldILlC39Yn1Q4KYdWz4AjuNpwnz7Ew_VG0qWtHHpOIg7AvMpQzI9NznGUnEuqThoiTYqVlEHAjPL-1RAD-TwRflwsp0cQkz63QF4NScV98_uGihJbc&e=939e09e235be96b0bea768d960703804&utm_source=bennettforgovernor&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=walking_tour_newscenter_8_26&n=2). People are tired of being told who to vote for. They are ready to be asked what they actually need. But here's the truth: an independent campaign runs on direct support from folks like you -- not DC party bosses or dark money special interest groups. Every mile of road I've walked, every diner stop, every ride from a volunteer is powered by donors like you. The walking tour is working because of you. To keep this momentum going through the fall, we need to fund the next stretch of the road - more nights in small towns, more travel, more listening, more signs on more Mainers' lawns. **Will you chip in today to keep the For a Better Maine tour and our independent campaign moving?**
* [**$50** \- fuels the next stretch of road](https://www.supportrickbennett.com/r?u=YfUDpXGo8gghXoXxri0tM4mMKq-jD0dJQftB77-60X6Rrf9j7Ih0g7tGW2uNtRFE&e=939e09e235be96b0bea768d960703804&utm_source=bennettforgovernor&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=walking_tour_newscenter_8_26&n=3)
* [**$100** \- covers a night in a small town ](https://www.supportrickbennett.com/r?u=YfUDpXGo8gghXoXxri0tM4mMKq-jD0dJQftB77-60X6Rrf9j7Ih0g7tGW2uNtRFE&e=939e09e235be96b0bea768d960703804&utm_source=bennettforgovernor&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=walking_tour_newscenter_8_26&n=4)
* [**$250** \- underwrites a full day of walking, listening, and organizing](https://www.supportrickbennett.com/r?u=YfUDpXGo8gghXoXxri0tM4mMKq-jD0dJQftB77-60X6Rrf9j7Ih0g7tGW2uNtRFE&e=939e09e235be96b0bea768d960703804&utm_source=bennettforgovernor&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=walking_tour_newscenter_8_26&n=5)

name: Jen Kiggans
subject: I apologize for asking again
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Kiggans for Congress
body:
Not what I spent my time doing

|
Peter,
I’ll be honest with you... I’m not great at asking for money. It’s the part of this job I hate the most.
I didn’t spend my twenties learning how to fundraise to run for office. I spent them flying H-46 helicopters for the Navy and deploying to the Persian Gulf.
And when I came home, I didn’t become a lobbyist who took clients out to expensive dinners. I used my GI Bill to become a Geriatric Nurse Practitioner. My "networking" was holding the hands of our seniors and listening to their stories, not cutting backroom deals.
That’s really who I am...a Helicopter Pilot...a Nurse Practitioner... and a Mom trying to raise four happy and healthy kids in a world that feels like it’s going in the wrong direction most days.
[I didn't run for Congress for the title. I ran because I looked at the country my children were inheriting, and I felt sick to my stomach. Dolly Parton, the Grammy-winning singer, songwriter, and actress whose [larger-than-life persona and six-decade](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0D1uhDAQBeDTmM7IDH-mcJGGbtOmRF48ZicyeGXPQrh9xOYI6UYa6T197-s23SwF2pZPu6JhH6cNjxyQGdPkYgjn0yaOmyPMPpy0LWx_aAIFnVRaQjfZmWnHqbGFMx4RsC7QVL3u-1pr3RYPY_W9UrZT3ul73bTe9z22XoOehwEGpQsyV57S0FVKadWU0NbYOu_A-6FybS0ahY44pvI70sYP9OGMO6ZyjmsRzIP5mUX9IWAUMB7HUc73fDmuv4DxOgWMb47888gLJO2CUis5x9fG6ZTrK9MsM9skYCyScc-DQqDc9aJRy2opvAv5nzvtBn4DAAD__wpgfsA) career made her one of America's most beloved entertainers, died peacefully at her Nashville home, her family announced Tuesday. She was 80. The fourth of 12 children raised in rural Tennessee, Parton sold over [100 million records](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0D1uAjEQxfHT2N0ie_y5hYs0dKRNaVnMGCYy69WuBeH2EeQIqZ_0l37v65RPhRsvl89yozRqzws99kZj0Jaxt_Zcyzb6gkx7bU9eLqP8cAYFflJxAp_LefCdsi0SUyUCMpKSDjEEE2N08ppK0DoAKWdnH4NCmE0o1jjUszVwdpLTq6cieK1UVPYAzpDDilDrrNEZYRUhj74dvjsv40q1PfudtsO532RL1zHWXZgPAUcBx5X62ug1CTi-CdOfYUIqOAXnXXRGbgnXB7fGuw_CqsutcHv3xj9vuCf4DQAA__8mxXDr) on the strength of hits like _Jolene_ and _I Will Always Love You_ , starred in the hit movie _9 to 5_ ,__ and built Dollywood into one of the country's most-visited theme parks. Parton was an inspirational figure to many, often focusing on forgiveness and prayer in interviews. ## Canada Hits Back with 50% Tariffs
Canada struck back Tuesday, announcing [retaliatory tariffs](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2unTAQBOCnMR3ILH-mcJGG7qRNiRZ2fXBkbGQ2h_D2V9xXuN1II30jzZ_X_EIffHz_xp2tuDRHvs7AIpxnSiHcB2ZJkTyfLtw-vgX_-xk09KU2JfQzruI_PLdYkHXMwE3Bth7MMDTGmK7Y7LhA1w84LgR1rZ3hgWkkXsZlbJCAC28fTxvoa62NbivoGu7IETg31tQ1qtVMXlKu_iYfZWMX7vThXK1pL4LdRI5TNb8UTAqm67qqNS7rUyqYHlrBpM2TOwXTihEJS8n_9qMUzN65s5SMxOWKOfJdBl4CxrXaZA9FtnRcPgR_9oNq9XtHH7535Yd3fSx8BQAA___1hIAa) as high as 50% on more than 700 American products, matching President Trump's newest levies "dollar for dollar."

## Study: 1 in 4 Deceased NFL Players Had CTE
At least one in four former NFL players who died between 2016 and 2021 had chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), and the true rate could be as high as 97.7%, according to a [study published](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0D2OpDAQxfHTmMzIlDEfgYNNyHrTDZHB5carahvhGhhuP-q-wsQ_6enp_-8xP1ykmJ5_3QsthzwnvAohMx6zz0T37g7OyUcsge6Ynuy-4wwKOqkGCd3sVo4nzq2rvA2IgLpC2_RD3-thGEy1WdfpZVxWrXVwi_HGOwULrkqPYQ3ahSra954aoGuUGlRbg9FofPAQwth4o0Wr0EfOR_0_x8QbBrrziUe95ldFdmPei9B_BEwCpuu6aix7eqOAKQUSMBXOxy1gmgVM0QuY2rGHpjHdx778LcuWryIJXWEJRqZAcid341GkxxMp73JlrA7r9ysSxdL1olXPl4v0ucG_rHda-AkAAP__D1GFiw) in _The British Medical Journal_. The findings land just as football season is about to kick off across America. The study tracked 1,712 former players who died between 2008 and 2021. Of the 338 who [donated their brains](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkMGOpCAURb8Gd1TwIYgLFpNMzGxqtr006HuUr4NikFS1f9-p_oVe3-TmnPNxn-6BE--P_2EjX2OednqdiWqlMmFO6TpCqXlHpjOmi_dHDV88gQIrlZNgp7BUftLUhQZ9JALSDfm2d32vnXOmWb2Kg221no1eYMDZ9joMvV1ii4PDxcwN-_efcmBbpZzqbmA0GYwIMQ4tGi06Rcg1l9tn5r2uFNOVn1RuS96a5Ndaj1PoPwJGAWOYl7fDexMw_qOQ6ipgbGUnYy4bFbnHJI8ULiqnRCaUF4UiDyqcUcB41lwuoUdGof-22gxada5risfjxSnxaXvRqccWOP0A1F92e3r4DgAA__8Ke4IR), 93.2% were diagnosed with CTE, and nearly 60% of those donors had dementia. By comparison, CTE appears in [less than 1%](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DFuhDAQQNHTmM5oGBvwFi7S0G3alMjg8eLIYGRml3D7aHOFXOA_6X_dx7uLKW6PT7eS5ZDHjc4jETOV0eeUrt0VzpuPdIR0xe3B7ieOCNhJMBK70c0cXzRqV3kbiJBURbbpTd8rY0xbLVYDTLd-Cgp0AwBdq5Vxqsfb7GHSXlfRvntgsGsADOgaW0WtDx5DuDW-VUID-ci51N85brxQSFd-UannvFbJLsz7IdSHwEHgcJ5nPT1r8k-Bgysc50SHwOFtCBxWt10y5LJSkVtIck_uonLIxXk5M8mJQi4kPTleqmL9fsaU4tH1QsNjdTH9ofzPVy-LvwEAAP__wHl-yg) of the general population. Most players in the study competed before 2005, when the disease was first identified in an NFL player, so recent safety reforms may not be reflected in the data.

It is already that time.
The midterm elections are not even here yet. We have no idea who will control the House or Senate. But apparently, it is time to start speculating about who will run for president in 2028
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/57cbad56-c47e-4b8a-b29b-21df1a501128?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I want to start with the Republicans.
I am ranking the potential candidates from D tier to S tier, with D being the worst and S sitting above A as the best. I am judging them on four basic questions:
Can they win a Republican primary? Can they defeat the Democratic nominee? Can they build and finance a national campaign? Do they have the charisma and media skills required to run for president?
Those categories are weighted evenly because this is not scientific. It is speculation, and, well... who the hell knows.
But I am going to do it anyway.
* * *
## D Tier
### Josh Hawley
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0d6e20ec-ad33-45ce-b997-d00aac1e5f93?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Josh Hawley has national name recognition. He is a sitting senator, reasonably telegenic and capable of raising money.
But I do not think he has the political power or charisma to break through a serious Republican presidential primary.
Hawley is still the guy who raised his fist toward protesters outside the Capitol on January 6 and was later shown running through the Capitol as the attack unfolded. Fairly or unfairly, that image made him look like a little bitch to a lot of people.
He may believe being an incumbent senator gives him enough clout to run. Incumbents normally win reelection, and senators naturally begin imagining themselves as presidents.
I do not see it.
More likely, Hawley positions himself for a future cabinet appointment or uses a presidential campaign to increase his influence within the party.
That puts him in D tier.
* * *
### Tim Scott
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9f0e4d4f-4494-4a9e-b60f-b9b7471f3555?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Tim Scott has more political connections than people give him credit for. He can raise money, and he knows how to move around a debate stage without completely embarrassing himself.
I simply do not think he projects the political backbone people expect from a presidential candidate. He does not come across as somebody who will take control of the party, define the race and make voters believe he should be president.
He has connections. He has donors. He has experience.
I do not think he has the gumption.
D tier.
* * *
### Vivek Ramaswamy
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c5adffd5-87e3-4302-8b5e-7454087c015c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Vivek Ramaswamy created plenty of attention during the 2024 Republican primary. That campaign helped him get selected to help lead the original Department of Government Efficiency effort with Elon Musk, although he "left" before the project formally began.
He is now the Republican nominee for governor of Ohio.
Vivek has money, national recognition and media skills. But I think the more people get to know him, the less they like him. He was passed over for the U.S. Senate appointment, passed over for vice president and never received a Senate-confirmed cabinet position. No one wants him anywhere.
Now he is running for governor.
If he wins and immediately turns around to run for president, people are going to ask why he wanted the governor's office in the first place. Ohioans would have every right to tell him to stay here and do the damn job.
If he loses the governor's race, that creates a different problem for a presidential campaign.
Either way, I have him in D tier.
* * *
### Pete Hegseth
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9350e2f3-e4cd-4daa-aa01-d477a4390735?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Pete Hegseth is currently the secretary of defense, and his recent political travel to Iowa has already [generated speculation about a possible 2028 campaign](https://substack.com/redirect/d43ce735-3b57-40d1-8e4d-06ebab957be5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
I do not know where Hegseth's political future goes.
I could see him trying to stay in Republican politics, campaigning for other candidates or positioning himself for another administration job. I could even see his name being floated as a running mate.
But as a presidential candidate, I do not see a strong fundraising organization, broad coalition or convincing general-election profile.
People are talking about him, so he belongs on the list.
He also belongs in D tier.
* * *
## C Tier
### Sarah Huckabee Sanders
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5199f713-6d9a-4e5d-9912-05d15ccff112?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Sarah Huckabee Sanders is a loyal Trump ally, the governor of Arkansas and a known national figure because of her time as White House press secretary.
I considered putting her in B tier.
She could raise a respectable amount of money. She has political connections, and I think some moderate Republicans could convince themselves that she offers a calmer version of Trump's politics.
She has also clearly been working on her presentation and political profile as governor.
But I still do not think she generates enough excitement or has enough charisma to take control of a national primary.
My reaction is basically: meh.
That puts her in C tier.
* * *
### Greg Abbott
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5e856c8b-2c31-4749-87af-1807d77c7a9f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Greg Abbott is a powerful Republican governor with national name recognition and deep connections inside the party.
But I do not think he has the charisma to win a presidential campaign.
American presidential politics is also obviously ableist. Voters and the media tend to favor candidates who are taller, conventionally attractive and physically commanding on television. Abbott's use of a wheelchair should not affect his qualifications, but I think the political system would unfairly make it part of the campaign.
Even beyond that, I do not think he has the presence to take over a crowded Republican field.
C tier.
* * *
### Tulsi Gabbard
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4817c317-b471-4e20-b89a-f891e2854fc9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Tulsi Gabbard is an odd political figure.
She was a Democratic member of Congress and a Democratic presidential candidate. She became a Republican, joined Trump's administration as director of national intelligence and resigned in 2026, publicly citing her husband's serious health problems.
I still wonder whether leaving the administration also preserves her ability to begin preparing for 2028.
Tulsi has charisma. She has a strong media presence. She can raise money, and she would probably perform well on a debate stage.
**Her problem is trust.**
Many Republicans still do not trust her because she spent years as a prominent Democrat. Democrats do not trust her because she joined Trump and became a Republican.
That leaves her in a strange political limbo.
I could imagine her fitting into some kind of Tucker Carlson or Marjorie Taylor Greene political movement. I could even imagine a third-party campaign designed to disrupt the general election.
As the Republican nominee, though, I do not see it.
C tier.
* * *
### Byron Donalds
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f249f839-a6d9-4244-9ec2-c8d7d852df0e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Byron Donalds just won the Republican nomination for governor of Florida. He will face former Republican congressman and now Democrat David Jolly in the November general election.
Donalds is generally liked within the Republican Party. Like Gabbard and Ramaswamy, he was previously a Democrat, but he does not carry the same political baggage from that transition.
He can raise money. He is comfortable on television, and I think he would perform well on a presidential debate stage.
His problem is timing.
If Donalds wins the governorship and immediately begins campaigning for president, Florida voters may reasonably ask why he ran for governor. If you win the job, do the job.
Would he really leave the Florida governor's office for a cabinet appointment? I would not.
He has potential, but 2028 may be too soon.
C tier.
* * *
## B Tier...

Let's say it plainly: the U.S. Supreme Court is nothing more than an extension of the Trump regime.
The proof is beyond obvious now. The Court's conservative supermajority, six of nine sitting Justices, has gone all in on Donald Trump's twisted authoritarian vision for America.
The Court has repeatedly sent a clear message, stretching from Bush v. Gore in the year 2000 all the way to today: The (Republican) President of the United States can now run elections throughout the 50 states.
We are rapidly on a glidepath to becoming a Western imitation of Putin's Russia. A place where elections only serve the party in power. Where democracy is an illusion. And where loyalty to party and to one person overrules the rule of law.

name: Chris Pappas
subject: A literal gold mine in Azerbaijan...
body:
[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1001&akid=8522%2E582294%2Eu3zsJB ]Chris Pappas for Senate[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1002&akid=8522%2E582294%2Eu3zsJB ]Chris Pappas for Senate

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260826_1.lV-dHU&refcode=em20260826-8522&amount=5&t=1003&akid=8522%2E582294%2Eu3zsJB ][IMG]
Josh Rogers/NHPR

At the GOP debate, John Sununu told a roomful of Republicans he's running
for Senate to send me back to "bussing tables” at my family’s “chicken
restaurant."

He meant it as an insult. As if the people who work in restaurants — who
cook your food, clear your plates, keep family businesses that are the
heart of our state alive — have something to be embarrassed about.

I’m not embarrassed. I’m proud.

My family opened our restaurant over 100 years ago. I know what a 65-hour
week feels like because I've worked one. I know what it means to show up
every day, work hard, and treat the people around you like they matter —
because they do.

John Sununu has never had to work hard a day in his life. He was born into
the Sununu political dynasty. His family's "business" isn't a restaurant
serving New Hampshire families. It owns a literal gold mine in Azerbaijan
that sells minerals to China.

That's what John Sununu calls “honest work.”

New Hampshire workers deserve a senator who knows what a hard day's labor
actually looks like — who fights for small business owners, for restaurant
workers, for every family just trying to make ends meet. John Sununu is
running to protect people like himself. I'm running for everyone else.

He showed us who he is with these elitist comments. Now let’s make sure he
doesn’t represent us.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260826_1.lV-dHU&amount=5&refcode=em20260826-1&t=1022&akid=8522%2E582294%2Eu3zsJB ]Donate $5 »

John Sununu doesn’t know the real New Hampshire. He doesn’t get how hard
we work — and he sure as hell doesn’t think our labor is worth respecting.

I do. That’s why I’m running for Senate.

— Chris Pappas

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260826_1.lV-dHU&refcode=em20260826-8522&amount=5&t=1023&akid=8522%2E582294%2Eu3zsJB ][IMG]

body:
Trump will always put himself first. Always.

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=3000%2E4032634%2E2xVwp1)
---
New reporting by The Wall Street Journal shows that Trump is the most corrupt president in history and that there are no limits to how far he is willing to go to use the presidency for his own enrichment. | [](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3756?t=8&akid=3000%2E4032634%2E2xVwp1)
---
Here's what they found:
Almost every night in the White House, Trump calls his fundraiser, Meredith O'Rourke, for an update. He asks which companies and donors have cut checks and which haven't — and for how much.
He's keeping score.
Then the Journal discovered something even more troubling. When a company has an issue with the federal government that reaches Trump's attention, he wants to know how much money that company has given him. If they haven't hit his fundraising goals, he rubs it in.
Trump's fundraiser told companies:
> _"This is very important to the president. He's asked me to call you and ask you for this donation."_
In some calls, she refers to Trump as "the boss," saying:
> _"The boss wants this money."_
The president of the United States is acting like a mob boss — keeping tabs on which corporations are giving him millions while those same companies may have business before the federal government.
And we're not talking about pocket change either. Trump has demanded that corporations hand over $25 million, even $50 million, to his personal and political projects.
That's not public service. It's a shakedown. And it's at the heart of Trump's corruption: He sees the presidency as a tool only for personal enrichment.
When it comes to his own money? Trump is like a dog with a bone. Using every tool at his disposal to line his pockets.
But when it comes to making life more affordable for you and other working Americans? Trump doesn't care. He thinks it's a big yawn that some Americans are being forced to sell their blood just to afford groceries.
And with his rubber-stamp Congress, there's far too little standing in his way of keeping on in that manner. Which is why we have to, have to, have to take back control of Congress in the midterms, so that we can stop his self-dealing and put policies in place that will actually help people.
Right now, Trump's allies are outspending us in many of the races that matter most. Every dollar we raise between now and November will help us reach the voters who need to hear the truth: Trump doesn’t care about you and your family. He will always put himself first.
[**If you're able, will you pitch in $28 — or any amount — to power our campaign to expose the lies, take back Congress, and get our government to ACTUALLY work for working people and not for the president's personal interests?**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3756?amount=28&t=9&akid=3000%2E4032634%2E2xVwp1)

I hope you're having a good day. I'm writing with some exciting news.
[](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckcGqnDAUhp8m7pTcE41x4aJFLS29U3qncJchJkfnlGiCidM-fhmY-wJdHTgffD_8__urfjXkaV8vZsOeUtIuOI1_ow8H5htu5nc4HhdTWFbUwEGWXJUgtbGZ7qhrU7i-gRe1qAL7l1a1bd2oWhS3fja8VY4DrwFn2XXAlbUdKmFAynlZCuofPq5AvgAXjaqsE52RrpnBzY0wgtX8jM5krGhP5DDZEGIMnjLZVIVjLXx_yzkmJj4xmBhMtC-hupH3yRmPFbqTwVSuuGOiVC4HYunurgzLggcTU7JMDJx3tbxwqOH7t8_Dj2EcrwzkmTedwnlYZGKIR0gRbaZ9faINHZ0bEwNuhvzzac0WDa07E8MzUru7-4Bhz7hnJoYv42W8fr1Ob-Oof7bl-6-38qOI4uhd_EPeU5Itq_n6sFc2bEX-33nuPfwLAAD__zRsoHQ)
Hillsdale College's popular online course, **" The Genesis Story: Reading Biblical Narratives,"** is now FREE on DVD.

In this six-lecture course, you'll explore some of the major themes of Genesis, including the complex relationship between God and man, and what it reveals about divine and human nature.

"The Genesis Story" is taught by Hillsdale College professor of English Justin Jackson, who has taught the subject to undergraduate students here at the College for 15 years. This course aims to deepen a student's theological understanding of the Old Testament by revealing the literary beauty and complexity of the text.

The course begins with a lecture and introduction by the president of Hillsdale College, Larry P. Arnn, in which he explains why we teach the Book of Genesis at Hillsdale College and why it's important to both faith and higher education.

Then, Dr. Jackson explains the four relationships that dominate the Book of Genesis: God and creation, God and man, man and man, and man and creation.

You'll explore these relationships in the narratives of Adam and Eve, Abraham and Sarah, Abraham and Isaac, Jacob and Esau, and finally, Joseph.

This course on DVD is perfect for viewing in your home with your family or for use in small groups such as Bible studies and book clubs.

**To receive your FREE Genesis DVD box set, please use the secure link here:**[https://info.hillsdale.edu/-genesis-free-dvd-offer](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckcGqnDAUhp8m7pTcE41x4aJFLS29U3qncJchJkfnlGiCidM-fhmY-wJdHTgffD_8__urfjXkaV8vZsOeUtIuOI1_ow8H5htu5nc4HhdTWFbUwEGWXJUgtbGZ7qhrU7i-gRe1qAL7l1a1bd2oWhS3fja8VY4DrwFn2XXAlbUdKmFAynlZCuofPq5AvgAXjaqsE52RrpnBzY0wgtX8jM5krGhP5DDZEGIMnjLZVIVjLXx_yzkmJj4xmBhMtC-hupH3yRmPFbqTwVSuuGOiVC4HYunurgzLggcTU7JMDJx3tbxwqOH7t8_Dj2EcrwzkmTedwnlYZGKIR0gRbaZ9faINHZ0bEwNuhvzzac0WDa07E8MzUru7-4Bhz7hnJoYv42W8fr1Ob-Oof7bl-6-38qOI4uhd_EPeU5Itq_n6sFc2bEX-33nuPfwLAAD__zRsoHQ)

Warm regards,

Bill Gray, '01

name: The Democrats
subject: Fighting for our future
body:
---
Hi Derek, today is Women’s Equality Day. We wanted to reach out this morning with some reflections about what that means to us. **On this date, 106 years ago, the Nineteenth Amendment was enshrined in our Constitution, codifying women’s right to vote — but only _some_ women. For millions of Black women and women of color, that right wouldn’t be won for several more decades.** This recognition of a fundamental right was not simply handed down by a benevolent government — it was _won_ by a group of trailblazing activists who envisioned a better future for American women and spent decades persevering through only partial progress to make it a reality. The ratification of the Nineteenth Amendment, and decades later, the passage of the Voting Rights Act, was the result of _years_ of organizing, protesting, and civil disobedience in the name of a noble cause. In the decades since, generations of activists have continued fighting for the rights of their daughters, granddaughters, sisters, and nieces. **Derek, women all over the country are _still_ being discriminated against and marginalized by their government — _especially_ with Donald Trump in the White House and his MAGA cronies in control of Congress.** Trump and the GOP work every day to turn back the clock on women’s rights — whether that’s by functionally gutting the Voting Rights Act, slashing funds for reproductive health research, or working to put anti-choice extremists into power who would love nothing more than to enact a national abortion ban. **It goes without saying that there’s a _lot_ at stake this year — _especially for women, their families, and their communities._** Democrats across the country are fighting _hard_ to make up for lost ground. And this year, we have the chance to flip both the House and the Senate and place a massive check on Trump’s power to continue enacting his destructive agenda. Derek, it’s up to us to fight right now. **Progress isn’t promised, it’s hard-fought and hard-won.** That’s exactly what the DNC is doing — fighting for communities across the country to have a government that envisions a brighter future for their communities. [**If electing Democrats who will continue to fight for women’s equality, bodily autonomy, reproductive rights, and more is important to you, we’re asking you to please chip in whatever you can afford to the DNC today. There’s so much at stake, and it’s up to us to fight for the future we want to see.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-august-2026-gfr?refcode=em_20260826_8784_fr&refcode2=8784_22930333_H5AvRv&akid=8784%2E22930333%2EH5AvRv) **[CONTRIBUTE](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-august-2026-gfr?refcode=em_20260826_8784_fr&refcode2=8784_22930333_H5AvRv&akid=8784%2E22930333%2EH5AvRv)** Thank you for fighting with us, The Democrats

_If you gave recently via check or mail, our system may not have yet processed your gift. We are appreciative and thank you greatly for your support._

Hey friends,
I'm thrilled to share this episode with you. My guest this week is the one and only, Corbin Trent!

[**Click Here to LISTEN NOW**](https://us.list-manage.com/6r2HTe9T7tq?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)
**Corbin has one of the wildest résumés in progressive politics.** His political awakening came listening to Bernie Sanders talk about the opioid epidemic and factory closures on the radio one day from his food truck, issues he'd seen firsthand growing up in East Tennessee. He went on to work twice on Bernie's presidential campaigns, in 2016 and 2020, and along the way co-founded Brand New Congress and [Justice Democrats](https://us.list-manage.com/9IlRFc7S1Co?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0), the groups that recruit and run working-class candidates for Congress. That work helped spot and elect AOC before anyone thought a bartender from the Bronx could beat a ten-term incumbent, and Corbin went on to become her first communications director on Capitol Hill.We get into the state of the Democratic Party, why the "socialist" label has become almost meaningless in political debate, healthcare and housing as supply problems, and his current project, a fully transparent super PAC called [A Fight Worth Having](https://us.list-manage.com/uezGjReW2Hy?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0), built to support progressive candidates across the country.This one's a real look at how movements get built from the ground up, starting right here in East Tennessee.Follow Corbin on [Substack](https://us.list-manage.com/8JxV2E7xdqR?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)! Check out his amazing work: [corbintrent.com](https://us.list-manage.com/k1XYzV7fpFK?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0) | [americasundoing.com](https://us.list-manage.com/qNunO9QQHrb?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0) | [afightworthhaving.com](https://us.list-manage.com/4g1lFsUD4Sv?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)

#### [**Listen or watch**](https://us.list-manage.com/nBYNInvUk70?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)**now wherever you get your podcasts. 🎧**

Thank you for being here,
Gloria

[ stdin# ]Our Revolution Logo

Peter Willis,

President Trump has raked in at least $2.2 BILLION since returning to the
White House — and over $1.4 billion of it is from his family’s
cryptocurrency empire.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39578?source=email-20260826&t=1011&akid=11233%2E5885482%2EaNnd66 ]Headline: Trump Pulled In at Least $2 Billion After Returning to the
White House

While millions of families struggle, Trump has used his political power
alongside unregulated crypto to amass a jaw-dropping fortune. And now,
Congress could hand him the keys to an even bigger pile of dirty money by
passing the CLARITY Act, a dangerous new regulatory framework for digital
currencies...written by crypto lobbyists themselves.

After months of deadlock, crypto leaders went to the White House last week
to meet PERSONALLY with Trump — and now *suddenly* a vote is scheduled for
the Senate in September. The bill already passed the House, so together we
MUST stop it in the Senate — and it will take all of us to do it.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39578?source=email-20260826&t=1012&akid=11233%2E5885482%2EaNnd66 ]Together, let’s make it clear: we won’t let Trump and his crypto
cronies get away with this. Will you urgently tell the Senate to vote NO
on the CLARITY Act?

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39578?source=email-20260826&t=1013&akid=11233%2E5885482%2EaNnd66 ]ADD YOUR NAME

The CLARITY Act isn’t about protecting consumers or fixing regulation
gaps. It would supercharge Trump’s crypto cash machine while putting our
entire financial system at risk.

It’s a bill written by crypto lobbyists to keep their profits flowing. And
those very same lobbyists are now funneling record-breaking campaign cash
to lawmakers to buy influence. New reports show they’ve spent $189 million
on the midterms SO FAR, and this is just the beginning.

Their investment is paying off. Senate leaders — including even some
Democrats — already helped the CLARITY Act sail through committee. Then,
crypto executives met with Trump personally, and now the Senate is racing
to get it across the finish line.

and let them know we won’t forget who sided with Trump’s crypto swindle
over the needs of everyday Americans.

body:
We’re up against more efforts to make voting as burdensome as possible |
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137929503/642442858/-901897163?refcode=emm_ff_20260826_DirectMailNOR_v1s2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDMvMS84ODQ1MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkZDVhYTRjMS00ZWExLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=-KCGrR3NOiNSjWbUcjDqTyAJiM7lgL1zJfmHYlP4hdY=&emci=37c2df17-44a1-f111-9b33-0022482a9f1d&emdi=dd5aa4c1-4ea1-f111-9b33-0022482a9f1d&ceid=1037277)

| | | “The current assault on participatory democracy is **consistent with a long U.S. history of political machinations intended to ensure power for White men** and keep it at a distance for everyone else, most especially Black Americans.” —CNN Politics
---
**Throughout the years, there has been one throughline in our work at Fair Fight — voter access.**
Creating a world in which each and every eligible American has the freedom to register to vote, cast their ballot, and have that ballot counted fairly — and that they had the information, safety, and comfort that they needed to show up to vote.
That is the driving force behind everything we do.
**Over the last few months, there have been more and more efforts to make voting as burdensome as possible across the South.** Republicans have been fighting tooth and nail to suppress the Black vote. They use racially-neutral language to be brutally racially targeted. You know what that’s called? RACISM.
[**Will you fight back for the freedom to vote with a donation of any amount today?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137929505/642442862/-2096927507?refcode=emm_ff_20260826_DirectMailNOR_v1s2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDMvMS84ODQ1MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkZDVhYTRjMS00ZWExLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=-KCGrR3NOiNSjWbUcjDqTyAJiM7lgL1zJfmHYlP4hdY=)
As the _Los Angeles Times_ put it, **“today's disenfranchisement efforts show less raw violence than in the Klan era, but more sophisticated means of voter suppression.”** The level of sophistication in their playbook is terrifying. In states across the country and in elections both big and small, they have worked quietly to:
* Limit polling locations
* Purge registered voters
* Make voter registration harder
* Require photo IDs and documents that prove citizenship
* Eliminate early voting, vote-by-mail, and ballot drop boxes

**If Republicans do not believe that they can win free and fair elections, they appear ready to try to silence the will of the people.**
This is all part of a broader power grab to ensure the 2026 midterm elections are not free or fair. This is how you hollow out a democracy.
**But Fair Fight is on the frontlines to protect and fight for disenfranchised voters. **
This year, we’re laser-focused on turning out Black voters across the South. That means winning in Mississippi, where we’re funding voter protection work, and carefully monitoring for election interference efforts and anti-voter schemes so we can be prepared to fight back nationally and regionally with partners.
And as we’ve proven again and again in the last few years, we’re going to win in Georgia. We’re going to re-elect Senator Jon Ossoff, win the Governor’s race, and flip the Georgia State House.
With all this work, today and across the years, the connective tissue has always been voter access, particularly for Black voters. We must continue fighting back against Republicans’ racist tactics.
[**But this work takes real resources, and we count on this grassroots team to take action when it matters most. clean_body: We’re up against more efforts to make voting as burdensome as possible | | | | “The current assault on participatory democracy is consistent with a long U.S. history of political machinations intended to ensure power for White men and keep it at a distance for everyone else, most especially Black Americans.” —CNN Politics Throughout the years, there has been one throughline in our work at Fair Fight — voter access. Creating a world in which each and every eligible American has the freedom to register to vote, cast their ballot, and have that ballot counted fairly — and that they had the information, safety, and comfort that they needed to show up to vote. That is the driving force behind everything we do. Over the last few months, there have been more and more efforts to make voting as burdensome as possible across the South. Republicans have been fighting tooth and nail to suppress the Black vote. They use racially-neutral language to be brutally racially targeted. You know what that’s called? RACISM. = As the Los Angeles Times put it, “today's disenfranchisement efforts show less raw violence than in the Klan era, but more sophisticated means of voter suppression.” The level of sophistication in their playbook is terrifying. In states across the country and in elections both big and small, they have worked quietly to: Limit polling locations Purge registered voters Make voter registration harder Require photo IDs and documents that prove citizenship Eliminate early voting, vote-by-mail, and ballot drop boxes If Republicans do not believe that they can win free and fair elections, they appear ready to try to silence the will of the people. This is all part of a broader power grab to ensure the 2026 midterm elections are not free or fair. This is how you hollow out a democracy. But Fair Fight is on the frontlines to protect and fight for disenfranchised voters. ** This year, we’re laser-focused on turning out Black voters across the South. That means winning in Mississippi, where we’re funding voter protection work, and carefully monitoring for election interference efforts and anti-voter schemes so we can be prepared to fight back nationally and regionally with partners. And as we’ve proven again and again in the last few years, we’re going to win in Georgia. We’re going to re-elect Senator Jon Ossoff, win the Governor’s race, and flip the Georgia State House. With all this work, today and across the years, the connective tissue has always been voter access, particularly for Black voters. subject: Arabella and Jeannette
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY CHRISTINA BOHANNAN FOR CONGRESS
body:
| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137930359/642445822/-975735282?refcode=em_logoheader&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MjIyOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwMjVhZDAxMC00ZWExLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=z8Sz4foH66UdnfUQ-fC4RJhoMqz5frb_scJhjg8_JjA=)

Peter,

There's a piece of Iowa history I think about a lot. In 1869, Arabella Mansfield became the first woman in the United States admitted to the bar, right here in Iowa. I love thinking about what it took for her to walk into that courtroom and say, in effect, _“Yes, I belong here.”_ But it took another 51 years before women in every state could practice law.

In 1916, Jeannette Rankin of Montana became the first woman elected to Congress, three years before women won the right to vote nationwide. Today, we celebrate the anniversary of the ratification of the 19th Amendment, and we mark it with Women's Equality Day.

**When you look at women's history in this country, you find contradictions everywhere.** We were trusted to run households but told we weren't fit to participate fully in public life. In some states, women could practice law, but in others, they couldn't even serve on juries. At one point, a woman could run for office even though the women in her own community couldn't vote for her.

The women who came before us spent generations fighting to establish their rightful place in society, and we owe it to them to keep the work going.

In 2026, politicians and judges are _still_ limiting women's freedoms. Since Iowa's six-week abortion ban took effect, women here have been forced to travel out of state, often at enormous personal cost, to get care that women in other states can access by simply making an appointment with their doctor and talking through their options.

I keep coming back to one simple question: **Can you name a single law telling men what they can do with their bodies in the same way these laws dictate what women can do with theirs? The answer is no.**
