clean_body: | = Peter, There's a piece of Iowa history I think about a lot. In 1869, Arabella Mansfield became the first woman in the United States admitted to the bar, right here in Iowa. I love thinking about what it took for her to walk into that courtroom and say, in effect, “Yes, I belong here.” But it took another 51 years before women in every state could practice law. In 1916, Jeannette Rankin of Montana became the first woman elected to Congress, three years before women won the right to vote nationwide. Today, we celebrate the anniversary of the ratification of the 19th Amendment, and we mark it with Women's Equality Day. When you look at women's history in this country, you find contradictions everywhere. We were trusted to run households but told we weren't fit to participate fully in public life. In some states, women could practice law, but in others, they couldn't even serve on juries. At one point, a woman could run for office even though the women in her own community couldn't vote for her. The women who came before us spent generations fighting to establish their rightful place in society, and we owe it to them to keep the work going. In 2026, politicians and judges are still limiting women's freedoms. Since Iowa's six-week abortion ban took effect, women here have been forced to travel out of state, often at enormous personal cost, to get care that women in other states can access by simply making an appointment with their doctor and talking through their options. I keep coming back to one simple question: Can you name a single law telling men what they can do with their bodies in the same way these laws dictate what women can do with theirs? The answer is no. Rob Bonta tried to bury the truth — The fight for election integrity continues

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/18JvRO1jtLa?e=1facf02470&c2id=205919520b3860dafbe9b9f5dda2019d)

Friend,
I have one simple question:
**Why is Bonta preventing me from exposing possible election fraud?**
Evidence of possible voter fraud in the Prop 50 election landed on my desk.
I did my job — got a legal warrant signed by a judge so we could simply count the ballots.
That’s it. Count them.Then AG Rob Bonta ordered me to stop. **I refused**.
---
| | | | | [Must Watch](https://us.list-manage.com/QDYSUGnyi6v?e=1facf02470&c2id=205919520b3860dafbe9b9f5dda2019d)
---
| |
No Attorney General in 250 years has the power to shut down a lawful investigation just because he says so.
He lost in Superior Court.He lost in the Appellate Court.
Now he’s at the highest court **demanding something never argued before** : the power to kill any investigation he wants — into his friends, donors, or allies.
**His lawyers still can’t explain the 45,000-vote discrepancy.** They just say “it doesn’t exist” and claim _the Sheriff found no evidence of fraud._
Of course we didn’t. Bonta stopped the investigation before we could finish.
So I’ll ask you:
**Why not just let us count the ballots?****What is Rob Bonta so afraid of?**
This is pure lawfare against me for looking under a rock I clearly wasn’t supposed to look under.
I’ll keep fighting.**Will you stand with me?**
— Sheriff Chad Bianco

body:
Now they’re rolling out this tool to the rest of the country, not because it worked well, but because it didn’t.
| | | | | [](https://wkfbo8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001DCIpnv8PRPQeCzJE5j_a9-1k9Jpz1RSXnjjUBh94YYyXHtltllPLXbDpKvcxzehitu7RsZodlus6lnnVgw_rEdNNIjYJ7zS9oU2OSqMbAkmvQQp_D7lhtRHrb9lDDRarAVInKgji1LXYwZdEwcirJFTcHV5vDSHU875vhz2UYRj44egqHRTgWpvXm68e2mKwTOjSlfiCsqxEtC0EtmuMnQ==&c=ATsJcKRptd5_Iwx-zpSvuPGX-MyNtlRVqy5-RVEZDZgqV2qEO3FWkw==&ch=Z9ocjHF5922w3NUR8pBW9QxkJkcQaT3um_bFBts6hQImDSgjrurFug==)
---
| Peter,
The Supreme Court just cleared the way for Trump to control who gets a mail-in ballot this November.
Monday's ruling means USPS can now resume demanding voter roll data directly from states. At the same time, DHS can keep running those rolls through the "SAVE" citizenship database. The Trump admin's plan is to cross-reference state voter data against SAVE's citizenship flags, and use any match to justify denying mail-in ballot delivery to that voter altogether.
Here in Louisiana, we do not have to guess what happens when this rolls out nationwide. That's because we were the guinea pigs for Trump's election rigging database:
---
| [](https://wkfbo8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001DCIpnv8PRPQeCzJE5j_a9-1k9Jpz1RSXnjjUBh94YYyXHtltllPLXbDpKvcxzehitu7RsZodlus6lnnVgw_rEdNNIjYJ7zS9oU2OSqMbAkmvQQp_D7lhtRHrb9lDDRarAVInKgji1LXYwZdEwcirJFTcHV5vDSHU875vhz2UYRj44egqHRTgWpvXm68e2mKwTOjSlfiCsqyzV2LqKXJcYA==&c=ATsJcKRptd5_Iwx-zpSvuPGX-MyNtlRVqy5-RVEZDZgqV2qEO3FWkw==&ch=Z9ocjHF5922w3NUR8pBW9QxkJkcQaT3um_bFBts6hQImDSgjrurFug==)
---
With the enthusiastic cooperation of our MAGA-occupied state government, Louisiana was one of the first states the Trump admin used to test DHS's "SAVE" database.
After they plugged our voting rolls into the database, out of nearly 3 million registered Louisiana voters, officials only turned up just a few hundred flagged names--almost all decades old. Our own Secretary of State admitted the true number is likely smaller still because the underlying data is riddled with errors:
---
| | [](https://wkfbo8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001DCIpnv8PRPQeCzJE5j_a9-1k9Jpz1RSXnjjUBh94YYyXHtltllPLXbDpKvcxzehitu7RsZodlus6lnnVgw_rEdNNIjYJ7zS9oU2OSqMbAkmvQQp_D7lhtRHrb9lDDRarAVInKgji1LXYwZdEwcirJFTcHV5vDSHU875vhz2UYRj44egqHRTgWpvXm68e2mKwTOjSlfiCsqw3KLCL904B8g==&c=ATsJcKRptd5_Iwx-zpSvuPGX-MyNtlRVqy5-RVEZDZgqV2qEO3FWkw==&ch=Z9ocjHF5922w3NUR8pBW9QxkJkcQaT3um_bFBts6hQImDSgjrurFug==)
---
Now they're rolling out this tool to the rest of the country, not not because it worked well, but because it didn't.
This tool was never about accuracy. It's meant to give state officials cover to purge eligible voters off the rolls, disproportionately Democrats, and hand the Trump admin an excuse to challenge results the moment MAGA loses an election.
In the words of Kamala Harris at the Louisiana Democrats annual state dinner just weeks ago: "Louisiana is ground zero." MAGA treats our state as the laboratory for their most insidious ideas, most recently canceling an ongoing election under a "state of emergency" and eliminating one of our majority-Black Democratic districts. This is exactly why what happens in Louisiana matters to Democrats everywhere. And why we need your help taking our state back. Every voter we register, every voter we protect, every voter we get out to the polls matters more when we're the testing ground for Trump's election rigging schemes.
[The Louisiana Democrats are one of the least funded Democratic Parties in the nation and we need your support to carry on this fight. Can we count on you to rush a donation of $25, $10, or even just $5, to fuel the Louisiana Dem's last ditch effort to save Democratic power in our state? ](https://wkfbo8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001DCIpnv8PRPQeCzJE5j_a9-1k9Jpz1RSXnjjUBh94YYyXHtltllPLXbDpKvcxzehinh5K9aUnhOYXf8wxj3CAOEUzLNN1BOHW2DEwS4Y0u6shuQeCS6qP_v88WjwQ6Vx68l9t0R88yq-krn0OMq4EddPiKXfOus6vfMX31MGPWkPDmOjVmpKGrRt9W1F02s6FIaBykK118ltKNL3vImYtYSf4EW5-a3nQ&c=ATsJcKRptd5_Iwx-zpSvuPGX-MyNtlRVqy5-RVEZDZgqV2qEO3FWkw==&ch=Z9ocjHF5922w3NUR8pBW9QxkJkcQaT3um_bFBts6hQImDSgjrurFug==)

body:
I gave a name that was not mine at an Alaska polling place. No ID. "Absolutely possible." Now the Senator's office wants me prosecuted.

| [](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckb2OpTAMhZ8mdKD8QMIUKVa6ut1suyUyiQHrEhLlZ-b1V8xqqu2ms4-PP9k6f96Xd6CTrv03BLRUypLLUg8qB5QVXQwICWrFfC2SS93zuZd6AVfpA5cROm8nKeZt7tAKMxszjWKcusNuasXNjXzWmzEzciPehPBcruhAKM87sjePz1KL8a4GA3p6c8o5p9Z14pKNvCUPFQe6CnksLsaU4kmVXBli3rvTHrWmwtQvJp9MPgu6lnGAC32sg4uByWd8IW4Y0BPsObZ0S2HvV9r70PIrfpYX9WHtU0zA1LPVsJTYskOmHv8ZmdS34aa1wNTja-mf5iAkoP1i6vH91_ckXhWvytSDSmFSQ4jtq1VTl61Pn3SeVLRhI98D0Hkf3tUfRPFh5d8AAAD__6uDmqI)

---
THE BIG
MURKOWSKI
Anchorage. Primary day. No ID required.
This investigation cost **$50,000**. [Help us fund the next one.](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckb2OpTAMhZ8mdKD8QMIUKVa6ut1suyUyiQHrEhLlZ-b1V8xqqu2ms4-PP9k6f96Xd6CTrv03BLRUypLLUg8qB5QVXQwICWrFfC2SS93zuZd6AVfpA5cROm8nKeZt7tAKMxszjWKcusNuasXNjXzWmzEzciPehPBcruhAKM87sjePz1KL8a4GA3p6c8o5p9Z14pKNvCUPFQe6CnksLsaU4kmVXBli3rvTHrWmwtQvJp9MPgu6lnGAC32sg4uByWd8IW4Y0BPsObZ0S2HvV9r70PIrfpYX9WHtU0zA1LPVsJTYskOmHv8ZmdS34aa1wNTja-mf5iAkoP1i6vH91_ckXhWvytSDSmFSQ4jtq1VTl61Pn3SeVLRhI98D0Hkf3tUfRPFh5d8AAAD__6uDmqI)
Dear Patriot,
Stand at that table with me for a second. Anchorage, Alaska. Primary day. There is a folding table, a laminated binder, and a perfectly nice woman working the poll book the way she probably has for years. I give her a name. It is not my name. The name is **Brian Murkowski**. He is the brother of a sitting United States Senator. He does not live in Alaska. He lives in Texas.
[ ](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckb2OpTAMhZ8mdKD8QMIUKVa6ut1suyUyiQHrEhLlZ-b1V8xqqu2ms4-PP9k6f96Xd6CTrv03BLRUypLLUg8qB5QVXQwICWrFfC2SS93zuZd6AVfpA5cROm8nKeZt7tAKMxszjWKcusNuasXNjXzWmzEzciPehPBcruhAKM87sjePz1KL8a4GA3p6c8o5p9Z14pKNvCUPFQe6CnksLsaU4kmVXBli3rvTHrWmwtQvJp9MPgu6lnGAC32sg4uByWd8IW4Y0BPsObZ0S2HvV9r70PIrfpYX9WHtU0zA1LPVsJTYskOmHv8ZmdS34aa1wNTja-mf5iAkoP1i6vH91_ckXhWvytSDSmFSQ4jtq1VTl61Pn3SeVLRhI98D0Hkf3tUfRPFh5d8AAAD__6uDmqI)
Then I tell her the one thing that is supposed to stop all of this cold. I tell her **I do not have my ID.** She looks up at me and says:
| "Absolutely possible."
---
ANCHORAGE POLL WORKER * AUGUST 18, 2026
I want you to watch this one for yourself. And then I want you to help me pay for the next one. **[You can chip in right here.](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckb2OpTAMhZ8mdKD8QMIUKVa6ut1suyUyiQHrEhLlZ-b1V8xqqu2ms4-PP9k6f96Xd6CTrv03BLRUypLLUg8qB5QVXQwICWrFfC2SS93zuZd6AVfpA5cROm8nKeZt7tAKMxszjWKcusNuasXNjXzWmzEzciPehPBcruhAKM87sjePz1KL8a4GA3p6c8o5p9Z14pKNvCUPFQe6CnksLsaU4kmVXBli3rvTHrWmwtQvJp9MPgu6lnGAC32sg4uByWd8IW4Y0BPsObZ0S2HvV9r70PIrfpYX9WHtU0zA1LPVsJTYskOmHv8ZmdS34aa1wNTja-mf5iAkoP1i6vH91_ckXhWvytSDSmFSQ4jtq1VTl61Pn3SeVLRhI98D0Hkf3tUfRPFh5d8AAAD__6uDmqI)** I asked her again anyway, because I wanted it recorded and I wanted it to be completely unmistakable to anyone who watched it later. All I have to do is fill out the question ballot, and then I can vote? **" Yes, sir."** We titled the video **" The Big Murkowski,"** and you really do have to laugh a little bit at it, because the only other available option is putting your head through a wall.
The funny part ends fast. **Every single thing I am about to tell you makes the thing before it worse.**
| ONE. A total stranger walked in off the street carrying no identification of any kind and was offered a ballot. TWO. The name on that ballot belongs to a United States Senator's brother who lives roughly three thousand miles away, in another state entirely. THREE. We did it again. Different polling place, same morning. One of my reporters gave the name **Karina Waller** -- Senator Murkowski's own **State Director**. No ID. Same offer. **[Help us keep doing exactly this.](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckb2OpTAMhZ8mdKD8QMIUKVa6ut1suyUyiQHrEhLlZ-b1V8xqqu2ms4-PP9k6f96Xd6CTrv03BLRUypLLUg8qB5QVXQwICWrFfC2SS93zuZd6AVfpA5cROm8nKeZt7tAKMxszjWKcusNuasXNjXzWmzEzciPehPBcruhAKM87sjePz1KL8a4GA3p6c8o5p9Z14pKNvCUPFQe6CnksLsaU4kmVXBli3rvTHrWmwtQvJp9MPgu6lnGAC32sg4uByWd8IW4Y0BPsObZ0S2HvV9r70PIrfpYX9WHtU0zA1LPVsJTYskOmHv8ZmdS34aa1wNTja-mf5iAkoP1i6vH91_ckXhWvytSDSmFSQ4jtq1VTl61Pn3SeVLRhI98D0Hkf3tUfRPFh5d8AAAD__6uDmqI)** FOUR. Alaska law says you show identification to get a ballot, and the one narrow exception written into it is that the poll worker personally knows the person standing in front of them. Nobody in either of those buildings had ever laid eyes on us before in their lives. FIVE. Nobody wrote anything down. Nobody picked up a phone. Nobody flagged a single thing. We asked, we got our answer, and we walked back out the door.
---
Now here is the part that should stop you cold. Senator Murkowski has spent this year fighting the SAVE Act, which her office describes as "an overly burdensome, one-size-fits-all mandate from Washington," and the argument underneath that position has always been the same one we hear everywhere: that the hole we keep describing does not actually exist outside of our imagination. **We just showed her the hole. In her own state. Using her own brother's name.** Before anyone calls this a partisan hit job, let me say it plainly: Senator Murkowski is a Republican, and it does not matter to me even a little, because a hole in the process is a hole in the process and it does not care one bit about which party happens to walk through it. Her office did not say they were going to fix it. Her office said this:
| "Voter impersonation is a crime and should be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law." OFFICE OF SEN. LISA MURKOWSKI
---
Now I want to be precise with you about what we did and did not do, because you fund this operation and you deserve that kind of accounting from me. **I did not vote. I did not sign anyone's name. I never touched a ballot.** I asked a question, I recorded the answer, and I left. That is what reporters do. The response from a sitting United States Senator's office was to start talking about prosecuting me for it. Patriot, this has become a pattern, and I want you to see it as clearly as I have come to see it over the last three weeks. Last week the Secretary of State of Minnesota published a statement accusing my journalists of **" lying, lawbreaking, and disruptions"** and announced that **law enforcement is reviewing** them. He never named a single law we broke. This week the office of a United States Senator is talking about prosecuting a journalist to the fullest extent of the law. Michigan. Minnesota. Alaska. Three states in three weeks, and every single time we have gone looking, we have found the same hole sitting there in plain sight. Nobody ever rushes to close the hole. **They come after the person holding the flashlight.**
[GIVE NOW -- FUND THE NEXT STATE](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckb2OpTAMhZ8mdKD8QMIUKVa6ut1suyUyiQHrEhLlZ-b1V8xqqu2ms4-PP9k6f96Xd6CTrv03BLRUypLLUg8qB5QVXQwICWrFfC2SS93zuZd6AVfpA5cROm8nKeZt7tAKMxszjWKcusNuasXNjXzWmzEzciPehPBcruhAKM87sjePz1KL8a4GA3p6c8o5p9Z14pKNvCUPFQe6CnksLsaU4kmVXBli3rvTHrWmwtQvJp9MPgu6lnGAC32sg4uByWd8IW4Y0BPsObZ0S2HvV9r70PIrfpYX9WHtU0zA1LPVsJTYskOmHv8ZmdS34aa1wNTja-mf5iAkoP1i6vH91_ckXhWvytSDSmFSQ4jtq1VTl61Pn3SeVLRhI98D0Hkf3tUfRPFh5d8AAAD__6uDmqI)
Let me tell you what Alaska cost.
| $50,000
---
What this single investigation cost to produce -- so that you could hear two words said out loud at a folding table in Anchorage.
That covered the flights to Anchorage and back, the weeks of preparation before anyone ever got on a plane, the records work, the equipment, and a team standing on the ground at dawn on primary day three thousand miles from our office. It also covered the lawyers who reviewed every frame of that footage before a single second of it went to air, because we understood exactly what was coming the moment it did. I would spend every dollar of it again tomorrow morning without blinking. Here is my problem. **[We do not have another fifty thousand dollars sitting in a drawer waiting for the next state.](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckb2OpTAMhZ8mdKD8QMIUKVa6ut1suyUyiQHrEhLlZ-b1V8xqqu2ms4-PP9k6f96Xd6CTrv03BLRUypLLUg8qB5QVXQwICWrFfC2SS93zuZd6AVfpA5cROm8nKeZt7tAKMxszjWKcusNuasXNjXzWmzEzciPehPBcruhAKM87sjePz1KL8a4GA3p6c8o5p9Z14pKNvCUPFQe6CnksLsaU4kmVXBli3rvTHrWmwtQvJp9MPgu6lnGAC32sg4uByWd8IW4Y0BPsObZ0S2HvV9r70PIrfpYX9WHtU0zA1LPVsJTYskOmHv8ZmdS34aa1wNTja-mf5iAkoP1i6vH91_ckXhWvytSDSmFSQ4jtq1VTl61Pn3SeVLRhI98D0Hkf3tUfRPFh5d8AAAD__6uDmqI)** And there is a next one. There is always a next one. Alaska is not special. Alaska is simply the state we happened to be standing in on Tuesday, and everything you are about to watch came out of a single morning and one honest question asked out loud at a folding table. **Imagine what is sitting untouched in the other forty-nine.** **In twenty-eight days, the first federal ballots for November go out.** After that date the machine is running, and everything we have not found yet gets voted on anyway. You and your family have to live under whatever comes out of those buildings, and so does mine, and that is the entire reason I keep walking into them with a camera when it would be far easier and considerably safer not to. There is nobody else writing this check, and there never has been. It has always been you.
[YES, JAMES -- I'LL HELP FUND THE NEXT ONE](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckb2OpTAMhZ8mdKD8QMIUKVa6ut1suyUyiQHrEhLlZ-b1V8xqqu2ms4-PP9k6f96Xd6CTrv03BLRUypLLUg8qB5QVXQwICWrFfC2SS93zuZd6AVfpA5cROm8nKeZt7tAKMxszjWKcusNuasXNjXzWmzEzciPehPBcruhAKM87sjePz1KL8a4GA3p6c8o5p9Z14pKNvCUPFQe6CnksLsaU4kmVXBli3rvTHrWmwtQvJp9MPgu6lnGAC32sg4uByWd8IW4Y0BPsObZ0S2HvV9r70PIrfpYX9WHtU0zA1LPVsJTYskOmHv8ZmdS34aa1wNTja-mf5iAkoP1i6vH91_ckXhWvytSDSmFSQ4jtq1VTl61Pn3SeVLRhI98D0Hkf3tUfRPFh5d8AAAD__6uDmqI)
Thank you for everything you do. In Truth, James O'Keefe Founder, O'Keefe Media Group
**P.S.** The video is called **" The Big Murkowski,"** and I hope it makes you laugh. Then I hope it makes you furious. Different polling place, same morning. One of my reporters gave the name Karina Waller -- Senator Murkowski's own State Director. No ID. Same offer. FOUR. Alaska law says you show identification to get a ballot, and the one narrow exception written into it is that the poll worker personally knows the person standing in front of them. Nobody in either of those buildings had ever laid eyes on us before in their lives. FIVE. Nobody wrote anything down. Nobody picked up a phone. Nobody flagged a single thing. We asked, we got our answer, and we walked back out the door. Now here is the part that should stop you cold. Senator Murkowski has spent this year fighting the SAVE Act, which her office describes as "an overly burdensome, one-size-fits-all mandate from Washington," and the argument underneath that position has always been the same one we hear everywhere: that the hole we keep describing does not actually exist outside of our imagination. We just showed her the hole. In her own state. Using her own brother's name. Before anyone calls this a partisan hit job, let me say it plainly: Senator Murkowski is a Republican, and it does not matter to me even a little, because a hole in the process is a hole in the process and it does not care one bit about which party happens to walk through it. The response from a sitting United States Senator's office was to start talking about prosecuting me for it. He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | | | | Editor’s Note: Jason Bodner spent two decades on Wall Street. For the last 78 years, one thing has predicted a bull market... With 100% accuracy... The midterm election. It’s happened every time since 1948. And some studies show it going back to the 1800s. It doesn’t matter which party wins. Or what the economic conditions are. In war and in peace... In fact, post-midterm years beat the prior year 6-to-1. And Nvidia soared 205% in the next 12 months... AMD was up 96%. And Super Micro Computer jumped 203%. All in just one calendar year after the election. | | | | | | Team Mackenzie,No surprise: Bob Brooks is refusing to agree to a September debate with Congressman Ryan Mackenzie — even though Pennsylvania voters will begin casting their mail-in ballots!Ryan agreed weeks ago to September debate dates with both BRC 13 and WFMZ. And while the September 8th WFMZ debate remains available, Brooks has refused to commit to it.Instead, Brooks has now agreed to a WFMZ debate where the second half would not air until **November 2, just one day before Election Day.** That means tens of thousands of voters will have cast their ballots before they ever see the candidates debate. That is simply wrong and undemocratic.More than one-quarter of Pennsylvania voters cast their ballots before Election Day in 2024.Ryan has been clear: **voters deserve to hear from both candidates before they vote.** “Every voter in the Lehigh Valley and the Poconos deserves an opportunity to compare the candidates in a debate. We have offered and agreed to several dates in September, but Bob Brooks has declined or ignored all of them. My opponent’s latest attempt to delay any debate from being broadcast until immediately before the election, when tens of thousands of district residents will have already voted, represents a deliberate effort to hide from voters. It’s time for my opponent to stop playing games, agree to a debate, and answer for his record.”Brooks has already faced criticism for his performance in previous public forums, with PoliticsPA reporting that he was accused of “barely answering the questions” during a Cedar Crest College debate during the primary.Brooks was also taken to task by former Democratic Congresswoman Susan Wild for refusing to take part in a voter education interview with our local media before this spring’s Primary Election - after originally agreeing to participate. Apparently hiding from the voters and letting dark money special interests try to buy him votes is Bob Brooks’ campaign strategy. Of course, it’s easy to see why Brooks wants to hide. Brooks refuses to debate and answer questions about the scandals that have plagued his campaign: \- stealing $162,000 from his own family that he refuses to pay after a court ordered him to do so \- not having workers’ comp coverage for his own employees \- taking multiple raises as a union boss, while cutting benefits for his members \- posting racists memes online \- calling volunteer firefighters “sh*tbags and scabs”
The list goes on and on. It would easily take a full 60 minute debate to confront Brooks on all of his outrageous behavior.**These are just some of the questions the voters of PA-7 deserve to hear answered before they cast their ballots.** Ryan is ready to debate. The September 8 WFMZ date is available.**Bob Brooks should stop delaying, stop hiding, and agree to debate in September.****Please look at the Press Release below for more details.**

disclaimer_text: Paid for by the DSCC | PO Box 96047, Washington, DC 20090 | **[dscc
body:
| | | [](https://go.dscc.org/go/23824?amount=7&t=4&firstname=&lastname=&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com&addr1=&addr2=&city=Cresco&state=Pennsylvania&zip=18326&phone=None&employer=&occupation=&ask=7&amounts=7%2C14%2C28%2C70&code=DPE-FM-20260826-PeggyFlanagan-FlanaganNativeVoicesTandem-Pros-sl1&refcode=DPE-FM-20260826-PeggyFlanagan-FlanaganNativeVoicesTandem-Pros-sl1&akid=25632%2E9716520%2Ed6iZkI)
Friend, in almost 250 years, there's never been a Native woman serving in the US Senate. **It's time to change that.**

I'm Peggy Flanagan, the Democratic nominee for US Senate in Minnesota.

I am Ojibwe and a proud member of the White Earth Nation. My family is the Wolf Clan. The mission of my clan is to never leave anyone behind - and that's been my guiding principle.

I am the descendant of people who were forced off their land onto the White Earth reservation. I am the relative of residential boarding school survivors. I am the daughter of a man who always spoke truth to power for the good of the Anishinaabe people.

I'm thinking of my daughter - who just got her first jingle dress - and whether or not she will see Indigenous women in all parts of our government.

**Right now, there are _no_ Native voices in the US Senate. _If I win this race, we can change that._**

[**It's high time that all our communities have a seat at the table. If you agree, will you pitch in $7 or whatever you can to power my campaign and the DSCC, help me make history, and flip the Senate?**](https://go.dscc.org/go/23824?amount=7&t=6&firstname=&lastname=&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com&addr1=&addr2=&city=Cresco&state=Pennsylvania&zip=18326&phone=None&employer=&occupation=&ask=7&amounts=7%2C14%2C28%2C70&code=DPE-FM-20260826-PeggyFlanagan-FlanaganNativeVoicesTandem-Pros-sl1&refcode=DPE-FM-20260826-PeggyFlanagan-FlanaganNativeVoicesTandem-Pros-sl1&akid=25632%2E9716520%2Ed6iZkI)

Fatma Al-Ajab stand beside her her ailing mother, Hanan Al-Ajab, holding up a nasal cannula that is unattached as a result of a lack of available oxygen cylinders inside the oncology department of Al-Shifa Hospital in Gaza City. August 2026. Screenshot of video by Abdel Qader Sabbah.
GAZA CITY--Hanan Al-Ajab lay on a gurney in the oncology department of Al-Shifa Hospital in Gaza City, barely clinging to life--her mouth agape, her eyes shut. Her daughter, Fatma Al-Ajab, held up a nasal cannula, the end of the plastic tube dangling in the air and unattached. "There is no oxygen cylinder," Al-Ajab told Drop Site News in distress. "There is nothing. Nothing is available. Most things are unavailable. The staff have done everything they can, God bless them, and they are working with whatever they have. But when there is a shortage of oxygen, everything deteriorates."
"My mother has become a skeleton," she said pointing to her mother's emaciated body. Hanan, 63, was diagnosed with pancreatic cancer several months ago. She is one of an estimated 10,000 to 12,000 cancer patients in Gaza who depend on access to specialized healthcare, according to the UN. Yet critical shortages in chemotherapy agents and other lifesaving medicines, as well as a lack of properly functioning medical equipment, have left her unable to receive proper care.
Israel has continued to heavily restrict humanitarian aid and life essentials from entering Gaza--in blatant violation of the ceasefire agreement that went into effect on October 10, 2025.
"She reaches the point where she is suffocating and dying," Al-Ajab said. "Look at her--do you see how her mouth is wide open? Look at the tube. She doesn't have what she needs. She is supposed to be receiving oxygen continuously. Her blood levels drop, everything drops. All of her bodily functions deteriorate at once because there is no oxygen and she can't breathe."
In adjacent rooms and hallways, other patients lay prone on hospital beds wearing oxygen masks and nasal cannulas--some attached to oxygen cylinders, others not, and all of them struggling to breathe.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/35d5414c-1cd7-4e08-b023-7338020e8744?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
###### Scenes inside the oxygen filling station and the oncology department at Al-Shifa Hospital. August 2026. Video by Abdel Qader Sabbah.
Last week, Gaza's Ministry of Health issued an urgent appeal, warning that the few functional oxygen plants in the enclave were operating beyond their maximum capacity and frequently breaking down. The ministry called for the immediate opening of crossings to allow for the importing of spare parts and technical equipment necessary for maintenance, as well as the emergency supply of new plants.
"Access to oxygen is not a medical luxury, it is a lifeline for many vital and life-saving departments," the Health Ministry said in a statement.
"Before the war, we had 34 oxygen generation plants. The occupation put 22 of them out of service," Mazen Al-Aryashi, the head of the Engineering Department at the Ministry of Health, told Drop Site. He stood inside the oxygen filling station in Al-Shifa Hospital--a mess of rusted cylinders and dusty machines surrounded by destroyed equipment piled in a corner. "The 12 remaining plants urgently need routine and emergency maintenance to ensure they continue operating properly and can supply ministry facilities with the oxygen needed to keep critical departments running--particularly neonatal units, intensive care units, operating rooms, and inpatient wards."
"Before the war, we had 30 filling units. Now, only four are available to serve all of these needs," Al-Aryashi continued. "If any one of these plants breaks down, God forbid, it would mean shutting down numerous departments in a hospital. If a central oxygen plant stops operating, it would effectively be a death sentence for patients."
Since the war began in October 2023, Gaza's health care system has come under sustained assault by the Israeli military. Hospitals, clinics, and medical centers were systematically bombed and raided, while doctors and health care workers killed and imprisoned. A suffocating siege on supplies caused severe shortages of not only medicine but also parts to repair and restore critical equipment. Little has changed since a so-called "ceasefire" went into effect nearly a year ago.
"The healthcare system in the Gaza Strip has experienced systemic collapse," UNRWA said in a [report](https://substack.com/redirect/5f40c9c1-5a80-4a35-ac7e-74c8de11e04e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) earlier this month. "The healthcare services in the Gaza Strip have been degraded at every level, from primary healthcare and specialist treatment to disease surveillance, maternal care, emergency response, and medical referral systems.... Despite the ceasefire, no health facility in the Gaza Strip has been rehabilitated to full functionality, while the healthcare system remains severely strained by shortages of personnel, medicines, medical supplies, and fuel."
Along with Israel's near-daily bombing, shelling, and shooting attacks in Gaza, the report stresses the continuing blockade as a primary cause for the collapse of medical infrastructure.
"Continued restrictions on the entry of humanitarian assistance, essential medicines, medical equipment, and construction materials needed to sustain and expand essential health services as well as rebuild destroyed healthcare facilities and infrastructure, have prevented much of the sector from being rehabilitated," the UNRWA report said. "As of June 2026, WHO reported that the principal barriers to health facilities being rehabilitated in the Gaza Strip were a lack of medical equipment, affecting 97% of facilities, and shortages of medicines, affecting over 80% of facilities."
In the face of crumbling medical equipment, teams of engineers in Gaza have resorted to salvaging parts from damaged machinery and refitting them in a desperate attempt to repair what they can and restore some functionality to various medical devices, including critical diagnostic equipment.
Inside Al-Shifa Hospital, the walls of the medical equipment maintenance room are lined with open shelves stacked with disassembled medical devices, soldering irons, circuit boards, and tangles of wires.
"In the past, spare parts were supplied as equipment broke down. Currently, that option is no longer available to us because of the situation in Gaza," Ahmed Younis, an engineer at Al-Shifa Hospital told Drop Site. "We now collect equipment damaged during the [Israeli] ground incursion and the bombing of the hospital. We collect them, dismantle matching equipment of the same type, salvage and repair the parts, and then reassemble the equipment. We have managed to restore only around 15% of the hospital's equipment. Most of the equipment needs to be replaced and is difficult to repair under the current conditions."
[](https://substack.com/redirect/71e48c48-ac8c-4be7-8713-e3100bc43652?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
###### Inside the medical equipment maintenance room at Al-Shifa hospital where engineers try to repair what they can with salvaged parts. August 2026. Video by Abdel Qader Sabbah.
Once the largest medical facility in the Gaza Strip, accounting for nearly a third of the entire territory's healthcare and medical capacity, Al-Shifa hospital is now a bombed-out, charred shell following successive Israeli raids.
Younis said most of the equipment at the hospital--diagnostic devices, laboratory equipment, X-ray machines, echocardiography machines, and ultrasound machines--have been refurbished in this way. "But the equipment is not operating at the level of efficiency it is supposed to," he warned. "The MRI machines and other radiology equipment, such as CT scanners and lithotripsy machines, were completely destroyed. Not a single one is currently operational at Al-Shifa hospital. There are no CT scanners, no MRI machines, no catheterization machine, and no other radiology equipment."
The lack of functional diagnostic equipment has severely impaired doctors' abilities to treat patients in Gaza.
"Most of the equipment was lost as a result of the destruction and fires caused by the war and the bombardment of Al-Shifa medical complex," Dr. Mohammed Amin Matar, the head of the radiology department at Al-Shifa and a specialist in diagnostic and interventional radiology, told Drop Site. "This has severely affected our ability to diagnose patients and manage medical cases. Diagnosis is the first step in treating a patient. Without a diagnosis, patients cannot receive proper treatment. In many cases, patients need an MRI for diagnosis, but it is not available. They also need other advanced tests that are completely unavailable now, although they were available before the war. We no longer have these capabilities. This has resulted in severe complications and, in some cases, patients have lost their lives because we were unable to determine the correct diagnosis."
The destruction of medical facilities and the steady deterioration of equipment that remained comes as Israel continues to bomb Gaza on a routine basis, including targeting civilian infrastructure. On Monday alone, the Israeli military struck a water desalination plant in Gaza City and destroyed a warehouse in Deir al-Balah belonging to Ard El Insan, a local humanitarian organization working in partnership with Medical Aid for Palestinians (MAP). The warehouse stored nutrition supplies intended for children, pregnant women, and breastfeeding mothers in Gaza.
"The loss of these supplies comes at a time when nutritional needs in Gaza remain severe," MAP said in a statement. "A new UNICEF report this week has shown there are concerning rates of maternal and chronic malnutrition in Gaza and that humanitarian aid is vital to prevent further deterioration of people's conditions."
Gaza's healthcare system is still reeling from nearly three years of attacks targeting medical personnel and infrastructure. As of June, the World Health Organization (WHO) documented 971 attacks on healthcare in Gaza, affecting at least 804 health facilities, including hospitals and clinics, and 268 ambulances. More than 1,700 health workers have been killed or injured, according to WHO, while hundreds of others have been arrested and imprisoned.
Meanwhile, the amount of humanitarian aid allowed into Gaza has declined throughout 2026 in an ongoing violation of the so-called ceasefire. "Between March and May 2026, over 42% of planned aid delivery missions to the Gaza Strip were cancelled or impeded by the Israeli authorities, the majority involving critical medical, water, and sanitation supplies," the August UNRWA report found. "During the same period, the volume of aid entering the Gaza Strip fell by over 43% compared with the first three months of the ceasefire. Of the total aid entering, only around 1.2% included medicines and health supplies."
In parallel with the decimation of Gaza's health care system, Israel is continuing to severely restrict the number of Palestinians allowed out of Gaza to seek treatment abroad. Some 300 Palestinians have died waiting for medical evacuations since the "ceasefire" went into effect, according to the Health Ministry, with 20,000 patients waiting for authorization and only around 2,000 being allowed to cross so far.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1ac54e3d-b01b-44a3-acc1-4c6d08f1f50b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Raed Al-Hagag received a referral for medical evacuation to receive treatment abroad for his heart condition, but like thousands of Palestinians he has spent months waiting for approval. August 2026. Screenshot of video by Abdel Qader Sabbah.
Raed Al-Hagag, 59, has been suffering from heart problems for over a decade and has required surgery to insert stents several times over the years. "Three of my main arteries are blocked, and I have narrowing in another artery, which is also very weak, so the doctor filled out a referral for me to receive treatment abroad," Al-Haggag told Drop Site as he sat in his makeshift tent in the Jawazat displacement camp in western Gaza City. "But unfortunately, until now, I haven't been able to leave. I'm waiting for my turn, just like thousands of other patients."
He continued, "Before, hospitals had the resources. I could get stents that helped keep me alive, and that gave many other patients a chance to live....After the war that was waged against us, the hospitals have no resources. The hospitals are destroyed, treatment is unavailable, and there are no facilities equipped to receive patients with serious conditions like heart disease."
"Medical equipment is virtually nonexistent, and what remains is poor quality and worn out," he said. "We are suffering from an extremely severe shortage of medical equipment. The longer this continues, the greater the danger. Our lives are at risk."
_Sharif Abdel Kouddous and Jawa Ahmad contributed to this report. Sami Vanderlip edited the video._

Please consider becoming a paid subscriber or making a . | | ---|---|--- Fatma Al-Ajab stand beside her her ailing mother, Hanan Al-Ajab, holding up a nasal cannula that is unattached as a result of a lack of available oxygen cylinders inside the oncology department of Al-Shifa Hospital in Gaza City. August 2026. Screenshot of video by Abdel Qader Sabbah. GAZA CITY--Hanan Al-Ajab lay on a gurney in the oncology department of Al-Shifa Hospital in Gaza City, barely clinging to life--her mouth agape, her eyes shut. Her daughter, Fatma Al-Ajab, held up a nasal cannula, the end of the plastic tube dangling in the air and unattached. "There is no oxygen cylinder," Al-Ajab told Drop Site News in distress. "There is nothing. Nothing is available. Most things are unavailable. The staff have done everything they can, God bless them, and they are working with whatever they have. But when there is a shortage of oxygen, everything deteriorates." "My mother has become a skeleton," she said pointing to her mother's emaciated body. Hanan, 63, was diagnosed with pancreatic cancer several months ago. She is one of an estimated 10,000 to 12,000 cancer patients in Gaza who depend on access to specialized healthcare, according to the UN. Yet critical shortages in chemotherapy agents and other lifesaving medicines, as well as a lack of properly functioning medical equipment, have left her unable to receive proper care. Israel has continued to heavily restrict humanitarian aid and life essentials from entering Gaza--in blatant violation of the ceasefire agreement that went into effect on October 10, 2025. "She reaches the point where she is suffocating and dying," Al-Ajab said. "Look at her--do you see how her mouth is wide open? Look at the tube. She doesn't have what she needs. She is supposed to be receiving oxygen continuously. Her blood levels drop, everything drops. All of her bodily functions deteriorate at once because there is no oxygen and she can't breathe." In adjacent rooms and hallways, other patients lay prone on hospital beds wearing oxygen masks and nasal cannulas--some attached to oxygen cylinders, others not, and all of them struggling to breathe. Scenes inside the oxygen filling station and the oncology department at Al-Shifa Hospital. August 2026. Video by Abdel Qader Sabbah. Last week, Gaza's Ministry of Health issued an urgent appeal, warning that the few functional oxygen plants in the enclave were operating beyond their maximum capacity and frequently breaking down. The ministry called for the immediate opening of crossings to allow for the importing of spare parts and technical equipment necessary for maintenance, as well as the emergency supply of new plants. "Access to oxygen is not a medical luxury, it is a lifeline for many vital and life-saving departments," the Health Ministry said in a statement. "Before the war, we had 34 oxygen generation plants. The occupation put 22 of them out of service," Mazen Al-Aryashi, the head of the Engineering Department at the Ministry of Health, told Drop Site. He stood inside the oxygen filling station in Al-Shifa Hospital--a mess of rusted cylinders and dusty machines surrounded by destroyed equipment piled in a corner. "The 12 remaining plants urgently need routine and emergency maintenance to ensure they continue operating properly and can supply ministry facilities with the oxygen needed to keep critical departments running--particularly neonatal units, intensive care units, operating rooms, and inpatient wards." "Before the war, we had 30 filling units. Now, only four are available to serve all of these needs," Al-Aryashi continued. "If any one of these plants breaks down, God forbid, it would mean shutting down numerous departments in a hospital. If a central oxygen plant stops operating, it would effectively be a death sentence for patients." Since the war began in October 2023, Gaza's health care system has come under sustained assault by the Israeli military. Hospitals, clinics, and medical centers were systematically bombed and raided, while doctors and health care workers killed and imprisoned. A suffocating siege on supplies caused severe shortages of not only medicine but also parts to repair and restore critical equipment. Little has changed since a so-called "ceasefire" went into effect nearly a year ago. "The healthcare system in the Gaza Strip has experienced systemic collapse," UNRWA said in a earlier this month. "The healthcare services in the Gaza Strip have been degraded at every level, from primary healthcare and specialist treatment to disease surveillance, maternal care, emergency response, and medical referral systems.... Despite the ceasefire, no health facility in the Gaza Strip has been rehabilitated to full functionality, while the healthcare system remains severely strained by shortages of personnel, medicines, medical supplies, and fuel." Along with Israel's near-daily bombing, shelling, and shooting attacks in Gaza, the report stresses the continuing blockade as a primary cause for the collapse of medical infrastructure. "Continued restrictions on the entry of humanitarian assistance, essential medicines, medical equipment, and construction materials needed to sustain and expand essential health services as well as rebuild destroyed healthcare facilities and infrastructure, have prevented much of the sector from being rehabilitated," the UNRWA report said. "As of June 2026, WHO reported that the principal barriers to health facilities being rehabilitated in the Gaza Strip were a lack of medical equipment, affecting 97% of facilities, and shortages of medicines, affecting over 80% of facilities." In the face of crumbling medical equipment, teams of engineers in Gaza have resorted to salvaging parts from damaged machinery and refitting them in a desperate attempt to repair what they can and restore some functionality to various medical devices, including critical diagnostic equipment. Inside Al-Shifa Hospital, the walls of the medical equipment maintenance room are lined with open shelves stacked with disassembled medical devices, soldering irons, circuit boards, and tangles of wires. "In the past, spare parts were supplied as equipment broke down. Currently, that option is no longer available to us because of the situation in Gaza," Ahmed Younis, an engineer at Al-Shifa Hospital told Drop Site. "We now collect equipment damaged during the [Israeli] ground incursion and the bombing of the hospital. We collect them, dismantle matching equipment of the same type, salvage and repair the parts, and then reassemble the equipment. We have managed to restore only around 15% of the hospital's equipment. Most of the equipment needs to be replaced and is difficult to repair under the current conditions." Inside the medical equipment maintenance room at Al-Shifa hospital where engineers try to repair what they can with salvaged parts. August 2026. Video by Abdel Qader Sabbah. Once the largest medical facility in the Gaza Strip, accounting for nearly a third of the entire territory's healthcare and medical capacity, Al-Shifa hospital is now a bombed-out, charred shell following successive Israeli raids. Younis said most of the equipment at the hospital--diagnostic devices, laboratory equipment, X-ray machines, echocardiography machines, and ultrasound machines--have been refurbished in this way. "But the equipment is not operating at the level of efficiency it is supposed to," he warned. "The MRI machines and other radiology equipment, such as CT scanners and lithotripsy machines, were completely destroyed. Not a single one is currently operational at Al-Shifa hospital. There are no CT scanners, no MRI machines, no catheterization machine, and no other radiology equipment." The lack of functional diagnostic equipment has severely impaired doctors' abilities to treat patients in Gaza. "Most of the equipment was lost as a result of the destruction and fires caused by the war and the bombardment of Al-Shifa medical complex," Dr. Mohammed Amin Matar, the head of the radiology department at Al-Shifa and a specialist in diagnostic and interventional radiology, told Drop Site. "This has severely affected our ability to diagnose patients and manage medical cases. Diagnosis is the first step in treating a patient. Without a diagnosis, patients cannot receive proper treatment. In many cases, patients need an MRI for diagnosis, but it is not available. They also need other advanced tests that are completely unavailable now, although they were available before the war. We no longer have these capabilities. This has resulted in severe complications and, in some cases, patients have lost their lives because we were unable to determine the correct diagnosis." The destruction of medical facilities and the steady deterioration of equipment that remained comes as Israel continues to bomb Gaza on a routine basis, including targeting civilian infrastructure. On Monday alone, the Israeli military struck a water desalination plant in Gaza City and destroyed a warehouse in Deir al-Balah belonging to Ard El Insan, a local humanitarian organization working in partnership with Medical Aid for Palestinians (MAP). The warehouse stored nutrition supplies intended for children, pregnant women, and breastfeeding mothers in Gaza. "The loss of these supplies comes at a time when nutritional needs in Gaza remain severe," MAP said in a statement. "A new UNICEF report this week has shown there are concerning rates of maternal and chronic malnutrition in Gaza and that humanitarian aid is vital to prevent further deterioration of people's conditions." Gaza's healthcare system is still reeling from nearly three years of attacks targeting medical personnel and infrastructure. As of June, the World Health Organization (WHO) documented 971 attacks on healthcare in Gaza, affecting at least 804 health facilities, including hospitals and clinics, and 268 ambulances. More than 1,700 health workers have been killed or injured, according to WHO, while hundreds of others have been arrested and imprisoned. Meanwhile, the amount of humanitarian aid allowed into Gaza has declined throughout 2026 in an ongoing violation of the so-called ceasefire. "Between March and May 2026, over 42% of planned aid delivery missions to the Gaza Strip were cancelled or impeded by the Israeli authorities, the majority involving critical medical, water, and sanitation supplies," the August UNRWA report found. "During the same period, the volume of aid entering the Gaza Strip fell by over 43% compared with the first three months of the ceasefire. Of the total aid entering, only around 1.2% included medicines and health supplies." In parallel with the decimation of Gaza's health care system, Israel is continuing to severely restrict the number of Palestinians allowed out of Gaza to seek treatment abroad. Some 300 Palestinians have died waiting for medical evacuations since the "ceasefire" went into effect, according to the Health Ministry, with 20,000 patients waiting for authorization and only around 2,000 being allowed to cross so far. | | ---|---|--- Raed Al-Hagag received a referral for medical evacuation to receive treatment abroad for his heart condition, but like thousands of Palestinians he has spent months waiting for approval. August 2026. Screenshot of video by Abdel Qader Sabbah. Raed Al-Hagag, 59, has been suffering from heart problems for over a decade and has required surgery to insert stents several times over the years. "Three of my main arteries are blocked, and I have narrowing in another artery, which is also very weak, so the doctor filled out a referral for me to receive treatment abroad," Al-Haggag told Drop Site as he sat in his makeshift tent in the Jawazat displacement camp in western Gaza City. "But unfortunately, until now, I haven't been able to leave. I'm waiting for my turn, just like thousands of other patients." He continued, "Before, hospitals had the resources. I could get stents that helped keep me alive, and that gave many other patients a chance to live....After the war that was waged against us, the hospitals have no resources. The hospitals are destroyed, treatment is unavailable, and there are no facilities equipped to receive patients with serious conditions like heart disease." "Medical equipment is virtually nonexistent, and what remains is poor quality and worn out," he said. "We are suffering from an extremely severe shortage of medical equipment. The longer this continues, the greater the danger. Our lives are at risk." Sharif Abdel Kouddous and Jawa Ahmad contributed to this report. clean_body: In Maine, the choice for governor is crystal clear. | = The choice in Maine's governor's race is crystal clear: Hannah Pingree (D) has spent her career fighting for Maine families. Bobby Charles (R) keeps siding with Donald Trump — even when Trump's agenda threatens to hurt the people he wants to represent. Hannah is a lifelong Mainer and proven leader who served as speaker of the Maine House and led the Governor's Office of Policy Innovation and the Future. Throughout her career, she's worked to lower costs, expand opportunity, protect kids from toxic chemicals, and defend reproductive freedom. Now, she's running to keep Maine moving forward — and EMILYs List is proud to stand with her. = | = The contrast with Bobby Charles couldn't be sharper. Charles has repeatedly backed Trump's agenda, even when it comes at Maine’s expense. He praised Trump’s tariffs as "exactly right" and "masterful" despite the damage they've done to Maine's export economy. He supports new restrictions on MaineCare, a critical program hundreds of thousands of Mainers depend on for affordable healthcare access. For Charles, staying in Trump's good graces comes first. For Hannah, Maine always does. Maine needs a governor who answers to the people who live there — not Donald Trump. Hannah Pingree is that leader. Mississippi Center for Public Policy MississippiWire.News

NATIONAL
Public Pension "No Stable Funding", warns official (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=public-pension-no-stable-funding-warns-official)
Mississippi's public pension system reported a 17.11% investment return for fiscal 2026 on Wednesday — and minutes later its board chairman read aloud language in the system's own revised investment policy stating the fund has no stable funding mechanism.
Continue reading → (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=public-pension-no-stable-funding-warns-official)
JPS Confirms Higher Attendance Threshold Under New State Law (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=jps-confirms-higher-attendance-threshold-under-new-state-law)
Jackson Public Schools says a new state law now requires students to be present for 66% of the school day, up from 63%, to avoid being marked absent.
Read → (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=jps-confirms-higher-attendance-threshold-under-new-state-law)
Pearl Board Denies Cannabis Dispensary Permit (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=pearl-board-denies-cannabis-dispensary-permit)
The Pearl Board of Aldermen voted to deny a conditional use permit for a proposed medical cannabis dispensary after city staff recommended against it.
Read → (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=pearl-board-denies-cannabis-dispensary-permit)

Madison County Board Upholds $292 Million Per-Building Valuation on Amazon Data Centers

OXFORD —
Greenwood Councilman Questions Process Behind Emergency Property Demolitions (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=greenwood-councilman-questions-process-behind-emergency-property-demolitions)
GREENWOOD — A city councilman told fellow council members Wednesday that Greenwood may not be properly following its own ordinance before declaring dilapidated properties emergencies and clearing them without a standard hearing.

JACKSON — Rights to name stadium deal approved

JACKSON —

GREENVILLE — Mayor Errick Simmons told a Greenville budget session he will ask the city council to hold ad valorem taxes flat, fund departments at last year's levels and approve no capital outlay for the coming year — while stressing that the decisions belong to the council, not to him.
Boom Belt Mississippi! Solero Technologies To Add 86 Jobs At Water Valley Plant In $14 Million Expansion (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=boom-belt-mississippi-solero-technologies-to-add-86-jobs-at-water-valley-plant-i)
WATER VALLEY — Automotive parts maker Solero Technologies is adding 14 manufacturing lines and 86 jobs at its Water Valley plant in a project the state values at more than $14 million, with assistance from the Mississippi Development Authority through the MFLEX program.

TUPELO — The Tupelo City Council on Aug. 18 approved an ordinance raising Water & Light electric rates, effective Oct. 1, 2026.

Mississippi's teacher spending through the state's ClassWallet platform has climbed to just over $10 million this year, State Superintendent Lance Evans told the Mississippi Board of Education.

State Education Enhancement Funds reach districts Wednesday. For the first time the money moves through ClassWallet, a digital platform that tracks spending and collects receipts automatically.

National

The Mississippi Board of Education finalized a revised rule for reporting unexcused student absences at its August meeting.

Too many North Carolinians are already feeling the burdens of rising prices. This chaotic trade war with Canada will only continue to hurt small businesses, farmers and hardworking people across the state.
I sat down with Jen Psaki to discuss how Canada's retaliatory tariffs will impact North Carolina and how North Carolina Republicans are trying to make it harder for people to vote. You can watch the full interview here:
[](https://substack.com/redirect/c316178e-7695-4808-92d8-5594eaed22ae?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/63d777a6-d499-45bf-8a05-2284bb42026d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
**Jen Psaki:**_It 's great to see you, Governor. I just want to start with this renewed trade war with Canada and how it's going to impact North Carolina... The retaliatory tariffs were announced today. What's your response to Trump restarting this tariff war with our neighbor to the north and the impact it could have on a state like North Carolina?_
_**Gov. Cooper:** Why are we fighting with Canada? Canada is North Carolina's number one foreign export country. And what we're seeing is small businesses and farmers getting killed. Pender in Wilson County, already hurt by the cost of fertilizer and equipment and having a difficult time making a profit. I was with Ann today [who runs a small business]. The tariffs are cutting into her profits, which she has very little now, and the rest of them are being passed on to consumers. We're hearing it from people. Stuff just costs too much._
_My opponent, though, Michael Whatley, is going to do and say whatever this president tells him to do and say, regardless of whether it 's good for the people of North Carolina or the people of this country. And he says that "prices are going down." He says that "we've defeated inflation." He says that "the tariffs are an important economic tool." We know that that's not true. And I think the people of North Carolina are going to see that they're not benefiting from this and, in fact, are hurting. But what he's going for here is the money to fuel his campaign._
_He knows North Carolina is close and can go either way. The Supreme Court, a month or so ago, gave them a new tool that is the worst decision since Citizens United that allows these join committed to funnel this money through and have unlimited spending, and now they 're scheming to get a discount rate on television advertising for all of it, and so his plan is to just overwhelm us. That's why we need grassroots donations, why we need help here in North Carolina to make sure we win this race and take back the Senate majority. People can go to [roycooper.com](https://substack.com/redirect/7a90fb4c-ef8f-489b-9994-433743d43920?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), see our plan to lower prices and to help us out._

But we need people to come out and vote. We're going to fight them every step of the way._

| | | | Peter, The 2001 Roadless Rule is probably the single most important forest conservation policy in modern history. It protects roughly 45 million acres of our wildest, most pristine national forests across 37 states from commercial logging and new road construction. It protects the headwaters of our drinking water, the deepest elk habitats, and the ancient forests of our backcountry. **And, to no one’s surprise, Senator Mike Lee just voted to bulldoze it all.** Under the cover of darkness, Lee attached a midnight rider to an unrelated bill to completely nullify the Roadless Rule. And because he knows exactly how unpopular this is—an overwhelming 99% of public comments oppose repealing the rule—he added a structural poison pill. His amendment legally prohibits the Forest Service from _ever_ issuing similar roadless protections in the future. He is effectively salting the earth so that no future generation can ever protect these forests again. [**We need to fight back against this ridiculous heist. Will you rush $25 to Public Land Warriors today to help us oppose the selloff of the places that make America beautiful?**](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/FekzkbUb4SvEJ6fLs6tSQw~~/AAUS1hA~/Yyqp50b2aMf083c767wa1JA6rJUxpzD3-x3AVTc2kA2g5cmxSptCbDcl5rYY-1KAYjX7o9CPJvS_4tMjOsQ4ih6E8Ff2QCv2OEAPwFEVIutJ-YZ0Bfl-VOJCjtlDQkombqvRcB16F2Ap95deb8_cFJg52QKVvMaAQ_XVdm1geYGC82h5-nxmLBY38R_SSGYKKyh7iftVUspeUxYj8NBnHBaznM7NtN0wEWcqCUZsz6uYn7uxq0xExdV6JQoFkhai) They are trying to label this as a "wildfire prevention" measure, but the data completely obliterates that claim.**It is a Trojan horse designed to let timber and extraction corporations carve up what’s left of our untouched backcountry.** Senator Lee and the politicians who voted with him think they are clever. clean_body: He's trying to backdoor us | | | | | Peter, The 2001 Roadless Rule is probably the single most important forest conservation policy in modern history. It protects roughly 45 million acres of our wildest, most pristine national forests across 37 states from commercial logging and new road construction. It protects the headwaters of our drinking water, the deepest elk habitats, and the ancient forests of our backcountry. And, to no one’s surprise, Senator Mike Lee just voted to bulldoze it all. Under the cover of darkness, Lee attached a midnight rider to an unrelated bill to completely nullify the Roadless Rule. And because he knows exactly how unpopular this is—an overwhelming 99% of public comments oppose repealing the rule—he added a structural poison pill. His amendment legally prohibits the Forest Service from ever issuing similar roadless protections in the future. He is effectively salting the earth so that no future generation can ever protect these forests again. They are trying to label this as a "wildfire prevention" measure, but the data completely obliterates that claim.It is a Trojan horse designed to let timber and extraction corporations carve up what’s left of our untouched backcountry. Senator Lee and the politicians who voted with him think they are clever. They think that by burying this raid in an unrelated bill in the middle of the night, they can avoid the anger of the hunters, anglers, hikers, and voters who actually depend on these lands. But that’s where we come in. We will expose these attacks on our public lands in the home districts of these anti-public lands politicians with the raw truth about this theft, and make sure every politician who voted to bulldoze the backcountry pays for it at the ballot box. They think they can kill 45 million acres of wilderness in the middle of the night and get away with it. Let's show them exactly what happens when the sun comes up. For the wild, Public Land Warriors | Public Land Warriors728 Gilbert StHelena, MT 59601United States "Website"

It was draped over my uncle’s casket after he died fighting the Nazis. So when I watch the socialist Left treat our flag like an old dish rag and act embarrassed by the country men like my uncle died defending, you better believe I take it personally. They can sneer at patriotism. They can badmouth America. They can act like loving this country is something we ought to be embarrassed about. But when I look at those stars and stripes, I think about generations of Americans who left their families, put on a uniform, and sacrificed everything because they believed this country was worth defending. That’s why I keep making noise in Washington, asking uncomfortable questions, and refusing to play along. It’s probably also why the socialist Left and the Washington sewer rats would be tickled pink to see me pack my bags and head back to Tennessee in November. | The Left can keep apologizing for American greatness.
