* * *
# Palestine
* **Killed and wounded in Gaza:** Over the past 24 hours, seven Palestinians were killed--five in new Israeli attacks and two due to wounds sustained in earlier attacks--and 10 were injured in attacks across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. One body was recovered from beneath the rubble.
* The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,438 killed, with 174,447 injured. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,303 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 4,336, while 814 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble.
* **Israeli strikes kill six Palestinians, wound pregnant woman:** At least one Palestinian was killed and several others wounded in an Israeli strike Wednesday on a tent sheltering displaced people in Al-Mawasi, Khan Younis, Al Jazeera reported. A pregnant woman was wounded in a separate Israeli strike on Jabalia refugee camp in northern Gaza.
* On Tuesday, Israeli forces [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/5ae757ea-9805-4878-9663-b010278ca89f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) four Palestinians and wounded others in the Jabalia refugee camp, with airstrikes hitting an area near the Abu Hussein schools. Drop Site's Mohamed Ahmed reported from the scene. One resident, whose brother was killed in the attack, told Ahmed that "Every hour there is another attack." "Whether there's a ceasefire or not, it's the same. There is no difference," he said. **Watch Ahmed 's video dispatch [here](https://substack.com/redirect/c54dd457-0774-4fd9-bfa3-ab2734d7eb90?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).**
* A separate Israeli strike on Al-Mawasi in Khan Younis killed another Palestinian.
* **Israeli attacks in occupied West Bank and East Jerusalem:**
* **Nablus:** An Israeli settler abducted two young brothers while they were traveling on the road linking Asira Al-Shamaliya to Nablus on Wednesday, WAFA reported, after stopping their truck and seizing its keys.**** Israeli settlers also [attacked](https://substack.com/redirect/e5ebd329-5eb9-4015-98c2-39196f393875?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a home in Madama on Tuesday evening, with gunshots heard in the area. Israeli lawmaker Tzvi Succot was [filmed](https://substack.com/redirect/a4f3ee80-ef2f-493d-a329-45b31e84e75f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) taking a sledgehammer to a Palestinian memorial in the same village, while Israeli soldiers and police stood guard.
* In Qusra, Israeli forces [installed](https://substack.com/redirect/e6f2bb89-e419-4e6f-929c-6d710cce4c78?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a gate on the only remaining road leading to three homes in Ras Al-Ain, south of Nablus, that have been under siege by Israeli settlers and soldiers for 18 consecutive days, WAFA reported. The other roads leading to the area have already been blocked with earth mounds, effectively isolating the three families, who are facing shortages of food and medicine.
* **Tulkarm:** Israeli forces [raided](https://substack.com/redirect/c74b7907-12f9-4b1c-8680-4e7f4cac5470?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the Shuweika suburb of Tulkarm on Tuesday, ransacked several shops, and detained two young men after assaulting them, WAFA reported.
* **Bethlehem:** On Tuesday, Israeli settlers [attacked](https://substack.com/redirect/6fc8332a-7a71-4ce2-bbba-44c6a9a801aa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a three-person AFP team covering settler attacks on Palestinians in the village of Jannatah, near Bethlehem, in violence that injured at least five people, AFP and medics said.
* **East Jerusalem:** Israeli forces shot and [wounded](https://substack.com/redirect/7282a854-8062-4839-945f-02c904ca17b9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a Palestinian child on Tuesday during an attack on the Qalandiya refugee camp, north of East Jerusalem, also [wounding](https://substack.com/redirect/be642c71-b1ee-44b9-8918-3db598f9bf59?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) several journalists, according to WAFA. Israeli authorities also [removed](https://substack.com/redirect/c70c6ea8-d836-4592-8300-3386991d04c5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) signs bearing the Arabic name "Bab Al-Amud" at Damascus Gate in occupied East Jerusalem and installed a sign reading "Old Gate." The Jerusalem Governorate said the move was part of a broader policy of replacing the city's historic Arabic place names with Hebrew names and reshaping its cultural and historical identity.
* **UN chief "greatly alarmed" as Israeli forces seize UNRWA's oldest training center: **UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres [condemned](https://substack.com/redirect/a4d9f8a0-ef31-4883-b0e5-44ad7d72397d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Tuesday the "unlawful" entry and seizure of the Qalandiya Training Center, an UNRWA vocational school in occupied East Jerusalem that has been training Palestinian refugees for more than 70 years.
* "The Secretary-General is greatly alarmed at this development, as it will deprive young people of the vocational education they were receiving," UN spokesman Stephane Dujarric said.
* Israeli officials entered the institute Wednesday and began what they described as "maintenance and renovation," as part of plans to establish an Israeli-run educational complex there.
* **Trump 's Gaza Board warns Hamas over kites as Israel continues strikes: **The Board of Peace overseeing the Gaza plan [warned](https://substack.com/redirect/161f6c62-2e86-4406-811d-2b21a8139caa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Hamas on Tuesday to halt all "militant activity," including flying kites, after Israel threatened further attacks over kites, drones or balloons, France 24 reported. The UN human rights office called Israel's threat of expulsion over children flying kites "outrageous."
* A Board official said Israel must also respect the ceasefire and restrict military action to "genuine and imminent threats"--a justification Israel has repeatedly invoked for attacks in Gaza without evidence.
* Since Hamas agreed to a second-phase plan with Trump's Board on July 30, Israel has killed 89 Palestinians in Gaza.
* **Katz visits Israeli troops illegally occupying Syria:** Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz [visited](https://substack.com/redirect/3425162b-ba51-4bce-b609-8543b8cb21f6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Israeli troops illegally occupying the summit of Mount Hermon, also known as Jabal Al-Shaykh, in southern Syria on Tuesday, pledging to keep forces there indefinitely, according to the AFP.
* Katz justified Israel's incursions and attacks, saying it sought to "thwart threats, to eliminate remnants of the old regime, [and] to prevent dangerous consolidation of the new regime."
* He also directly addressed Syria's president, Ahmed Al-Sharaa, saying, "When you wake up in the morning in your palace in Damascus, look up at Mount Hermon and see the IDF."
* Syria's Foreign Ministry noted the visit was a "flagrant violation" of its sovereignty and a breach of the 1974 disengagement agreement. It comes after two separate days of Israeli strikes near Damascus in the past week.
* **Israel expels Dutch officials from U.S.-backed Gaza center over settlement trade ban:** Israel is [expelling](https://substack.com/redirect/e162b494-5546-45c7-a4f1-ee468844e5df?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Dutch representatives from the U.S.-backed Civil-Military Coordination Center for Gaza in Kiryat Gat, Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar said, citing "a series of anti-Israel moves by the Dutch government," according to Israeli and international media.

* The Netherlands is the second country expelled from the center, which was set up under President Donald Trump's Gaza plan and is run by U.S. Central Command. Spain was removed in April.
* **Forty-one U.S. lawmakers call for the release of Palestinian-American student:** Forty-one members of Congress are demanding Secretary of State Marco Rubio secure the immediate release of Sama Safi, a 20-year-old Palestinian-American citizen and Birzeit University student held by Israel without charge since June 2.
* Lawmakers say her severe chronic illness has rapidly deteriorated in detention and doctors warn she risks "irreversible and life-threatening" organ damage.
* The letter says Safi, who suffers from Familial Mediterranean Fever, has received medication inconsistently and, since being returned to detention August 16 after a brief medical release, has reportedly received none of her daily medication or seen a doctor. "Her life is at risk on your watch," lawmakers told Rubio.
* Signatories to the letter [include](https://substack.com/redirect/a44ec06b-ccda-496f-a17c-8fe96f217d04?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Sens. **Bernie Sanders** , **Chris Van Hollen** , and **Elizabeth Warren** , and Reps. **Rashida Tlaib,** **Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez** , **Ilhan Omar** , and **Greg Casar**.

# Iran
* **Iran and Oman discuss phased Hormuz deal:** Iran and Oman announced Tuesday that they are [discussing](https://substack.com/redirect/d2b351fb-bb04-4501-a75c-3f1cf5af5578?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a phased framework to restore safe navigation through the Strait of Hormuz.
* In a joint statement after talks in Tehran between Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and Omani Foreign Minister Badr Al-Busaidi, the two sides said the proposal includes establishing a "temporary joint navigation corridor" through Hormuz and launching a "joint project to clear the Strait of mines."
* Following the talks, Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi [said](https://substack.com/redirect/414b67bf-d4b5-4009-96ad-fbb31277c50b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the sides had agreed to close the U.S.-backed southern route, and that, per the agreement, vessels entering the Persian Gulf would travel through Iranian waters, and that those exiting would use both Omani and Iranian waters. He compared the corridor to a "two-way highway."
* The agreement, once binding, would bar all military vessels from passing through, Gharibabadi said. "No military vessel will be permitted to pass through the Strait of Hormuz."
* Iran and Oman said any arrangement must preserve their sovereignty and called for consultations with other Gulf coastal states.
* Technical talks will continue on a permanent navigation corridor, the future management of the Strait, and related maritime security services. An IRGC spokesperson said Wednesday that an agreement was reached between the two countries on the share of each "in the waters of the strait" and their respective shares of its revenues, according to Tasnim.

* **China condemns latest wave of Iran sanctions:** China's Foreign Ministry [condemned](https://substack.com/redirect/cb8ab8d3-90dc-46f3-9897-38fe8b7008a5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the Trump administration's "economic D-Day" against Iran, saying Beijing "firmly opposes" sanctions that "have no basis in international law."
* "Economic warfare and maximum pressure provide no solution," the ministry said, warning they will fuel tensions, disrupt the global economic and financial order, and "hurt everyone else's interests."

* **Regional oil exports plunge, with Saudi and Iranian exports first among losers:** Saudi and Iranian oil exports [collapsed](https://substack.com/redirect/afade488-df08-4f7d-9934-40a0a7d2ed36?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in August, while the UAE and Iraq captured some of the displaced Gulf trade, Kpler data released on Tuesday indicates.
* Saudi exports fell to 1.93 million barrels per day (bpd) in August, down 2.68 million from July and 3.74 million from last August.
* Iran shipped only 277,000 bpd, falling by 616,000 month-over-month.
* Meanwhile, UAE exports rose by 631,000 bpd month-over-month to 3.58 million, while Iraq gained 699,000 bpd to reach 2.15 million.
* Iraq, which gained from the displacement, has still [exported](https://substack.com/redirect/2bc752b2-ba51-40ce-ab1c-019758ce596b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) nearly half of what it shipped before the war, according to State Oil Marketing Organization figures obtained by Rudaw, with an average of 54 million barrels per month exported at present to 106 million barrels per month sold overseas previously.
* **Iraq loads largest single-day oil shipment:** Iraq [loaded](https://substack.com/redirect/6203aa56-1ab0-47c9-aaf1-57be4538f595?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) nearly 11 million barrels of crude onto seven tankers at Basra on Tuesday, marking its largest single-day surge in export activity in three months, according to Kpler data.
* The surge follows Iran's decision Saturday to grant several Iraqi oil tankers special permission to pass through the Strait of Hormuz after repeated requests from Baghdad, Reuters reported.

* **Iran says U.S. minesweepers would be "very good targets":** Iran's deputy foreign minister for legal and international affairs, Kazem Gharibabadi, warned that U.S. mine-detection vessels would become "very good targets" if they entered the region, according to remarks reported by The New Arab.
* He dismissed President Trump's comments on demining as "only aimed at calming the markets."
* Gharibabadi also [said](https://substack.com/redirect/13b3feb8-4f84-4289-b9fb-553fbda5d40e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that Tehran still considers itself at war and warned it could take preemptive action against the U.S., but would change its posture if the U.S. adhered to the terms of the Islamabad memorandum of understanding.

* **Iran slams U.S. sanctions as global coercion:** Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei [condemned](https://substack.com/redirect/bc859932-4566-493d-a78f-e871f9856df3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the latest U.S. sanctions on Iran, part of a campaign U.S. officials have called an "economic D-Day," in a post on X on Tuesday.
* "When a bully declares that every bank, company, port, and government must choose between obeying Washington's whims or facing American vengeance, this is no longer just about Iran," he wrote.

# U.S. News
* **Meta agrees to up to $17.1 billion settlement with 47 states over child safety claims** : Meta [reached](https://substack.com/redirect/c2b60082-3201-46d8-9298-473ca997aa34?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a landmark settlement Wednesday with 47 states, the District of Columbia, and U.S. territories, agreeing to pay up to $17.1 billion in penalties and impose major product changes after it had been accused of endangering children with addiction to its social media platforms.
* The product changes for users under 18 include two-hour daily time limits on Instagram and Facebook, notification blackouts between 10 p.m. and 7 a.m., and restrictions on features like beauty filters and "like" counters linked to negative social comparison.
* The agreement follows a suit filed by four states in the U.S. Northern District of California, in which the plaintiffs sought roughly $200 billion.
* **Tuesday 's primary results:**
* **Darline Graham** won Tuesday's Republican Senate runoff in South Carolina, CBS News projects, defeating Rep. **Ralph Norman** to secure the party's nomination for a full six-year term following the death of her brother, longtime Sen. **Lindsey Graham** , last month. Graham, appointed by Gov. **Henry McMaster** to serve out her brother's current term, will now face Democratic nominee Dr. **Annie Andrews** in November.
* Former Gwinnett County School Board Chairman **Everton Blair** won Tuesday's runoff election to serve the remainder of the late Rep. **David Scott 's** term in Georgia's 13th District, defeating Scott's daughter, **Marcye Scott**. Blair, who campaigned on progressive policies including a tax on households earning over $50 million, "Medicare for All," and universal childcare, will serve only a short term, as State Rep. **Jasmine Clark** , who did not run in the special election, is the heavy favorite to win the regularly scheduled November election for the deep-blue Atlanta-area seat; Blair had run against Clark in that separate primary and lost.
* **Second "Dan Sullivan" advances to Alaska Senate ballot: **Former teacher **Dan J. Sullivan** will [appear](https://substack.com/redirect/c8f127cb-e675-4abb-9ba8-e5c0bf00426f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) alongside Republican Sen. **Dan Sullivan** and Democratic challenger **Mary Peltola** on Alaska's general election Senate ballot.
* Alaska's elections are ranked choice, with the top four candidates advancing regardless of party in the primary. While voters could rank both Sullivans in the general, which is also ranked choice, some may rank only one, a dynamic that could matter in what's expected to be one of the closest Senate races in the country this year.
* State and federal prosecutors are investigating whether the second Sullivan's candidacy is part of a coordinated effort to sow confusion, with a grand jury issuing subpoenas last week related to his campaign.
* **Canada announces up to 50% retaliatory tariffs on American goods** : Canada announced retaliatory tariffs of up to 50% on about 700 American products Tuesday, set to take effect September 8, following the collapse of trade talks and new U.S. tariffs.
* The measures, covering roughly $20 billion in annual U.S. imports to match the value of Canadian exports hit by American tariffs, include a doubling of tariffs on U.S. steel and aluminum to 50%, and levies on appliances like dishwashers and stoves. Canada also announced it would maintain its 25% tariffs on American-made cars.
* **M elanie Joly**, Canada's industry minister, said that some of the items on the tariff list were chosen to target states that voted for Trump.
* **ICE arrests hit record 49,571 in July:** U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement [arrested](https://substack.com/redirect/f75e2529-814a-4b57-b681-6fc7a5de8f80?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 49,571 people in July, the highest monthly total of Trump's second term and a 15% jump from June, according to data obtained through a Freedom of Information Act lawsuit by the Deportation Data Project and analyzed by the Associated Press.
* The surge, which follows a February dip after fatal shootings in Minnesota sparked public backlash, has come through less visible tactics including traffic stops and expanded 287(g) partnerships with state and local police.
* Data shows more than half of those arrested in July had no criminal convictions or pending charges. It also shows that more than half were "non-custodial," meaning that ICE arrested people in the community rather than people already in prison or held by local police.
* **Rogers attends spate of AIPAC fundraisers in L.A.:** Michigan Republican Senate nominee **Mike Rogers** [attended](https://substack.com/redirect/d049a9a4-4053-40dd-8dee-274c4ea4b569?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) four AIPAC-hosted fundraisers in Los Angeles on Sunday and Monday, according to the Detroit News.
* At the fundraisers, Rogers reportedly conveyed "significant" reservations to AIPAC board chair Michael Tuchin about the pro-Israel group's planned ad campaign against Democratic nominee **Abdul El-Sayed** , fearing it could galvanize El-Sayed's supporters.
* AIPAC's super PAC, United Democracy Project, spent $32 million trying to defeat El-Sayed in his primary against **Haley Stevens**.
* UDP spokesman **Patrick Dorton** said the group'' board has not yet decided how it will help Rogers but remains "unequivocal in its goal of defeating Abdul El-Sayed."
* **Pro-Israel Democrats win key posts on House Foreign Affairs Committee:** Three vocally pro-Israel House Democrats--Reps. **Jared Moskowitz**(Fla.), **Debbie Wasserman Schultz**(Fla.), and **Wesley Bell**(Mo.)--were [appointed](https://substack.com/redirect/7b6570ac-7fce-4e42-95ca-65b926b9b1aa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to the House Foreign Affairs Committee Tuesday.
* Moskowitz will lead Democrats on the subcommittee overseeing U.S.-Middle East policy, with the congressman noting that if Democrats retake the House, he would be positioned to "help steer U.S. policy on Israel and the Middle East" as the subcommittee's chair.
* All three appointees defeated left-wing primary challengers who had targeted their stances on Israel this election cycle.
* Progressive Rep. **Mark Pocan** (Wisc.) was also appointed to the subcommittee.
* **CIA director John Ratcliffe visited Moscow, holds talks with Russian intelligence officials:** Central Intelligence Agency Director **John Ratcliffe** [traveled](https://substack.com/redirect/2323d813-c71e-4b68-a424-79b27c8e3693?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to Moscow on Tuesday for talks with Russian intelligence officials, with officials from the Kremlin acknowledging the meetings.
* Ahead of the visit, Washington reportedly asked Kyiv to pause strikes on Ukraine until the American delegation departed Russia.
* The trip, Ratcliffe's first known visit to Moscow as CIA director, followed the sighting of a U.S. Air Force C-17 transport plane and a diplomatic motorcade in the Russian capital, and comes as U.S.-mediated peace talks between Ukraine and Russia remain largely stalled.

# Other International News
* **Ukrainian drones destroy Wildberries warehouse, strike Russian oil refinery:** Ukrainian long-range drones [struck](https://substack.com/redirect/62827799-30b0-4c04-af4e-499d6cd09718?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a Wildberries warehouse in Russia's Tambov region on Wednesday, hitting the facility for the second time in five weeks and burning it to the ground. Two people were injured in the attack.
* Ukraine's General Staff also announced that a drone hit a Lukoil refinery in Russia's Nizhny Novgorod region overnight. The facility, which has a processing capacity of about 125 million barrels annually, remained on fire after the attack.
* Separately, Russia struck a residential building in northern Ukraine's Chernihiv, killing a woman and a 4-year-old child, and a house in Lipetsk, killing two more.
* **Tinubu orders rescue operation after possible mass kidnapping of 600 in Nigeria** : Nigerian President Bola Tinubu [ordered](https://substack.com/redirect/70c16a1e-b5db-4b8b-bdbc-5e738cafdbcd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) security agencies to launch an immediate rescue operation Tuesday after an armed group allegedly kidnapped about 600 women, children, and elderly people during an attack on a mosque in Niger State, according to a video posted by the group and cited by residents. A district official said 30 people were killed in the attacks. At least 2,000 people fled into neighboring Benin, according to a tribal official.
* **Nepal flash flood kills at least 95, hundreds missing** : A massive flash flood [swept away](https://substack.com/redirect/f5f820bd-2461-49a5-8d4d-301aa08e62ed?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) villages in Nepal's mountainous Rasuwa district near the Tibet border Wednesday, killing at least 95 people and leaving hundreds missing, including 384 tourists and eight South Korean employees at a hydropower project.
* Across the border in Tibet's Gyirong county, a mudslide caused "major casualties" and cut off roads, communications, and power, prompting Chinese President Xi Jinping to call for "all-out" search efforts.
* **At least 14 infants killed in Islamabad hospital fire** : At least 14 infants were killed when a fire broke out in the mother and child health ward of Pakistan's state-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences in Islamabad Wednesday, the Associated Press [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/d3425d87-9229-449a-9f30-6c76dbc0c313?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
* Health Minister Mustafa Kamal attributed the blaze to an air conditioner explosion that spread quickly amid ample oxygen in the ward.
* Grieving parents claimed that the ward lacked proper fire exits, that doctors and nurses were absent at the time of the fire, and that bodies were removed "in boxes" without allowing families to view them.
* Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif suspended his health secretary and ordered an investigation into the incident.
* **Ethnic attacks in South Kordofan kill 27 civilians, including 4 children:** Attacks in Sudan's South Kordofan [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/3fc375c1-4c3f-41f2-b7f7-f88a9ef2f11b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at least 27 civilians, including four children, a Sudanese medical group said Tuesday, in the latest bloodshed from an ethnic conflict layered on top of the country's civil war.
* The killings were carried out by the rebel Sudan People's Liberation Movement-North (SPLM-N) in Qardud and Abu Hamama, areas home to the Otoro tribe, a minority in the Nuba Mountains, according to the Sudan Doctors Network, which tracks casualties nationwide.
* Separately, the SPLM-N [claimed](https://substack.com/redirect/cf8d0bd0-8981-4926-b003-2dd3d55df536?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that it re-established control over its regional stronghold of Kauda on Wednesday, releasing footage showing its forces entering civil administration offices in the city.
* **Kurdish-led SDF dissolves, folding fighters into Syria 's army: **The Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/a2075ab1-058f-46f1-80d4-3637b08b8503?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) its dissolution as an independent military force, completing its merger into the Syrian state, commander Mazloum Abdi said in a televised speech from the presidential palace in Damascus, Rudaw reported.
* "We announce today the end of the mission of the Syrian Democratic Forces and announce with full responsibility its dissolution as an independent military force," Abdi said.
* The U.S.-backed SDF, which spearheaded the fight against the Islamic State and once controlled an autonomous zone in Syria's northeast, agreed to integrate in January after losing most of its territory in a government offensive led by President Ahmed al-Sharaa.
* U.S. envoy Tom Barrack praised the outcome, crediting Trump's "leadership." The core Kurdish YPG had already been folded into state forces, with its commander named deputy defense minister for eastern Syria in March.
* **Sikh separatist leader warned of new credible death threat by FBI, Canadian police:** Sikh separatist leader Gurpatwant Singh Pannun [said](https://substack.com/redirect/ab2a24b5-d6f0-40cf-bb41-cee877029954?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Tuesday that FBI agents visited him August 12 to warn him of a new credible threat to his life and advise against travel, followed by a Tuesday phone warning from the Royal Canadian Mounted Police, though neither agency disclosed details of the plot.
* Pannun, who is considered a terrorist by India for advocating a separate Sikh state, said he remains "unfazed and undaunted."
* The warnings, issued under a U.S. "Duty to Warn" law requiring notification of credible murder threats, come as Nikhil Gupta, an Indian national who pleaded guilty to conspiring in a 2023 plot to assassinate Pannun after being directed by an Indian government employee to do so, awaits a November sentencing in Manhattan federal court.

This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Palestine Killed and wounded in Gaza: Over the past 24 hours, seven Palestinians were killed--five in new Israeli attacks and two due to wounds sustained in earlier attacks--and 10 were injured in attacks across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. One body was recovered from beneath the rubble. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,438 killed, with 174,447 injured. A pregnant woman was wounded in a separate Israeli strike on Jabalia refugee camp in northern Gaza. On Tuesday, Israeli forces four Palestinians and wounded others in the Jabalia refugee camp, with airstrikes hitting an area near the Abu Hussein schools. Drop Site's Mohamed Ahmed reported from the scene. One resident, whose brother was killed in the attack, told Ahmed that "Every hour there is another attack." "Whether there's a ceasefire or not, it's the same. There is no difference," he said. Watch Ahmed 's video dispatch . A separate Israeli strike on Al-Mawasi in Khan Younis killed another Palestinian. Israeli attacks in occupied West Bank and East Jerusalem: Nablus: An Israeli settler abducted two young brothers while they were traveling on the road linking Asira Al-Shamaliya to Nablus on Wednesday, WAFA reported, after stopping their truck and seizing its keys.** Israeli settlers also a home in Madama on Tuesday evening, with gunshots heard in the area. Israeli lawmaker Tzvi Succot was taking a sledgehammer to a Palestinian memorial in the same village, while Israeli soldiers and police stood guard. In Qusra, Israeli forces a gate on the only remaining road leading to three homes in Ras Al-Ain, south of Nablus, that have been under siege by Israeli settlers and soldiers for 18 consecutive days, WAFA reported. The other roads leading to the area have already been blocked with earth mounds, effectively isolating the three families, who are facing shortages of food and medicine. Tulkarm: Israeli forces the Shuweika suburb of Tulkarm on Tuesday, ransacked several shops, and detained two young men after assaulting them, WAFA reported. Bethlehem: On Tuesday, Israeli settlers a three-person AFP team covering settler attacks on Palestinians in the village of Jannatah, near Bethlehem, in violence that injured at least five people, AFP and medics said. East Jerusalem: Israeli forces shot and a Palestinian child on Tuesday during an attack on the Qalandiya refugee camp, north of East Jerusalem, also several journalists, according to WAFA. Israeli authorities also signs bearing the Arabic name "Bab Al-Amud" at Damascus Gate in occupied East Jerusalem and installed a sign reading "Old Gate." The Jerusalem Governorate said the move was part of a broader policy of replacing the city's historic Arabic place names with Hebrew names and reshaping its cultural and historical identity. UN chief "greatly alarmed" as Israeli forces seize UNRWA's oldest training center: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres on Tuesday the "unlawful" entry and seizure of the Qalandiya Training Center, an UNRWA vocational school in occupied East Jerusalem that has been training Palestinian refugees for more than 70 years. "The Secretary-General is greatly alarmed at this development, as it will deprive young people of the vocational education they were receiving," UN spokesman Stephane Dujarric said. Israeli officials entered the institute Wednesday and began what they described as "maintenance and renovation," as part of plans to establish an Israeli-run educational complex there. Trump 's Gaza Board warns Hamas over kites as Israel continues strikes: The Board of Peace overseeing the Gaza plan Hamas on Tuesday to halt all "militant activity," including flying kites, after Israel threatened further attacks over kites, drones or balloons, France 24 reported. The UN human rights office called Israel's threat of expulsion over children flying kites "outrageous." A Board official said Israel must also respect the ceasefire and restrict military action to "genuine and imminent threats"--a justification Israel has repeatedly invoked for attacks in Gaza without evidence. Since Hamas agreed to a second-phase plan with Trump's Board on July 30, Israel has killed 89 Palestinians in Gaza. Katz visits Israeli troops illegally occupying Syria: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz Israeli troops illegally occupying the summit of Mount Hermon, also known as Jabal Al-Shaykh, in southern Syria on Tuesday, pledging to keep forces there indefinitely, according to the AFP. Katz justified Israel's incursions and attacks, saying it sought to "thwart threats, to eliminate remnants of the old regime, [and] to prevent dangerous consolidation of the new regime." He also directly addressed Syria's president, Ahmed Al-Sharaa, saying, "When you wake up in the morning in your palace in Damascus, look up at Mount Hermon and see the IDF." Syria's Foreign Ministry noted the visit was a "flagrant violation" of its sovereignty and a breach of the 1974 disengagement agreement. It comes after two separate days of Israeli strikes near Damascus in the past week. Israel expels Dutch officials from U.S.-backed Gaza center over settlement trade ban: Israel is Dutch representatives from the U.S.-backed Civil-Military Coordination Center for Gaza in Kiryat Gat, Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar said, citing "a series of anti-Israel moves by the Dutch government," according to Israeli and international media. In explaining the expulsion, Sa'ar pointed to a Dutch law that bans trade in Israeli products from the illegally occupied West Bank, East Jerusalem, and the Golan Heights, which is set to take effect on September 22. The representatives were given one week to leave. The Netherlands is the second country expelled from the center, which was set up under President Donald Trump's Gaza plan and is run by U.S. Central Command. Spain was removed in April. Forty-one U.S. lawmakers call for the release of Palestinian-American student: Forty-one members of Congress are demanding Secretary of State Marco Rubio secure the immediate release of Sama Safi, a 20-year-old Palestinian-American citizen and Birzeit University student held by Israel without charge since June 2. Lawmakers say her severe chronic illness has rapidly deteriorated in detention and doctors warn she risks "irreversible and life-threatening" organ damage. The letter says Safi, who suffers from Familial Mediterranean Fever, has received medication inconsistently and, since being returned to detention August 16 after a brief medical release, has reportedly received none of her daily medication or seen a doctor. "Her life is at risk on your watch," lawmakers told Rubio. Signatories to the letter Sens. Bernie Sanders , Chris Van Hollen , and Elizabeth Warren , and Reps. Rashida Tlaib, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez , Ilhan Omar , and Greg Casar. Iran Iran and Oman discuss phased Hormuz deal: Iran and Oman announced Tuesday that they are a phased framework to restore safe navigation through the Strait of Hormuz. In a joint statement after talks in Tehran between Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and Omani Foreign Minister Badr Al-Busaidi, the two sides said the proposal includes establishing a "temporary joint navigation corridor" through Hormuz and launching a "joint project to clear the Strait of mines." Following the talks, Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi the sides had agreed to close the U.S.-backed southern route, and that, per the agreement, vessels entering the Persian Gulf would travel through Iranian waters, and that those exiting would use both Omani and Iranian waters. He compared the corridor to a "two-way highway." The agreement, once binding, would bar all military vessels from passing through, Gharibabadi said. "No military vessel will be permitted to pass through the Strait of Hormuz." Iran and Oman said any arrangement must preserve their sovereignty and called for consultations with other Gulf coastal states. Technical talks will continue on a permanent navigation corridor, the future management of the Strait, and related maritime security services. An IRGC spokesperson said Wednesday that an agreement was reached between the two countries on the share of each "in the waters of the strait" and their respective shares of its revenues, according to Tasnim. China condemns latest wave of Iran sanctions: China's Foreign Ministry the Trump administration's "economic D-Day" against Iran, saying Beijing "firmly opposes" sanctions that "have no basis in international law." "Economic warfare and maximum pressure provide no solution," the ministry said, warning they will fuel tensions, disrupt the global economic and financial order, and "hurt everyone else's interests." Regional oil exports plunge, with Saudi and Iranian exports first among losers: Saudi and Iranian oil exports in August, while the UAE and Iraq captured some of the displaced Gulf trade, Kpler data released on Tuesday indicates. Saudi exports fell to 1.93 million barrels per day (bpd) in August, down 2.68 million from July and 3.74 million from last August. Iran shipped only 277,000 bpd, falling by 616,000 month-over-month. Meanwhile, UAE exports rose by 631,000 bpd month-over-month to 3.58 million, while Iraq gained 699,000 bpd to reach 2.15 million. Iraq, which gained from the displacement, has still nearly half of what it shipped before the war, according to State Oil Marketing Organization figures obtained by Rudaw, with an average of 54 million barrels per month exported at present to 106 million barrels per month sold overseas previously. Iraq loads largest single-day oil shipment: Iraq nearly 11 million barrels of crude onto seven tankers at Basra on Tuesday, marking its largest single-day surge in export activity in three months, according to Kpler data. The surge follows Iran's decision Saturday to grant several Iraqi oil tankers special permission to pass through the Strait of Hormuz after repeated requests from Baghdad, Reuters reported. Iran says U.S. minesweepers would be "very good targets": Iran's deputy foreign minister for legal and international affairs, Kazem Gharibabadi, warned that U.S. mine-detection vessels would become "very good targets" if they entered the region, according to remarks reported by The New Arab. He dismissed President Trump's comments on demining as "only aimed at calming the markets." Gharibabadi also that Tehran still considers itself at war and warned it could take preemptive action against the U.S., but would change its posture if the U.S. adhered to the terms of the Islamabad memorandum of understanding. Iran slams U.S. sanctions as global coercion: Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei the latest U.S. sanctions on Iran, part of a campaign U.S. officials have called an "economic D-Day," in a post on X on Tuesday. "When a bully declares that every bank, company, port, and government must choose between obeying Washington's whims or facing American vengeance, this is no longer just about Iran," he wrote. Lebanon Israel continues assault on southern Lebanon despite "ceasefire": Israeli forces heavily along the Litani River in the Marjayoun district on Wednesday, Lebanon's National News Agency reported. An Israeli Apache helicopter also flew over the area and conducted a sweep above the same section of the river that had been shelled. In the Tyre (Sour) district, Israeli forces a large demolition in Buyout Al-Sayyad, opposite Mansouri. On Tuesday, Israeli warplanes a wave of airstrikes across southern Lebanon, hitting the village of Dohat Kfar Roummane, the nearby village of Dabsha, and the important Ali Al-Taher hills outside Nabatieh. Strikes also targeted Al-Qantara and the outskirts of Srebbine in the Bint Jbeil district, Lebanon's Al-Nahar reported. Journalist Courtney Bonneau artillery fire on 11 towns and areas, airstrikes on six, home demolitions in ten and machine-gun fire in three. U.S. News Meta agrees to up to $17.1 billion settlement with 47 states over child safety claims : Meta a landmark settlement Wednesday with 47 states, the District of Columbia, and U.S. territories, agreeing to pay up to $17.1 billion in penalties and impose major product changes after it had been accused of endangering children with addiction to its social media platforms. The product changes for users under 18 include two-hour daily time limits on Instagram and Facebook, notification blackouts between 10 p.m. and 7 a.m., and restrictions on features like beauty filters and "like" counters linked to negative social comparison. The agreement follows a suit filed by four states in the U.S. Northern District of California, in which the plaintiffs sought roughly $200 billion. Tuesday 's primary results: Darline Graham won Tuesday's Republican Senate runoff in South Carolina, CBS News projects, defeating Rep. Ralph Norman to secure the party's nomination for a full six-year term following the death of her brother, longtime Sen. Lindsey Graham , last month. Graham, appointed by Gov. Henry McMaster to serve out her brother's current term, will now face Democratic nominee Dr. Annie Andrews in November. Former Gwinnett County School Board Chairman Everton Blair won Tuesday's runoff election to serve the remainder of the late Rep. David Scott 's term in Georgia's 13th District, defeating Scott's daughter, Marcye Scott. Blair, who campaigned on progressive policies including a tax on households earning over $50 million, "Medicare for All," and universal childcare, will serve only a short term, as State Rep. Jasmine Clark , who did not run in the special election, is the heavy favorite to win the regularly scheduled November election for the deep-blue Atlanta-area seat; Blair had run against Clark in that separate primary and lost. Second "Dan Sullivan" advances to Alaska Senate ballot: Former teacher Dan J. Sullivan will alongside Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan and Democratic challenger Mary Peltola on Alaska's general election Senate ballot. Alaska's elections are ranked choice, with the top four candidates advancing regardless of party in the primary. While voters could rank both Sullivans in the general, which is also ranked choice, some may rank only one, a dynamic that could matter in what's expected to be one of the closest Senate races in the country this year. State and federal prosecutors are investigating whether the second Sullivan's candidacy is part of a coordinated effort to sow confusion, with a grand jury issuing subpoenas last week related to his campaign. Canada announces up to 50% retaliatory tariffs on American goods : Canada announced retaliatory tariffs of up to 50% on about 700 American products Tuesday, set to take effect September 8, following the collapse of trade talks and new U.S. tariffs. The measures, covering roughly $20 billion in annual U.S. imports to match the value of Canadian exports hit by American tariffs, include a doubling of tariffs on U.S. steel and aluminum to 50%, and levies on appliances like dishwashers and stoves. Canada also announced it would maintain its 25% tariffs on American-made cars. M elanie Joly, Canada's industry minister, said that some of the items on the tariff list were chosen to target states that voted for Trump. ICE arrests hit record 49,571 in July: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement 49,571 people in July, the highest monthly total of Trump's second term and a 15% jump from June, according to data obtained through a Freedom of Information Act lawsuit by the Deportation Data Project and analyzed by the Associated Press. The surge, which follows a February dip after fatal shootings in Minnesota sparked public backlash, has come through less visible tactics including traffic stops and expanded 287(g) partnerships with state and local police. Data shows more than half of those arrested in July had no criminal convictions or pending charges. It also shows that more than half were "non-custodial," meaning that ICE arrested people in the community rather than people already in prison or held by local police. Rogers attends spate of AIPAC fundraisers in L.A.: Michigan Republican Senate nominee Mike Rogers four AIPAC-hosted fundraisers in Los Angeles on Sunday and Monday, according to the Detroit News. At the fundraisers, Rogers reportedly conveyed "significant" reservations to AIPAC board chair Michael Tuchin about the pro-Israel group's planned ad campaign against Democratic nominee Abdul El-Sayed , fearing it could galvanize El-Sayed's supporters. AIPAC's super PAC, United Democracy Project, spent $32 million trying to defeat El-Sayed in his primary against Haley Stevens. UDP spokesman Patrick Dorton said the group'' board has not yet decided how it will help Rogers but remains "unequivocal in its goal of defeating Abdul El-Sayed." Pro-Israel Democrats win key posts on House Foreign Affairs Committee: Three vocally pro-Israel House Democrats--Reps. Jared Moskowitz(Fla.), Debbie Wasserman Schultz(Fla.), and Wesley Bell(Mo.)--were to the House Foreign Affairs Committee Tuesday. Moskowitz will lead Democrats on the subcommittee overseeing U.S.-Middle East policy, with the congressman noting that if Democrats retake the House, he would be positioned to "help steer U.S. policy on Israel and the Middle East" as the subcommittee's chair. All three appointees defeated left-wing primary challengers who had targeted their stances on Israel this election cycle. Progressive Rep. Mark Pocan (Wisc.) was also appointed to the subcommittee. CIA director John Ratcliffe visited Moscow, holds talks with Russian intelligence officials: Central Intelligence Agency Director John Ratcliffe to Moscow on Tuesday for talks with Russian intelligence officials, with officials from the Kremlin acknowledging the meetings. Ahead of the visit, Washington reportedly asked Kyiv to pause strikes on Ukraine until the American delegation departed Russia. The trip, Ratcliffe's first known visit to Moscow as CIA director, followed the sighting of a U.S. Air Force C-17 transport plane and a diplomatic motorcade in the Russian capital, and comes as U.S.-mediated peace talks between Ukraine and Russia remain largely stalled. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News Ukrainian drones destroy Wildberries warehouse, strike Russian oil refinery: Ukrainian long-range drones a Wildberries warehouse in Russia's Tambov region on Wednesday, hitting the facility for the second time in five weeks and burning it to the ground. Two people were injured in the attack. Ukraine's General Staff also announced that a drone hit a Lukoil refinery in Russia's Nizhny Novgorod region overnight. The facility, which has a processing capacity of about 125 million barrels annually, remained on fire after the attack. Separately, Russia struck a residential building in northern Ukraine's Chernihiv, killing a woman and a 4-year-old child, and a house in Lipetsk, killing two more. Tinubu orders rescue operation after possible mass kidnapping of 600 in Nigeria : Nigerian President Bola Tinubu security agencies to launch an immediate rescue operation Tuesday after an armed group allegedly kidnapped about 600 women, children, and elderly people during an attack on a mosque in Niger State, according to a video posted by the group and cited by residents. A district official said 30 people were killed in the attacks. At least 2,000 people fled into neighboring Benin, according to a tribal official. Nepal flash flood kills at least 95, hundreds missing : A massive flash flood villages in Nepal's mountainous Rasuwa district near the Tibet border Wednesday, killing at least 95 people and leaving hundreds missing, including 384 tourists and eight South Korean employees at a hydropower project. Across the border in Tibet's Gyirong county, a mudslide caused "major casualties" and cut off roads, communications, and power, prompting Chinese President Xi Jinping to call for "all-out" search efforts. At least 14 infants killed in Islamabad hospital fire : At least 14 infants were killed when a fire broke out in the mother and child health ward of Pakistan's state-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences in Islamabad Wednesday, the Associated Press . Health Minister Mustafa Kamal attributed the blaze to an air conditioner explosion that spread quickly amid ample oxygen in the ward. Grieving parents claimed that the ward lacked proper fire exits, that doctors and nurses were absent at the time of the fire, and that bodies were removed "in boxes" without allowing families to view them. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif suspended his health secretary and ordered an investigation into the incident. Ethnic attacks in South Kordofan kill 27 civilians, including 4 children: Attacks in Sudan's South Kordofan at least 27 civilians, including four children, a Sudanese medical group said Tuesday, in the latest bloodshed from an ethnic conflict layered on top of the country's civil war. The killings were carried out by the rebel Sudan People's Liberation Movement-North (SPLM-N) in Qardud and Abu Hamama, areas home to the Otoro tribe, a minority in the Nuba Mountains, according to the Sudan Doctors Network, which tracks casualties nationwide. Separately, the SPLM-N that it re-established control over its regional stronghold of Kauda on Wednesday, releasing footage showing its forces entering civil administration offices in the city. Kurdish-led SDF dissolves, folding fighters into Syria 's army: The Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces its dissolution as an independent military force, completing its merger into the Syrian state, commander Mazloum Abdi said in a televised speech from the presidential palace in Damascus, Rudaw reported. "We announce today the end of the mission of the Syrian Democratic Forces and announce with full responsibility its dissolution as an independent military force," Abdi said. The U.S.-backed SDF, which spearheaded the fight against the Islamic State and once controlled an autonomous zone in Syria's northeast, agreed to integrate in January after losing most of its territory in a government offensive led by President Ahmed al-Sharaa. U.S. envoy Tom Barrack praised the outcome, crediting Trump's "leadership." The core Kurdish YPG had already been folded into state forces, with its commander named deputy defense minister for eastern Syria in March. Sikh separatist leader warned of new credible death threat by FBI, Canadian police: Sikh separatist leader Gurpatwant Singh Pannun Tuesday that FBI agents visited him August 12 to warn him of a new credible threat to his life and advise against travel, followed by a Tuesday phone warning from the Royal Canadian Mounted Police, though neither agency disclosed details of the plot. body:
# [](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/43706?t=1&akid=241035%2E444211%2Erabe5q)
These next few months are going to decide the outcome of November’s elections and the balance of power in our country. As we ramp up our engagement on campuses, at political rallies and other places young people will be gathering in order to help turn their energy and emotion into action and votes, I want to take a minute to describe the path that brought us here.
A year ago, Powered by People led in Texas and across the country to bring attention and resources to the fight against Trump’s attempt to steal 5 Congressional seats. We rallied public support behind the Democratic legislators who left the state to successfully deny Republicans the quorum they needed in their first special session, and while ultimately Abbott rigged the new maps, we were able to push Democrats across the country to respond.
That meant that California stepped up to meet Texas’ five new gerrymandered districts by redrawing five of their own. And it meant that we could draw in national support to help Texas Democrats fight to win in the new districts.
While we were successful, it came at significant cost. The Texas Attorney General tried to jail me, sued me personally and sought to put Powered by People out of business, all for fighting for our right to free and fair elections. While it cost us more than $500,000 to defend ourselves (so far), we have won at both the district and appeals courts and have proven that you don’t have to bend the knee to the thugs in power.
In fact, as Paxton issued his threats and lawsuits, we traveled the state, helped host organizing rallies, and personally called prospective candidates to get a Democrat to run in every single State House, State Senate and U.S. Congressional seat in Texas for the first time in 50 years. That means a fighter on every front in every part of the state.
At the beginning of 2026, we worked a special election in Tarrant County that had outsized implications for the country — helping Taylor Rehmet defeat his Republican opponent for State Senate by 17 points, contributing to a 31-point swing in what was thought to be a reliably Trump district.
We also partnered with the Texas Democratic Party to ensure that voting by mail — under heavy attack by Trump and Republicans — could be used by Democrats who were unlikely to vote without this important tool.
We had our most successful college organizing effort of the year over the spring semester, meeting tens of thousands of college students in person, helping them to get registered, to stay in touch with them and ensure they turn out to vote.

Peter,

Early in my career, Bernie Sanders gave me a piece of advice I've never
forgotten.

He told me people succeed in politics one of two ways: either by getting
really good at lying, or really good at telling the truth. I clearly
wasn't cut out for the first one, he said. So my job was to get really
good at the second.

That’s why today, I want to tell you three truths about our race:

1. This is still anybody’s seat to win. Poll after poll shows it. The
Cook Political Report rates Michigan a toss-up. We can’t get
comfortable even for a second.
2. By Election Day, dark money groups and GOP Super PACs will have spent
$121 million trying to beat us. That’s not a typo. Mike Rogers and his
MAGA billionaire backers will spend whatever it takes to try to tear
down everything we’ve built.
3. This race could decide who controls the U.S. Senate majority. If we
lose here, the path for Democrats to take back the majority is
virtually gone. This isn't just Michigan’s fight.

This is, no exaggeration, a make-or-break moment for our campaign. The
grassroots support we generate right now determines how much coverage
we’ll get over the airwaves and on the ground when Michiganders begin
voting later this fall.

That’s why earning your support today is so crucial.

Abdul

subject: This is bigger than one election
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY TURNING POINT ACTION (TPACTION
body:
At this point, it’s not about winning anybody over. It's about who actually shows up.

| | | |
---
Friend,
---
We've looked at the polling in every swing state and swing race in the country. It's margin of error, either way, almost everywhere.

At this point, it's not about winning anybody over. _It's about who actually shows up._

If conservatives turn out in November, we'll win every critical battleground and lay the groundwork for victory in 2028 and beyond.

That's why Turning Point Action is focusing all our efforts on three key states: Arizona, Nevada, and New Hampshire.

**We call these states the new RED WALL.**

_Let me explain why they matter so much... _

After 2024, Charlie looked at the numbers, looked at the maps, and told our team something simple. If we lock down Arizona, Nevada, and New Hampshire, the Left's entire strategy falls apart. Their map collapses. Their path back to power disappears.

Here's why... Winning the presidency comes down to 270 electoral votes. Lose Arizona and most of the realistic paths to the White House in 2028 are gone. Lose Nevada and New Hampshire and the Left rebuilds the Blue Wall they lost in 2024.

Whoever wins in 2028 controls the 2030 Census. The Census drives redistricting. Redistricting sets the congressional map for the next ten years.

This midterm decides which way that goes.
---
[](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckTuO3DAMhk8jdx7oZUkuXAQYuNsUQYCUAi1RtrB-RaIn1w-8mROk5Ud-IPn_-vAfkNe8z99hw6FQ8qV6WnLNdcrzjIUW2I8dccVA2UsuTctdK42HQPmFXkMThxgiiNDgIKyz1nAuZbMMznbKaBVMTGCscFqL5HgvjZGiQ66bPNw-7qQRhnNhH9ymlJTpEp-0ADExzWHFQo-C5zWtOcBOUD_TUQI-wrE167AQnZWpb0yOTI4Vw1XwATvGg-4OJkc671WPncmx0xO6NOl2mjrZao7Y9tGpNmHQqsdeCdszNdbjKgF9OCIy9fzxcxRKaOuYNBdtfsOYr42pJ26Q13fx3whTzwVKhPrpIfx-owDbCXnemXrSCV8v9IFeb0pYbldThnj-yeuaq7FM8_l2f51I_5nKa5B_AwAA__-KLJti)

We're not sitting around waiting on November and hoping everything falls our way. Our teams are already on the ground in these three states, doing the actual work. Knocking doors. Registering voters. Chasing down every conservative ballot until it's counted. Clipboard and tennis shoes work, the kind that doesn't trend online but wins elections. We proved this model in 2024. We ran the most sophisticated ballot-chasing operation the Right has ever put together, and we won every single state where we ran it. 10 for 10. Now we're doing it again, in the three states that decide everything this time. Friend, this is how you can help us win this November. **Every dollar you send fuels the machine we're building in Arizona, Nevada, and New Hampshire right now. More volunteers in the field. More doors knocked. More voters registered. More ballots chased before Election Day.** [**Chip in $25, $50, $100, or whatever you can today. subject: 15 leaders said yes. Here's what happened next:
body:
Fifteen new organizers graduated from the Dream Lab. Now they're organizing in their own communities. | | | Peter, **** Last month, I wrote to you about 15 immigrant youth leaders who were in the middle of a six-week intensive called **Level Up: The Dream Lab**. They graduated! 👩🏽🎓🎉✊🏽 Twelve sessions across six weeks, leaders from eight regions, and by the end, _every single one of them walked away with a community event of their own — planned from start to finish_ , happening this September. Whether it's a training session for high schoolers, a pickup soccer game, or a community mural about where we come from, 15 different communities now have a trained leader who, six weeks earlier, had never organized an event. That's not an accident. **This is what United We Dream does.** **[United We Dream provides the tools, resources, training, and support to make the impossible, inevitable. Will you chip in $15 to power the leadership development that turns 15 people into 15 organizers?](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqswjENXoYacFGtlMLXh6NAeIGjw8YzSH_UAUmMq7WLV0krCNSeQgLJ3AAolc0INa2eTyBEs_xB_hY2lzZHbOAxjyw-kAdfFheVC5z20xSvJkufGs0CTn2EKwkriPmP69WuvklePZ6sl5vrLVsTubHXOIxYzYHjjIEP_mg1VAYG44qVs1rMUQlACvwtYFy8MF-zWx5YBGZ1ozxV39u-EbJki17evvjdO7ViWAgQ4N-AwWegtNr6Lx2FIORLjd7w9fJVAOBC7NP-UmlvuOkAgGHmB6-bB37mUO0eGWCxqMh0V6ZV28JclnICGkPel40yppPkLKMnc4Q4dDiqlTFRQLx_Tk9YlFEtHcqfo17zTA5DGp-GECmYbJxbeHjBQMXlt32tNiREcSjgMjXOTghWIXRO57qa3bmLRbggiZBmgVKKO0oe4ViLKpNHqy3WdPCpegSowSYrKQR8yxE_Jo1Shd3F780lyXPY9RObJXev9m_OKRuHSusgPoccub4oA9_7jmq0/4ti/9U3U6boAT72x3WuLH40N5A/h0/h001.koPjx1llTfjv61wIH4sHKJS_Z6asXUEQwu9ev2i_gy8)** One of our staff facilitators described the moment it clicked, during a session on artivism — the creative power and strategy inside movement-building:
> _"We talked about how movement work isn't limited to protests or traditional organizing. It can be music, dance, poetry, murals, digital media, performance, or something completely different. Then, we gave them space to actually apply it... They were talking through their own ideas, imagining what they wanted to create, and figuring out how they could make those ideas real."_
And on what it means to be the person doing the training:
> _"I might be the trainer today, but the goal is for a member to eventually be the person organizing an event, facilitating a meeting, teaching someone else, or coming up with an idea that none of us on staff could have created for them."_
Peter, that's the whole point. The billionaire class is betting that we'll play it small and stay divided. But we're the builders and the creators who power this country every day — and **every organizer we train is one more person who knows how to bring their neighbors together.** Fifteen of them do. clean_body: Fifteen new organizers graduated from the Dream Lab. Now they're organizing in their own communities. | | | Peter, ** Last month, I wrote to you about 15 immigrant youth leaders who were in the middle of a six-week intensive called Level Up: The Dream Lab. They graduated! 👩🏽🎓🎉✊🏽 Twelve sessions across six weeks, leaders from eight regions, and by the end, every single one of them walked away with a community event of their own — planned from start to finish , happening this September. Whether it's a training session for high schoolers, a pickup soccer game, or a community mural about where we come from, 15 different communities now have a trained leader who, six weeks earlier, had never organized an event. That's not an accident. This is what United We Dream does. One of our staff facilitators described the moment it clicked, during a session on artivism — the creative power and strategy inside movement-building: "We talked about how movement work isn't limited to protests or traditional organizing. It can be music, dance, poetry, murals, digital media, performance, or something completely different. Then, we gave them space to actually apply it... They were talking through their own ideas, imagining what they wanted to create, and figuring out how they could make those ideas real." And on what it means to be the person doing the training: "I might be the trainer today, but the goal is for a member to eventually be the person organizing an event, facilitating a meeting, teaching someone else, or coming up with an idea that none of us on staff could have created for them." Peter, that's the whole point. The billionaire class is betting that we'll play it small and stay divided. But we're the builders and the creators who power this country every day — and every organizer we train is one more person who knows how to bring their neighbors together. Fifteen of them do. Next time, we want it to be more. ** If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | | | | | | | | | In solidarity, Matias, United We Dream Follow us on: | | | | |

* * *
Hey folks,
I want to spend a minute talking about what a petulant child the president of the United States is. This is a man who simply has no self-control and throws wild tantrums whenever he doesn't get his way.
That's not news, of course. But I was struck yesterday by the sheer absurdity of Trump's legal team telling a federal court that if they don't get their way on renaming the Kennedy Center after Donald Trump, they intend to tear it down and replace it with an outdoor amphitheater.
Read that again. Trump's plan is to hold the Kennedy Center hostage unless he gets to rename it and remake it after himself.
And I think that's a great preview of what happens to basically every public institution in America that Trump can't put his name on or twist into whatever bizarre shape he and his people want. It's how he took over the Republican Party, too. He promised he'd burn the whole thing to the ground unless they remade themselves in his image, and now they're virtually gone as a party. The once-great Republican Party of states' rights and personal freedom has become a big-government party shoving a scammy, radical Christian nationalist agenda down our throats while letting Big Tech and corrupt billionaires do whatever the hell they want with this country.
The other piece of news that struck me yesterday, is that Trump's administration is trying to make it actively harder for you to know when and where they're planning to build AI data centers. The EPA wants to strip the public's right to give feedback. No notice. No comment period. Nothing. You don't get a say in what's best for your community and your kids. That might sound like a completely different story from the Kennedy Center. It's not. It's the same instinct: if something stands between them and what they want, it either bends or it breaks.
That's what's amazing to me. If they don't pass that rule, if this community won't take an AI data center, if they don't get to rename this thing after Trump, if the MAGA movement doesn't get exactly what it wants, they promise to just burn it all down. At this point you're basically negotiating with terrorists. These are not people governed by a core set of fundamental values and beliefs beyond self-enrichment, accumulating power, owning their political enemies, and most of all, winning. And once winning becomes the only value, there is basically nothing you can't justify.
It's not too dissimilar from what I told you yesterday about Pennsylvania Republicans suddenly having a positive opinion of John Fetterman. The only reason they like Fetterman is that people like me hate him. It's not because his politics have changed that much. He still votes with Democrats 85 percent of the time. They like him more than they like Dave McCormick, their own Republican senator who votes with Trump 100 percent of the time. It just flows on down.

* * *
Trump is very much a symptom of broader diseases in American society today: the lack of accountability for a very wealthy class of people, our broken campaign finance laws, an institutional rot and malaise that has allowed people to get lazy and refuse to modernize and recognize that we are living in a very different time, where the way people operate is very different. He didn't create all of this. But he figured out how to exploit it, and he accelerates it. And he's also somebody who corrupts everything and everyone around him just by the way he acts. People get enamored by his glow and corrupted by the access to power and opportunity it brings.
I mean, those lawyers arguing in court right now that they'll tear the Kennedy Center down if they can't rename it after him? Those people probably didn't go to law school intending to argue for shit like that. I simply can't believe anybody begins a career that way. So how does somebody become so worn down and characterless over time that they end up trapped in a movement like this? Are they so thirsty for power and money and access that they'll argue and say whatever? I think that's probably the answer. Occam's razor. The simplest answer is usually the correct one. You compromise one thing, then another, then another, until eventually you're standing in federal court, arguing that the president should be allowed tear down a national cultural institution that has belonged to the American people for generations, all because he can't put his name on it. It's disgusting.
I'll end this rant with this: We have to fight like hell to make sure the Democratic Party does not become a mirror-image reverse of what the Republican Party has become. There are a lot of people in the party right now propagating slop and trying to convince you that we should give up and abandon our values, the people we fight for, and the country we want to build together, all in order to beat these guys. But winning cannot be the only value. That's exactly how people end up where Trump's Republican Party is today. It needs to be deeper than that. If we beat the MAGA movement in November, if we beat Donald Trump and his handpicked successor in 2028, but we do it in a way that abandons our core Democratic Party values, we're not going to build a government that can actually solve the fundamental crises we have in this country. We won't get real accountability. We won't fix a broken economy. We won't clean up our broken campaign finance laws. We won't remake this country in the way I believe we really can.
And we have such an opportunity. Every crisis is an opportunity. I'd rather we weren't in this crisis right now. I'd rather Kamala Harris had won the 2024 election. I was proud to support her. But let's take this for the opportunity it is. Trump has shined a light on everything that's broken in American politics today. The brazenness of the Epstein class, these corrupt billionaires, these failed politicians on both sides, frankly, have given us an opening to turn this country around and remake it the same way both Roosevelts did, the way Lincoln did. Not just to defeat something. To build something better in its place. To win in service of something greater than ones self or party.**** That's a generational opportunity. It comes along maybe once, maybe twice in a lifetime. And it's right in front of us.
So my advice to everybody: find the thing you're good at. Find the way you can be useful, to your community, to your family, to your friends. Let's take this moment and turn it around. Because I think we can take the darkness of this moment and the petulant nature of our president and build something pretty goddamn special, something we can all look back on and be proud of, the way past generations turned around rampant corruption and economic calamity and stupid foreign wars. We can do that again.
The pendulum swings, my friends.
Let's fucking go.
With urgency,
--Mike

It's how he took over the Republican Party, too. He promised he'd burn the whole thing to the ground unless they remade themselves in his image, and now they're virtually gone as a party. The once-great Republican Party of states' rights and personal freedom has become a big-government party shoving a scammy, radical Christian nationalist agenda down our throats while letting Big Tech and corrupt billionaires do whatever the hell they want with this country. The other piece of news that struck me yesterday, is that Trump's administration is trying to make it actively harder for you to know when and where they're planning to build AI data centers. The EPA wants to strip the public's right to give feedback. No notice. No comment period. Nothing. You don't get a say in what's best for your community and your kids. That might sound like a completely different story from the Kennedy Center. It's not. It's the same instinct: if something stands between them and what they want, it either bends or it breaks. That's what's amazing to me. If they don't pass that rule, if this community won't take an AI data center, if they don't get to rename this thing after Trump, if the MAGA movement doesn't get exactly what it wants, they promise to just burn it all down. At this point you're basically negotiating with terrorists. These are not people governed by a core set of fundamental values and beliefs beyond self-enrichment, accumulating power, owning their political enemies, and most of all, winning. And once winning becomes the only value, there is basically nothing you can't justify. It's not too dissimilar from what I told you yesterday about Pennsylvania Republicans suddenly having a positive opinion of John Fetterman. The only reason they like Fetterman is that people like me hate him. It's not because his politics have changed that much. He still votes with Democrats 85 percent of the time. They like him more than they like Dave McCormick, their own Republican senator who votes with Trump 100 percent of the time. It just flows on down. Trump is very much a symptom of broader diseases in American society today: the lack of accountability for a very wealthy class of people, our broken campaign finance laws, an institutional rot and malaise that has allowed people to get lazy and refuse to modernize and recognize that we are living in a very different time, where the way people operate is very different. He didn't create all of this. But he figured out how to exploit it, and he accelerates it. And he's also somebody who corrupts everything and everyone around him just by the way he acts. People get enamored by his glow and corrupted by the access to power and opportunity it brings. I mean, those lawyers arguing in court right now that they'll tear the Kennedy Center down if they can't rename it after him? Those people probably didn't go to law school intending to argue for shit like that. I simply can't believe anybody begins a career that way. So how does somebody become so worn down and characterless over time that they end up trapped in a movement like this? Are they so thirsty for power and money and access that they'll argue and say whatever? I think that's probably the answer. Occam's razor. The simplest answer is usually the correct one. You compromise one thing, then another, then another, until eventually you're standing in federal court, arguing that the president should be allowed tear down a national cultural institution that has belonged to the American people for generations, all because he can't put his name on it. It's disgusting. I'll end this rant with this: We have to fight like hell to make sure the Democratic Party does not become a mirror-image reverse of what the Republican Party has become. There are a lot of people in the party right now propagating slop and trying to convince you that we should give up and abandon our values, the people we fight for, and the country we want to build together, all in order to beat these guys. But winning cannot be the only value. That's exactly how people end up where Trump's Republican Party is today. It needs to be deeper than that. If we beat the MAGA movement in November, if we beat Donald Trump and his handpicked successor in 2028, but we do it in a way that abandons our core Democratic Party values, we're not going to build a government that can actually solve the fundamental crises we have in this country. We won't get real accountability. We won't fix a broken economy. We won't clean up our broken campaign finance laws. We won't remake this country in the way I believe we really can. And we have such an opportunity. Every crisis is an opportunity. I'd rather we weren't in this crisis right now. I'd rather Kamala Harris had won the 2024 election. I was proud to support her. But let's take this for the opportunity it is. Trump has shined a light on everything that's broken in American politics today. The brazenness of the Epstein class, these corrupt billionaires, these failed politicians on both sides, frankly, have given us an opening to turn this country around and remake it the same way both Roosevelts did, the way Lincoln did. Not just to defeat something. To build something better in its place. To win in service of something greater than ones self or party.** That's a generational opportunity. It comes along maybe once, maybe twice in a lifetime. And it's right in front of us. So my advice to everybody: find the thing you're good at. Find the way you can be useful, to your community, to your family, to your friends. Let's take this moment and turn it around. Because I think we can take the darkness of this moment and the petulant nature of our president and build something pretty goddamn special, something we can all look back on and be proud of, the way past generations turned around rampant corruption and economic calamity and stupid foreign wars. We can do that again. The pendulum swings, my friends. Let's fucking go. Please accept this shirt as our way of saying thank you for joining this mission. **Give any amount today and choose your shirt size and select a color.**

---
Now let me tell you why this mission means so much to me. My name is Eduardo Verástegui. Several years ago, I learned firsthand about the horrific reality of child trafficking. What I heard broke my heart. Children were being bought and sold.
Families were being torn apart.
Lives were being destroyed. **I couldn't forget it.** **I couldn't stay silent.** I kept asking myself one question: **"What if it were my child?"** That question changed my life. What started as a film project became a mission and a calling. That calling eventually led me to help produce the film _Sound of Freedom_. **Not for fame.**
**Not for awards.**
**But because I believed people needed to see the truth.** For years, many people said the film would never succeed. Doors closed.
Studios walked away.
People told us to give up. **But when innocent children are suffering, silence is not an option.** And while the film helped awaken millions of people to this crisis, awareness alone is not enough. That is why we created the **Sound of Freedom Foundation**. Our mission is simple: **To stop the sale of God's children.**
---

---
Every day, vulnerable children are targeted by traffickers who prey on poverty, instability, loneliness, and fear. And every day, we work to fight back. Jesus said, _"Let the little children come to me, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these."_ (Matthew 19:14) **Every child is precious in God's eyes.** **Every child is created with dignity, purpose, and worth.** And every child deserves someone willing to stand up and fight for them

* **Educate parents and communities** about the warning signs traffickers use to target children.

* **Raise awareness** so more people understand the reality of this crisis.

* **Advocate for stronger protections** for vulnerable children and greater accountability for traffickers.

---
This is how change happens. **One person refuses to ignore the suffering, refuses to stay silent, and chooses to fight for a child they may never meet.** **Today, that person can be you.**

Friend, did you know that I made history as one of the first Native American women elected to Congress, then as the first Native American Cabinet Secretary in U.S. history?

**And when we win this race, I will be the first Native American woman elected Governor in any state.**
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15433?refcode=jtk1263-fr-nd&t=2&akid=11978%2E400544%2EKkITIf)
| | [Donate](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15433?refcode=jtk1263-fr-nd&t=3&akid=11978%2E400544%2EKkITIf)

But while this may be a historic accomplishment — and one that I don't take lightly — the honest truth is this: _My fight has never been about titles or being the first._ It’s always been about working families, standing up for New Mexicans, and making sure more people have a seat at the table.
I’m in this race to lower costs, invest in education, and make healthcare more accessible and affordable. **But I can't get there without you, friend — and with Election Day less than three months away, I need you with me now more than ever.****_[Will you please chip in $5 or more to help me become Governor of New Mexico and continue the fight for working families?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15433?refcode=jtk1263-fr-nd&amount=5&t=4&akid=11978%2E400544%2EKkITIf)_**
