body:
| | | |
---
Friends,

Over the past month, I have criss-crossed this district, meeting voters where they are and hearing what they want and need from their member of Congress.
Across all 28 towns and cities, I am hearing the same struggles. I talk to people working two jobs, who can’t keep up with the rising cost of healthcare, utilities, and other basic necessities; veterans who served this country and came home to find it isn’t fighting for them; parents who did everything right, only to watch their kids have to move back home because they’re drowning in debt. **These are failures of government, and they are unacceptable.** **I am running for Congress to make life easier, not harder. That means cleaning up corruption, lowering costs, and creating a more affordable future for the Hudson Valley.** **I will fight to end the corruption and dysfunction in Washington** by banning members of Congress and the White House from trading stocks and by implementing term limits for Congress and the Supreme Court. **I will work to lower costs** by holding monopoly utility companies accountable, cracking down on corporate landlords and hedge funds driving up housing costs, taking on Big Pharma and insurance companies to lower prescription drug and healthcare costs, expanding access to affordable childcare and universal pre-K, and ending the reckless tariffs. **I will invest in our communities and our future** by expanding BOCES, CTE, and community college programs; putting guardrails on AI and data centers; and creating America’s first Public Service Home Loan Program so teachers, nurses, and first responders can afford to live in the communities they serve.
**The next generation deserves a country where the American Dream can become a reality. That’s what’s on the ballot on November 3rd.**
With gratitude and fire,
Cait Conley

clean_body: | | | | Friends, Over the past month, I have criss-crossed this district, meeting voters where they are and hearing what they want and need from their member of Congress. Across all 28 towns and cities, I am hearing the same struggles. I talk to people working two jobs, who can’t keep up with the rising cost of healthcare, utilities, and other basic necessities; veterans who served this country and came home to find it isn’t fighting for them; parents who did everything right, only to watch their kids have to move back home because they’re drowning in debt. These are failures of government, and they are unacceptable. I am running for Congress to make life easier, not harder. That means cleaning up corruption, lowering costs, and creating a more affordable future for the Hudson Valley. I will fight to end the corruption and dysfunction in Washington by banning members of Congress and the White House from trading stocks and by implementing term limits for Congress and the Supreme Court. I will work to lower costs by holding monopoly utility companies accountable, cracking down on corporate landlords and hedge funds driving up housing costs, taking on Big Pharma and insurance companies to lower prescription drug and healthcare costs, expanding access to affordable childcare and universal pre-K, and ending the reckless tariffs. I will invest in our communities and our future by expanding BOCES, CTE, and community college programs; putting guardrails on AI and data centers; and creating America’s first Public Service Home Loan Program so teachers, nurses, and first responders can afford to live in the communities they serve. The next generation deserves a country where the American Dream can become a reality. That’s what’s on the ballot on November 3rd. subject: my mother could not vote
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Strickland for Washington
body:
---
| |

Today is Women’s Equality Day, the anniversary of the ratification of the 19th Amendment and an opportunity to honor the generations of women who organized, marched, and were jailed for the right to vote.

But the 19th Amendment did not guarantee equal access to the ballot for every woman.

Asian immigrants, like my mother, were barred from becoming American citizens until 1952. Black women across the South, like my grandmother, faced poll taxes, literacy tests, and other discriminatory barriers until the Voting Rights Act was passed in 1965.

The right to vote was hard won. That’s why this week’s news out of the Supreme Court is something we all need to know.

The Court is allowing the Trump Administration to move forward with an executive order that gives them the power to compile federal citizenship lists, threaten election officials with investigations, and develop new Postal Service requirements for mail-in ballots.

This is a clear attempt to make voting harder, to intimidate the people who administer our elections, and to give one man more say over who gets to participate in our democracy.

clean_body: It's time to hold ICE accountable. | | | | = | | | Peter, Watching ICE terrorize communities across this country has been horrifying. And they're only escalating those tactics here in Michigan. We've seen people targeted because of the language they speak or the way they look. We've seen masked agents detain people while families are left wondering what happened. Fear should never be a government policy. I've stood alongside local leaders, clergy, and neighbors demanding accountability. I've introduced legislation to increase transparency and oversight. And I won't stop fighting until we have an immigration system rooted in justice, due process, and basic human dignity. = | | | | | = | | | = | | | = | | | = | | | | = | | Donald Trump has turned ICE into a political weapon. I want to help build a Congress that will finally hold this administration accountable and restore the rule of law. We have a lot of work ahead of us, but I'm not backing down. I hope you'll stand with me. Friend, There is truly nothing like being out on the road, meeting people from all parts of Tennessee, and talking face-to-face about _the future we can build together._ When Jerri talks to folks at diner booths and community centers all across the state, _the message is clear:_ Tennesseans want a governor who will _tackle the rising cost of living_ , _protect healthcare access for every family_ , _and fully fund our public schools_ instead of draining them with private voucher schemes. clean_body: The Court has completely lost its moral authority as a guardian of the Constitution.| | | | Peter, right to vote is under attack. The Supreme Court just cleared the way for the Trump administration’s sweeping executive order to restrict mail-in voting, giving DHS the power to create "state citizenship lists" of voters approved to receive and cast absentee ballots. This is the latest blow from a Supreme Court that has repeatedly weakened voting-rights protections. The majority’s decision in Louisiana v. Callais earlier this year gutted the Voting Rights Act by effectively diluting the voting power of Black Americans. Now Trump is attempting to seize power over elections that the Constitution gives to the states—and the Supreme Court has refused, for now, to stop him. The Court has completely lost its moral authority as a guardian of the Constitution. To restore it, we must enact comprehensive reforms: ✅ Expand the Court from 9 to 13 justices✅ Establish 18-year term limits✅ Institute a binding code of ethics for Supreme Court justices Americans have spent generations fighting to expand democracy. * _He doesn't want to stand on a stage and explain why he took $1 million from Elon Musk while handing tax breaks to the data centers drinking Texas dry. _
* _He doesn't want to answer for the more than 5 million Texans who still have no health insurance — while rural hospitals close on his watch. _
* _He doesn't want to defend taking a $3 million bribe to protect Ken Paxton from being impeached by the Senate._

A debate would force him to face all of it. So instead, he’s avoiding the question and hoping the people of Texas don’t notice.
**We're going to make sure he can’t hide.**
Every day Dan Patrick refuses to show up, we are going to make his silence **_louder_**.
He can avoid me, but he can’t avoid what’s coming in November.

She’s someone we can truly trust to follow the science, and we know the science tells us we’re running out of time to secure a livable future.
Annie sees that reality clearly, and she’s not afraid to take on _anyone_ who’s sold out the people she serves. **That’s why we refuse to write off South Carolina when there’s a climate champion like her on the ballot.**

| | | **August 26, 2026** |
---|---|---|---
| | |
### Senate Update: Two Things at Once - Fighting a Lawless Trump Administration While Delivering for Maryland
As we continue to confront huge challenges at home and abroad, I want to update you on the work I am doing to stand up for Marylanders, defend our democracy, and hold the Trump Administration accountable. Here at home, we continue to see the tragic consequences of an Administration that believes it is above the law. Last month, Trump's Department of Homeland Security and ICE agents shot and killed [two more people](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15236.62433980.8150200.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov%2fpost%2f3mqptam45hk2n&redir_log=298885885804444) in a single week, bringing the total number of people killed by DHS and ICE agents since President Trump returned to office to ten - and that is in addition to the more than 50 people who have died in ICE custody in that same time.
A few weeks ago, I traveled to Minneapolis and visited the makeshift memorials for Renee Good and Alex Pretti. It was heartbreaking to see the teddy bears at the site for Renee Good, reminding us all that her children's stuffed animals were on the passenger side of her car when she was gunned down. The Alex Pretti site displayed photos of the veterans he had cared for as a nurse at the local VA Hospital. Renee Good, Alex Pretti, and the eight others should all be alive today. And, to add insult to injury, Trump's DHS and his Administration will lie to avoid accountability for those who gunned them down. In all of these killings, we need the truth, and we need accountability. I will continue working to ensure these shootings are independently investigated and that those responsible are held accountable. This killing spree must end.
These attacks are part of the Trump Administration's broader assault on immigrant communities - which also includes stripping legal status from Temporary Protected Status (TPS) holders to fuel Trump's mass deportation agenda. Congress established TPS decades ago, with bipartisan support, to ensure that when people cannot safely return to their countries of origin, we do not [put their lives at risk](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15236.62433980.8150200.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov%2fpost%2f3mp7laccim22l&redir_log=403096733467442) by forcing them to go back. While in the United States, these TPS holders are subject to strict eligibility requirements, repeated vetting, and thorough background checks as part of maintaining their legal status. Many of them have lived in the United States for decades, started small businesses, and become part of the fabric of our communities. The fact that his Administration is seeking to end TPS protections puts a lie to Trump's claim that he is focused on deporting "the worst of the worst."
I joined Senate Democrats on the floor to fight to pass legislation that would [redesignate Haiti](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15236.62433980.8150200.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.youtube.com%2flive%2fIDJ5_L4wDbg&redir_log=852189870699268) for TPS through early 2029. That legislation would have protected Haitian TPS holders from being forced back into a country which our State Department's own travel advisory warns is too dangerous to visit for any reason.

I also went to the [Senate floor](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15236.62433980.8150200.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.youtube.com%2flive%2fm87eS833TU8&redir_log=775667314928261) to bring up my [SECURE Act](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15236.62433980.8150200.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.vanhollen.senate.gov%2fnews%2fpress-releases%2ffollowing-trump-attacks-on-tps-van-hollen-30-senators-put-forward-bill-to-protect-tps-and-ded-recipients&redir_log=742000654021097), which would provide qualified TPS and Deferred Enforced Departure (DED) recipients with a pathway to lawful permanent residence after years of living and working legally in the United States. Republicans blocked us from moving forward on both efforts, putting these individuals' lives at great risk.
We must not give up. I will continue pushing to redesignate TPS for Haiti, as well as Yemen and Syria, and restore these protections. We also understand that the Administration is planning to remove TPS for Salvadorans, who represent a large community within Maryland. I will continue fighting to uphold the once bipartisan principle that, in the United States of America, we do not send people directly into harm's way.
Meanwhile, the Trump Administration remains engaged in what a federal judge determined was a [vindictive prosecution](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15236.62433980.8150200.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov%2fpost%2f3mtekz5u6xs2y&redir_log=998325889034447) against Kilmar Abrego Garcia because he exercised his constitutional rights. The judge called the Administration's attack "an abuse of prosecuting power." The Justice Department has asked the federal appeals court to reinstate the charges against Kilmar Abrego Garcia that were already dismissed, as the Administration continues trying to deport him to Liberia. This is unacceptable. I will not stop fighting to uphold Kilmar's constitutional rights - because when the rights of one of us are threatened, the rights of all of us are at risk.
Whether it is standing up for immigrant communities, defending our Constitution, or delivering for Maryland families, I will keep standing up and speaking out to hold this Administration accountable and deliver results for the people of our state. Here's the latest:

---
### Pushing Back Against Trump's Illegal War in Iran
President Trump declared victory in Iran months ago. But almost six months into this war, more Americans and civilians are being killed, the conflict is expanding, and American families are paying higher prices for everything from groceries to gas as a result.
In June, both chambers of Congress passed House Concurrent Resolution 86, directing the President to terminate hostilities against Iran. The passage of that resolution should have marked the end of this disastrous war. But time and again, President Trump has shown he has no respect for the Constitution or the rule of law. So, in July, I brought my [War Powers Resolution](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15236.62433980.8150200.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fyoutube.com%2flive%2f1Qa48A7U0yc%3fsi%3d9u5yowTwyEkFRV-z&redir_log=14463877165375) to the Senate floor to end this senseless and illegal war and force every senator to go on the record. Republicans voted it down, even as they refuse to pass an affirmative resolution to authorize the Iran war. The Constitution is clear: the power to declare war belongs to Congress because our founders understood the danger of allowing any one person to send our service members into harm's way.
Republicans have continued to duck their constitutional duties. If they had the courage of their convictions, they would vote to give President Trump the authorization to use military force. They have refused to do that. Yet, at the same time, they have voted against our effort to end these unauthorized hostilities. Meanwhile, the [costs continue to mount](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15236.62433980.8150200.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov%2fpost%2f3mtm6qzdnf22k&redir_log=967976375119444).
The death toll among American service members is now eighteen, while hundreds more have been injured. Thousands of civilians have been killed across the region. The Strait of Hormuz is closed, gas prices have climbed to about $4 per gallon, and rising fuel costs continue to push up the prices of groceries and other necessities for families here at home.
President Trump told the American people this war would last only weeks. He later repeatedly claimed that we had won. But if we won in March, why were more Americans killed in July? Why is the Strait of Hormuz closed? And why are American families still paying the price? I put those questions directly to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth when he appeared before the Senate Appropriations Committee last month. I asked him: What does winning this war look like? [He had no clear answer](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15236.62433980.8150200.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov%2fpost%2f3mr6x2azimc2y&redir_log=956836475652445).
He eventually said the mission was to prevent Iran from developing a nuclear weapon - even though he and President Trump previously claimed their bombing campaign last year had already "obliterated" Iran's ability to do so. It is clear that this is a war in search of a mission.
Meanwhile, Trump and his Administration have demonstrated contempt for our soldiers on the front lines. Our Marines and members of the Navy have endured grueling conditions aboard the [USS Abraham Lincoln](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15236.62433980.8150200.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov%2fpost%2f3mt7s22crpk2e&redir_log=153601367322441) during its record-breaking deployment of more than eight months without a port of call. The Lincoln is finally headed home, but the Administration's dismissive response to the serious concerns raised by those on board was shameful - including President Trump saying the deployment was "not nearly long enough."

Instead of confronting these failures, the Administration continues to attack the journalists who bring them to light. The Administration wants a press that will spout their propaganda, rather than the facts. They even recently fired the head of the [Stars and Stripes](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15236.62433980.8150200.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov%2fpost%2f3mtoy2ubyuk2i&redir_log=378174426097450) - the independent Department of Defense newspaper funded by taxpayer dollars - yet another blatant crackdown on free speech and a free press.

While they mislead the public about the costs of the war, the Trump Administration is asking Congress for approximately $70 billion more to fund it and replenish depleted weapons stocks. That request comes on top of a proposed $1.5 trillion defense budget, despite the fact that the Pentagon has never passed a clean audit.
Congress should not hand the President a blank check to continue a war that it refuses to authorize. But that's what Republicans want to do. I have been clear: I will not vote to support this illegal, senseless war or add billions to a [bloated Pentagon budget](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15236.62433980.8150200.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.youtube.com%2fshorts%2fK36_jobYZH0&redir_log=197300124779285) that serves as a de facto authorization for it. I will keep fighting to end this war, reassert Congress's constitutional authority, and stop the Trump Administration from sacrificing more American lives and taxpayer dollars for this strategic blunder of epic proportions.

### Fighting Trump's Crypto Corruption
The power of the presidency should be used to serve the American people, not to enrich the person who holds the office. Unfortunately, we are seeing the opposite under Donald Trump. He has turned the presidency into a vehicle for personal enrichment schemes, using the power of the office to benefit himself, his family, and his political allies. The Trump and Melania ["meme coins"](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15236.62433980.8150200.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov%2fpost%2f3mq3jxdaot224&redir_log=336802912674440) are among the clearest examples of this corruption. Nearly one million people who bought Trump's meme coin have lost money, with combined losses totaling $3.8 billion. At the same time, Donald Trump has made approximately $1.4 billion from his family's crypto schemes. In 2025 alone, he raked in $636 million from his crypto coin as part of at least $2.2 billion amassed through all of his business ventures, while the American people pay the price. And it is not just the meme coin. His family's World Liberty Financial venture brought in $799 million last year alone. This is all while the Trump Administration leverages its power over agencies to expand this venture's reach. Earlier this month, the Trump Administration approved a bank charter for World Liberty Financial. The company, the deal, and the entire process are corrupt to the core. [I warned this would happen](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15236.62433980.8150200.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov%2fpost%2f3mtetuizp5k22&redir_log=629330272785445). That's why I joined Senator Warren and our colleagues in [introducing a bill](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15236.62433980.8150200.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.vanhollen.senate.gov%2fnews%2fpress-releases%2ffollowing-approval-of-trump-crypto-company-bank-application-van-hollen-warren-colleagues-introduce-the-ending-presidential-corruption-in-banking-act&redir_log=020246334521420) to ensure that no President, Vice President, their immediate families, or other senior government officials can exploit their positions to own or control a bank, which could serve as a major vehicle for corrupt dealings. We saw the potential for corruption last year when Trump held a special dinner for the largest holders of his meme coin, including foreign investors who spent millions of dollars to gain access to the President of the United States. We've also seen foreign investors from the United Arab Emirates (UAE) make massive investments in World Liberty Financial while the President relaxed export controls on very sensitive chip technology to the UAE. The American people should never have to wonder whether a policy decision was made in the public interest or to increase the value of an asset owned by the President and his family. Congress is currently considering the CLARITY Act, legislation that would establish a new regulatory framework for digital assets. I've said repeatedly that any such legislation must protect consumers, safeguard our financial system, protect our national security, crack down on illicit finance, AND establish real, enforceable protections against corruption, including guardrails against self-dealing and conflicts of interest by the President and Members of Congress. But the CLARITY Act fails all those tests. When the Senate Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs Committee considered the bill in May, I [offered amendments](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15236.62433980.8150200.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov%2fpost%2f3mpm6iz6sns2f&redir_log=215754987845446) to crack down on public officials - including the President and Members of Congress - using digital assets for personal enrichment and to strengthen protections against illicit finance, self-dealing, and other abuses. Republicans blocked those amendments. Without critical changes, the CLARITY Act risks opening the door to more corruption and abuse while failing to provide the protections Americans deserve. The American people see what is happening. They see a President using the power of his office to enrich himself while ordinary people are left holding the bag. They see a system where the people at the top make money and everyone else takes the risk. They deserve better. The presidency is not supposed to be a pathway to owning a pay-to-play casino, and I will keep fighting to ensure that our laws will never allow elected officials to use public office as a vehicle for personal profit.
### Delivering for Maryland and Preserving Our History
Despite the dysfunction and chaos generated by the Trump Administration, I remain focused on delivering real results for communities across Maryland.
In Baltimore, Team Maryland celebrated a major milestone with the completion of the Howard Street Tunnel project. Thanks to $125 million in federal funding we secured for the project, the expanded tunnel can now accommodate double-stacked rail containers. That will allow more cargo to move efficiently through the Port of Baltimore and along the East Coast, increase the Port's container business by an estimated 160,000 containers annually, and support more than 13,000 jobs.
I also joined Congressman Mfume and Beloved Community Services Corporation to celebrate the restoration of the historic [Juanita Jackson Mitchell Law Office](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15236.62433980.8150200.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.instagram.com%2fp%2fDaV6Kn9j7et%2f&redir_log=618641505506266). Juanita Jackson Mitchell was a trailblazing civil rights leader and the first Black woman admitted to practice law in Maryland. The building will now serve as the home of the University of Maryland, Baltimore's ROAR Center, which provides holistic services to survivors of crime. We secured $1.75 million in federal funding to help restore this important civil rights landmark and give it a new life serving Baltimore residents.
And in Baltimore County, I joined local leaders at [AfriThrive Inc.'s community food center](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15236.62433980.8150200.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.instagram.com%2fp%2fDblnBRsnfq3%2f&redir_log=349958689761272) to announce $800,000 secured in federal funding for facility renovations that will increase AfriThrive's ability to help immigrant and low-income families across Baltimore County and Baltimore City put food on the table.
In Southern Maryland, I joined local leaders for the public launch of the Management Plan for the Southern Maryland National Heritage Area. I was proud to help secure the region's designation as a National Heritage Area in 2023, recognizing its extraordinary contributions to our state and nation. This new plan will help preserve Southern Maryland's history and environment, strengthen local tourism, and support economic opportunity throughout the region.
In Montgomery County, I joined the community to celebrate the reopening of the [Pleasant View Historic Site](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15236.62433980.8150200.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.instagram.com%2fp%2fDaGMBZ5kXNc%2f&redir_log=498582223446264). Founded in 1868 by formerly enslaved Maryland families, Pleasant View served as a school, place of worship, and community gathering space at a time when Black Marylanders were denied their most basic rights. We secured $943,000 in federal funding to support its restoration so future generations can learn from this history.
Earlier this month, I traveled to the Eastern Shore to speak with local leaders at the Maryland Association of Counties annual conference and to highlight two federal investments that Senator Alsobrooks and I secured for Shore communities. In Berlin, we fought to deliver $1.4 million that will help transform the historic Flower Street School site into a new community center that will house the SHORE UP! Head Start Center, recreational spaces, and a museum honoring the history of the Flower Street School. In Ocean City, we secured $20 million to support the Army Corps of Engineers' work to replenish the beach, protecting the shoreline, homes, and businesses against storms and erosion.
And last week, I spent the day in Western Maryland with Congresswoman McClain Delaney, highlighting $6.25 million in federal investments we secured in Garrett and Allegany Counties. At Frostburg State University, we delivered over $3.5 million to expand STEM education opportunities, and in Westernport, we delivered $675,000 for the Potomac Fire Company to replace its 35-year-old fire engine. We also highlighted $1 million we secured to support the Garrett Regional Medical Center's new radiation department that will provide treatment for cancer patients across the region, and another $1 million we secured for the Town of Oakland to help replace their aging water infrastructure.
I also recently wrote about the lessons Maryland's history holds for us as our nation commemorated its [250th anniversary](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15236.62433980.8150200.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.baltimoresun.com%2f2026%2f07%2f02%2fchris-van-hollen-america-250%2f&redir_log=91257500696448). From the sacrifice of the Maryland 400 and George Washington's decision to surrender power by resigning his military commission in Annapolis to the courage of Frederick Douglass, Harriet Tubman, and Thurgood Marshall, Marylanders have repeatedly challenged our country to live up to its democratic ideals.
At a moment when the Trump Administration is attacking our history and democratic institutions, their examples remind us that preserving our democracy requires active participation from all of us.

### Important SNAP and Medicaid Changes and Constituent Resources
Marylanders are already feeling the harmful impacts from the devastating cuts to SNAP and Medicaid by the Trump Administration and congressional Republicans in their so-called "Big Beautiful Bill."
Last November, the law imposed more burdensome administrative barriers, making it harder for eligible Maryland families to keep their SNAP benefits. And we've already seen over 35,000 Marylanders lose SNAP because of these Republican cuts. The Maryland Department of Human Services has put together information and resources to help Marylanders navigate these changes, which can be found [here](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15236.62433980.8150200.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fdhs.maryland.gov%2fimportant-changes-snap-benefits%2f&redir_log=61984512624401).

The law will also impose new Medicaid eligibility restrictions beginning October 1, 2026, as well as work requirements beginning January 1, 2027, that may cause up to 165,000 Marylanders to lose their coverage in the coming years. Those who may be affected should watch for official notices from Maryland Health Connection and the Maryland Department of Health. The Maryland Department of Health has put together information and resources to help Marylanders understand these changes and find alternative health care options. You can learn more [here](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15236.62433980.8150200.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fhealth.maryland.gov%2fmmcp%2feligibility%2fPages%2fchanges.aspx&redir_log=571141662802444).

These cuts are among the many changes the Trump Administration and Republicans chose to make to health care and food assistance that are impacting families across Maryland while they, in turn, provided enormous tax breaks to billionaires and wealthy corporations. I voted against these devastating cuts, and I will continue fighting to protect and strengthen access to SNAP and health care for Maryland families.

### Thank You
There is no shortage of urgent work ahead, from protecting the Constitution and ending Trump's illegal war to fighting corruption, defending our elections, delivering for Maryland, and making life more affordable. I am grateful to everyone across Maryland who continues to share their experiences, raise their voices, and stay engaged. Your input directly shapes the fights we take on in the Senate and the solutions we continue to push forward.

Onwards, Chris Van Hollen

To see more on my daily efforts to fight back against the Trump Administration, follow me on: [YouTube](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15236.62433980.8150200.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.youtube.com%2f%40senatorvanhollen&redir_log=49030338036296), [Bluesky](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15236.62433980.8150200.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov&redir_log=939838092693319), [Instagram](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15236.62433980.8150200.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.instagram.com%2fchrisvanhollen%3futm_source%3dig_web_button_share_sheet%26igsh%3dZDNlZDc0MzIxNw%253D%253D&redir_log=547268099313732), [Threads](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15236.62433980.8150200.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.threads.com%2f%40chrisvanhollen&redir_log=958032566321279), [Facebook](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15236.62433980.8150200.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.facebook.com%2fchrisvanhollen%2f&redir_log=328155479639284), and [X](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15236.62433980.8150200.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fx.com%2fChrisVanHollen&redir_log=218313979356198).

And we've already seen over 35,000 Marylanders lose SNAP because of these Republican cuts. The Maryland Department of Human Services has put together information and resources to help Marylanders navigate these changes, which can be found . The law will also impose new Medicaid eligibility restrictions beginning October 1, 2026, as well as work requirements beginning January 1, 2027, that may cause up to 165,000 Marylanders to lose their coverage in the coming years. Those who may be affected should watch for official notices from Maryland Health Connection and the Maryland Department of Health. The Maryland Department of Health has put together information and resources to help Marylanders understand these changes and find alternative health care options. You can learn more . These cuts are among the many changes the Trump Administration and Republicans chose to make to health care and food assistance that are impacting families across Maryland while they, in turn, provided enormous tax breaks to billionaires and wealthy corporations. I voted against these devastating cuts, and I will continue fighting to protect and strengthen access to SNAP and health care for Maryland families. Thank You There is no shortage of urgent work ahead, from protecting the Constitution and ending Trump's illegal war to fighting corruption, defending our elections, delivering for Maryland, and making life more affordable. I am grateful to everyone across Maryland who continues to share their experiences, raise their voices, and stay engaged. Your input directly shapes the fights we take on in the Senate and the solutions we continue to push forward. # Newsom's hidden tax is hitting YOUR wallet
---
| Dear Friend,

The other day, I sat down with Fox News to expose something Gavin Newsom doesn't want you to know about.
---
| [ ](https://us.list-manage.com/6E9FCTL2qds?e=affd398937&c2id=4fd8e839bd16eef39626cb246bcc01d8)
---
| It's called the Vessel at Berth rule. Buried in California's environmental bureaucracy, it forces cargo ships docked at our ports to either plug into state-approved power or pay tens of thousands of dollars a day in fines. Shipping companies aren't eating that cost, you are. California's ports move over 40% of all U.S. container traffic. Every fine gets baked into the price of what's on the truck: your Amazon packages, your groceries, the gas in your tank, the goods on the shelf at your local store. That's not an environmental policy. That's a hidden tax, one Newsom imposed without a single vote in Congress, and one that could spread to ports in every state if we let it stand. I'm not letting it stand. I introduced H.J.Res. 210 to roll back this rule. I am using the Congressional Review Act to force a vote and strike this hidden tax down before it costs families more. As I told Fox News: "It's a massive hidden climate tax that's being imposed on every single ship that's coming into California." Sacramento has an army of bureaucrats and unlimited taxpayer money to defend rules like this one. I have you. Thank you for standing with me. Sincerely

Congressman Vince Fong

name: John Yob
subject: The Virgin Islands Needs Balance
body:
One party Democrat rule has failed. Our islands deserve better.

| | | | | |
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/UwwNNcITWui?e=4f81ceec6f&c2id=39a671a1d75d16cde42206c3cb925b2d)
| | | | | |

Dear Friends,
For nearly three decades, the Virgin Islands Legislature has operated without a single Republican member.
When one political establishment governs without meaningful competition, accountability suffers, new ideas are ignored, and failure becomes easier to excuse.

**This November, the Republican Party in the Virgin Islands will present voters with a platform and candidates to stop corruption, replace WAPA’s failed model, make our communities safer, improve education, and expand affordable housing.**
**Derrick A. Callwood and Eric Tillet are fantastic Republican candidates in St. Thomas–St. John, and we strongly encourage you to support them. Eric has recently launched a website with detailed plans at**[**https://erictillett.com/**](https://us.list-manage.com/1qS9H4wLGB9?e=4f81ceec6f&c2id=39a671a1d75d16cde42206c3cb925b2d)**. More to come from these great candidates!**
**Raymond T. James is running as a Republican in St. Croix. We look forward to hearing more from him soon.**
You do not have to agree with Republicans on everything to believe that our government needs competition.
In the coming weeks, we will introduce our candidates, share our plans, and provide opportunities to get involved. We will also begin recruiting field representatives across St. Thomas, St. John, and St. Croix. Stay tuned!
More competition means more accountability, which creates a better government for every Islander.
Onward!
John Yob
Chairman

# [Musk just committed $100B to Louisiana's Starship fortress](https://substack.com/redirect/7ffadd8d-4343-4820-b5b1-cc1e184abb41?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Lede: SpaceX plans to spend up to $100 billion **[on a Starbase in Vermilion Parish, Louisiana,](https://substack.com/redirect/901c7b64-008b-45ed-9d1b-8cb078c0999b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** at a **[former Exxon property](https://substack.com/redirect/22eef4b2-d94d-4c7c-bc65-1c9a36cfb440?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to support thousands of Starship launches annually as its main facility.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7ffadd8d-4343-4820-b5b1-cc1e184abb41?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Seven-year site search:** SpaceX chose the Vermilion Parish location after a seven-year hunt for launch pads and ample fuel access, making it the company's fourth launch site and primary Starship base.
* **Major jobs projection:** Musk said the spaceport will bring probably 10,000 really exciting jobs, while a state fact sheet estimates 3,000 direct new jobs over 10 years and 8,100 indirect ones.
* **Shares rise on news:** SpaceX stock rose about 2% to close at $137.95, as Wall Street loves the huge spending and sees a bigger payoff tied to Starship-driven nearly $2 trillion valuation.
* **Coastal restoration plan:** SpaceX will partner with Louisiana on historic coastal restoration to bring the marsh back and provide storm protection for the wetlands surrounding the new facility.

# [Zuckerberg's $18B bill for years of teen social media harm](https://substack.com/redirect/7ffadd8d-4343-4820-b5b1-cc1e184abb41?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Meta agreed to pay as much as $18 billion over 10 years **[to settle claims by dozens of states](https://substack.com/redirect/9927fe6f-290d-4db7-a360-731f3bfd1c51?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** that Facebook and Instagram were **[designed to addict children,](https://substack.com/redirect/d08a8e6c-f772-4856-b86c-ebb088fa5273?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** adding teen time limits and urging rivals to match.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7ffadd8d-4343-4820-b5b1-cc1e184abb41?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Settlement Payment Details:** Meta will pay approximately $12.7 billion over 10 years to participating states, with an additional $5.3 billion conditional on YouTube and TikTok adopting similar youth protections and matching payments.
* **Required Platform Changes:** The deal requires daily usage limits and nighttime blocks for teens on Facebook and Instagram plus enhanced age assurance measures, school-hour notification mutes and additional parental control tools.
* **Trial Stock Reaction:** The settlement ended the second week of a high-stakes federal trial in Oakland that averted potential testimony from CEO Mark Zuckerberg as Meta shares rose on the news.
* **Pennsylvania Sues Snapchat:** Attorney General Dave Sunday **[sued Snap Inc.](https://substack.com/redirect/892b75ce-224a-4b01-b87f-f074e843df72?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/892b75ce-224a-4b01-b87f-f074e843df72?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)alleging features like Snapstreaks and infinite scrolling keep minors compulsively engaged, expose them to adult content and mislead parents about safety.

* * *
* * *
# [Anthropic eyes $30 trillion as OpenAI threatens Nvidia's throne](https://substack.com/redirect/7ffadd8d-4343-4820-b5b1-cc1e184abb41?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
OpenAI **[unveiled its Jalapeño custom inference chip](https://substack.com/redirect/9e07df6b-c567-44fb-a75f-77f71167cd46?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** with Broadcom that tests show beats Nvidia Blackwell on efficiency, **[Anthropic eyes over $30 trillion potential revenue](https://substack.com/redirect/f9554ab0-20e3-43a6-acf0-f4aff794de46?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/f9554ab0-20e3-43a6-acf0-f4aff794de46?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)topping SpaceX, and Microsoft **[faces opacity criticism](https://substack.com/redirect/65634a11-d960-447e-bf43-fab728f41206?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** on AI.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7ffadd8d-4343-4820-b5b1-cc1e184abb41?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Chip efficiency gains:** SemiAnalysis found OpenAI Jalapeño beat Nvidia Blackwell on performance per watt in nearly all scenarios after visiting labs, though HBM4 makes Rubin a fairer comparison.
* **Nvidia margin threat:** Analysts say the Broadcom-partnered chip threatens Nvidia inference margins in the fastest-growing field and could cut reliance by OpenAI, one of its largest customers, with year-end deployment.
* **Anthropic revenue target:** The Claude maker is expected to tell investors its potential revenue opportunities exceed $30 trillion, topping SpaceX's $28.5 trillion estimate according to people familiar with the matter.
* **Microsoft opacity critique:** Microsoft stands out among tech giants for limited transparency on AI businesses from capital expenditures to its flagship Azure platform after years of asking investors to take strategy on faith.

* **Relocation interest surges:** Florida Chamber CEO Mark Wilson reported inquiries from technology firms and others seeking to escape higher taxes, with one Rochester company calling Florida the land of opportunity.
* **Economic contrast drawn:** An $80,000 welder in Ocala enjoys median homes under $300,000, no state income tax and beaches while the same worker in New York City faces unaffordable housing and heavier taxes.
* **Budget and population gaps:** New York City's $125.8 billion fiscal 2027 budget exceeds Florida's $117.6 billion even as Florida's population tops 23 million against the city's roughly 8.3 million.

* * *
* * *
# [Trump's DOJ just forced Deloitte to pay $21.5M over DEI](https://substack.com/redirect/7ffadd8d-4343-4820-b5b1-cc1e184abb41?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Deloitte agreed to pay $21.5 million to resolve Justice Department allegations t**[hat its DEI practices violated anti-discrimination rules in federal contracts](https://substack.com/redirect/d02cd83a-53d8-44a8-af98-ea348a7a0d3b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** under the False Claims Act, without admitting liability.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7ffadd8d-4343-4820-b5b1-cc1e184abb41?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Settlement terms clarified:** The $21.5 million payment settles False Claims Act claims brought via qui tam by the American Alliance for Equal Rights, which will receive a $4.3 million share of the recovery.
* **Alleged DEI tracking:** Business units received monthly demographic goal summaries and partners were evaluated partly on contributions to workforce composition targets aimed at boosting Black and Hispanic representation.
* **No liability admitted:** Deloitte stated the settlement avoids the cost and distraction of litigation and resolves only allegations with no determination of liability by any court.
* **Justice Department stance:** Attorney General Todd Blanche said government contractors cannot reward or penalize based on race or sex and that labeling the practice DEI does not make it lawful.

Hi, friend,

I’m Adam Hamilton, an independent-minded Democrat running for U.S. Senate in Kansas. If you have a moment, I'd love to share a bit about who I am and why I'm in this race.
I’m a husband, a father of two remarkable daughters and a grandfather to an amazing 12-year-old granddaughter. I’m also the founding pastor of the largest United Methodist Church in the country and a proud fifth-generation Kansan.
My great-great-grandparents moved to Dickinson County, Kansas, 147 years ago. They were farmers and builders and good people who helped build their communities of Hope and Elmo. Like them, I love Kansas and its people, and I love my country. That’s why I feel called to run for the U.S. Senate.
Today, our nation’s highest values and aspirations are being undermined, and chaos and corruption in Washington are tearing Americans apart. We’ve insulted and alienated our allies. And we have a government in D.C. that’s making life harder for Kansans. People can’t afford the basics — food, gas and health care.
I’m running for the U.S. Senate because I care about our country, because things need to change and because I know I can build bridges, bring people together to solve problems and be a champion for Kansas.
I’ve heard from Kansans all over the state who voted for Roger Marshall six years ago and now feel he’s not listening to them. People who have met with him and felt unseen or dismissed by the man they elected to represent them.
I believe we can and must do more — and as the leader of a large, diverse congregation of roughly equal parts Democrats, Republicans and Independents, I am ready to disrupt partisan gridlock in Washington, bring people together and create meaningful solutions to our problems.
**That work starts now, and if you agree that what’s going on in our country is unacceptable, then I need you with me. Nothing about this race will be easy, and we’re going to need an incredible grassroots team to create change in Kansas._[If you're able to, please consider joining us now by chipping in anything you can spare.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137971104/642553880/-540544497?amounts=10,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk75-fr-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjMvMS8xMjYxMjYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiN2NkOTRmMjgtNzhhMS1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5ZjFkIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=Huz0y5PTihkfAcZ5PV4VpOH6X1Kpt4UEHOTqkwYW1Hc=)_**

**_I couldn’t read or write when I came to this country at nine years old._**

I arrived the _**legal**_ way, on the Fourth of July.

_**My first meal in America was a Big Mac.**_
I had certainty that this place was different — that if you worked, if you obeyed the law, if you refused to quit, **you could build something no one could take from you.**

**My first job was cleaning rooms as a maid in a casino. **

Long nights. Hard floors. Invisible work.

I didn’t complain. I learned the language. I worked. _**I earned every step.**_

That is the American Dream as I lived it, not a slogan, not a handout, not a political prop.

It was sweat, order, and the rule of law.

**Today, Democrats are working tooth and nail to destroy that Dream.**

_They reward those who skip the line while the people who did it the right way get lectured. _

_They treat our border like a suggestion and our laws like optional guidelines. _

And in state after state, they have turned the Attorney General’s office into a political weapon, a partisan battering ram aimed at parents, businesses, law enforcement, and anyone who still believes in equal justice under the law.

_That is not what the office is for._

**The Attorney General is supposed to be the person who runs the legal war room for the state. **

The one who defends the Constitution, enforces the law without fear or favor, protects citizens from cartels and criminals, and stops the Left’s lawfare before it metastasizes.

Not a partisan activist with a government letterhead. _Not a tool._ **A guardian.**

I know what it costs to build the American Dream because I paid that cost with my own hands.

clean_body: Will you read my story?| | | I couldn’t read or write when I came to this country at nine years old. I arrived the legal way, on the Fourth of July. My first meal in America was a Big Mac. I had certainty that this place was different — that if you worked, if you obeyed the law, if you refused to quit, you could build something no one could take from you. My first job was cleaning rooms as a maid in a casino. Long nights. Hard floors. Invisible work. I didn’t complain. I learned the language. I worked. I earned every step. That is the American Dream as I lived it, not a slogan, not a handout, not a political prop. It was sweat, order, and the rule of law. Today, Democrats are working tooth and nail to destroy that Dream. They reward those who skip the line while the people who did it the right way get lectured. They treat our border like a suggestion and our laws like optional guidelines. And in state after state, they have turned the Attorney General’s office into a political weapon, a partisan battering ram aimed at parents, businesses, law enforcement, and anyone who still believes in equal justice under the law. That is not what the office is for. The Attorney General is supposed to be the person who runs the legal war room for the state. The one who defends the Constitution, enforces the law without fear or favor, protects citizens from cartels and criminals, and stops the Left’s lawfare before it metastasizes. Not a partisan activist with a government letterhead. Not a tool. A guardian. I know what it costs to build the American Dream because I paid that cost with my own hands. I will not stand by while they dismantle it for the next generation, including the children of legal immigrants who still believe this country is worth the sacrifice. That’s why we’re asking WFP supporters across Pennsylvania to get behind them now. **[Split a contribution between Sara and Brad’s campaigns and help us turn two close races into two wins for working people.](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqu_GJOObYrLsTGSvl2mTcjtvbey4ZHZ3frxg8y-TOwGUkw7TsCVsbRgYRtvXcZQ5FA8l1wosKt5PMc9rQ0e0dGWj0OxdU80ybAf2Y_1_xx5mq5nCLhJe_PeUMlYTE4hMBVHAcGKTLUJbNdebd4Km9mTQZneON3rb3mEICCgEEQw4XEHD23iyA3_OeS3PLb2_oFhW0nzWWfDsNV40QDPKIT5Dm5sNaqe8hh0Wy-eCFFzESftCcgc9rfDFAsdR1VNYt1VpIojlId1PIVjKUAWth7wW8dAVTnNvV0g3LqqbhPZRsIDP2hkL2j5Bze8Ia40BZAjVTcwjDa_xnxLharp7ea6V7lohkOSXMnCglH0mxL5Ei-3bDgQ4azQeJI2QGVeupk/4ti/NyZ3eEBHQVurxFjcQQ6y7A/h0/h001.xASpZoIGg5_q2GfFM84Mo_xMajTeHtf9U2nDlcrQbUc)** **[Split a contribution to Sara and Brad](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqu_GJOObYrLsTGSvl2mTcjtvbey4ZHZ3frxg8y-TOwGUkw7TsCVsbRgYRtvXcZQ5FA8l1wosKt5PMc9rQ0e0dGWjzDOFX6YaLYWyvT2Vku6s1v4AA4-n2CDFyZFcnXT8u9xj3BHnBI2ME5vNZE-3Zh22a7xWDI4Iqq7aKMbb2Uofhuttp05Ud312RhPykTY6TXNO5YgAe3Yl-4AzJqSLO__OSvRAbCNpvcMQLQFHduanXoOvTMqIKloZd8RBbjh9QFGJARNmW1SrlleE54k3bcacK1HGEYZkjs63DkRcpMEZQZJ_lnuZjsGkORg-xVc5eyWwewSMvzjs3rKZYvLNKdmm-sZQvP0iRerMbQ4lXQcmzQDLtb1ZWFS1D69uSfDMiw/4ti/NyZ3eEBHQVurxFjcQQ6y7A/h1/h001.BEp-ep1t9mhy5miGYRHSCydl4Ard-TgD_-km_QX8Zv8)** Both Sara and Brad ran in 2024. Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

body:
You can imagine how hard it was...
---
| |
---
As a grassroots candidate up against an incumbent with corporate PAC money, I need all the help I can get to fuel this movement. So when a new supporter tried to slide me a check for $10,000 today - I was overwhelmed with gratitude. **But I couldn 't accept it. ** Campaign finance laws are strict about how much candidates can accept in individual contributions, and now that we're post-Primary, that means $3,500 per person. **Some campaigns might start looking for loopholes to accept the extra funds. But that 's not how we do things. ** I told him how grateful I was that he believes in our shared vision for a better East Tennessee, but that I got into this race to change our political system so it's beholden to the people again. I want to follow not only the letter but the spirit of the law while I work for comprehensive campaign finance reform to return our power to us. **We don 't change the system by becoming the system. ** We're a 100% people-powered campaign with an average donation of $64. There are folks with the means to give more, and we're honored that they do. But this campaign is truly funded by the working people who believe, as I do, that our government should _work for us_ , not just the wealthy and well-connected. **If you 've been wondering if your $5, $10, or $25 will make a difference, I am so excited to tell you that we're just a few of those contributions away from our first $100,000 month! ** This milestone unlocks radio ads (especially in our rural communities), digital billboards on thousands of screens, physical billboards on roadsides, and a few more surprises we have in store for this historic moment. **Will you chip in whatever you can to help put me in Congress so we can fix our government?**

name: Americans for Responsible Innovation
subject: NEW DATE: Meet the Lawmakers Speaking Out On Data Centers
body:
September 10: the Republicans and Democrats writing the rules for data center deals in Ohio, New York, Georgia, and Missouri, on what communities can demand.

| | Virtual Panel |
---|---
# NEW DATE: Meet the Lawmakers Speaking Out on Data Centers
Virtual event rescheduled for 2 PM ET on September 10
Across the country, residents are demanding a voice in negotiations for data center deals that impact their communities. Some voters have passed guardrails protecting against rising energy demand, some have demanded a moratorium, and some have secured local investment in education and workforce training.

**On September 10, hear from state and local leaders who have secured guardrails in their community.** State lawmakers, county officials and advocates will share their success stories advocating for agreements that mandate transparency and benefit their communities.
|
---
Construction is accelerating. In most places, the terms are not public.
| Thursday, September 10
2:00 PM ET, online | | [Register](https://us.list-manage.com/wMx0riSzsiE?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
---
What we'll explore | What have communities actually secured from developers and hyperscalers, and which of those wins can be replicated?
---
Where do negotiations break down, and what do siting trackers and energy reporting change at the bargaining table?
What should residents be entitled to when a data center comes to town?
Panelists | Ohio Rep. Adam Holmes Chair, House Energy Committee | New York Sen. Kristen Gonzalez Chair, Internet & Technology Committee
---|---
Georgia Comm. Peter Hubbard Georgia Public Service Commission | Missouri Sen. Joe Nicola District 11, Jackson County
| Moderator Jessica Maksimov Americans for Responsible Innovation
---|---

Peter,
**Over the last few weeks, the momentum behind this campaign has been unbelievable.** Three separate polls have me within one point of Greg Abbott.
And everywhere I go in Texas, people are making it clear that they are ready for a clean slate and a governor that actually works for them.
**Because of this surge in support, our team set an ambitious goal to raise $2 million online this month.** The great news is that thanks to grassroots supporters like you, we are already 86% of the way to our goal.
We know $2 million sounds like a massive number — and it is. But right now, Greg Abbott is sitting on a $67 million war chest, and his campaign is already ramping up major ad buys across Texas.
We don't need to match his millions dollar-for-dollar. We just need enough resources in this final stretch to make sure our message is heard, keep traveling across the state, and execute our turnout strategy on the ground.

That means we have to raise the remaining 14% of our goal before our deadline on August 31st.

name: Andrew Sneed for Congress
subject: Join us for a Town Hall tonight – Plus a campaign update!
body:
Here's where the campaign stands, and how you can get involved.
---
| | | | [ View in browser](https://h8g0t.r.ag.d.sendibm3.com/mk/mr/sh/SMJz09SDriOHTaoDGkpqIpMfjg9x/PDFpTL4R5N7G)
---
| | | | |
---
| | | Peter,
We are less than 70 days away from Election Day! Here is what is what we're up to these next few weeks.
---
**TOWN HALLS ACROSS THE DISTRICT** Please join us tonight, August 26th, in Decatur for our second Town Hall! Details below. We're excited to have newly elected Alabama Democratic Party Chair, Senator Bobby Singleton join us in support!
We have two more 'Hear Every Voice' Town Halls to follow in Athens and Huntsville. I'd love to see you there and hear from you directly. Every voice in this district deserves to be heard, and I want to hear yours: your thoughts, your concerns, whatever's on your mind, regardless of your political affiliation. It is past time for a representative that listens.
**Doors open at 5:30 PM for each event:** August 26, 6:00 PM - Turner Surles Resource Center, Decatur, ALSeptember 9, 6:00 PM - McCandless Hall, Athens, ALOctober 5, 6:00 PM - Bob Harrison Center, Huntsville, AL
|
---
Save the date and stop by if you're able. I know you're in this with me, but we need you (and your friends) to show up and ask the hard questions that your Representative should answer.
| [ RSVP Online!](https://h8g0t.r.ag.d.sendibm3.com/mk/cl/f/sh/SMK1E8tHeFuBlbNaKGvxQIyuMhJZ/fokBQ0YWze7l)
---
**CANVASSING & PHONEBANKING ARE IN FULL SWING**Our team is pushing to build a presence in every precinct across the district. Since launching the general election field program, volunteers have knocked and called over 6,000 voter contacts spanning all 6 counties, door to door and phone to phone. Every one of those conversations counts. AL-05 deserves a representative who actually shows up, and that's exactly what we're doing.
We need more hands on deck: canvassing, phonebanking, event support, and more. Reach out and we'll get you plugged in!
| [ Join Us & Volunteer!](mailto:info@sneedforcongress.com?subject=Becoming%20a%20Volunteer)
---
**NEW MERCH STORE IS LIVE** Rep the campaign with our new gear: shirts, hats, and more, all on the new website! We will be launching new products soon, and hope to see more Sneed for Congress merch across the district! We're proud that these items are union-made here in the United States.
| [ Shop Here!](https://h8g0t.r.ag.d.sendibm3.com/mk/cl/f/sh/SMK1E8tHeG13DkCXVR5RW8HeKztp/mTneQZujN1Bm)
---
**REQUEST A SNEED FOR CONGRESS YARD SIGN** Want to show your support where your neighbors can see it? Yard signs are back in stock and ready to go.Pick one up: Stop by the campaign office at 303 Williams Ave SW, Building 1, Suite 116, Huntsville, AL, 35801
Request a sign at the link below or email Info@SneedforCongress.com to let us know you'd like one!
| [ Request a Sign!](https://h8g0t.r.ag.d.sendibm3.com/mk/cl/f/sh/SMK1E8tHeG7uft1UgbEvbxaOJIU5/83zvFz92sU0d)
---
| Thank you for standing with this campaign. Every door knocked, dollar given, and conversation started is how we win this district back for working people. Let's keep working towards a better future, together!
- Andrew Sneed

---

| | | |
---
**Andrew Sneed for Congress**
614 Madison Street, 35801, Huntsville
This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com.You've received this email because you've subscribed to our newsletter.
[_Unsubscribe_](https://h8g0t.r.ag.d.sendibm3.com/mk/un/v2/sh/SMJz09a0vkbXpgHt2UzdRcFmzNm5/GWtSKre95B8k)

I hope you’ll take a moment to read it – but if you’re short on time and already committed to electing VA Democrats up and down the ballot this November,[_**chip in before my first end-of-month fundraising deadline of the general election.**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137976053/642562015/1355166437?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_EOM1_260826_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwZjkxNDE4ZC03ZmExLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=evrVuHcWHq9KSV6yKg7m8BpQHNJtT2R7le4YuMOBqx0=))_ I’m asking Virginians to re-hire me one last time, Derek, because I truly believe in this simple idea:

**Where you start should never determine where you end up.**

I grew up in a middle class family, went to public school, and was the first in my family to graduate from college.

I tried to break into the business world, and I failed in less than six weeks. My second venture was equally unsuccessful. But the great thing about this country is that you can always pick yourself back up and start over. On my third try, I was fortunate enough to have a breakthrough in the telecommunications industry.

**Those experiences taught me that success should _never_ depend on where you were born, who your parents are, or whether you had the right connections.**

But right now, too many folks don’t feel that way:

→ Virginians are facing skyrocketing prices at the grocery store and gas pump due to this president’s reckless war in Iran and downright dumb tariff policies.

→ They see health care access shrinking and rural hospitals closing because this administration would rather give tax breaks to those at the very top than help working families.

→ And they see blatant corruption and cruelty from Trump and his GOP allies that goes completely unchecked.

I’m running for reelection because I believe every American deserves the same shot as success I had. They deserve someone who will fight for them, work to make their lives better, and put some real guardrails on this administration run amok.

I’m asking you to re-hire me so I can fight to bring down everyday costs, expand access to health care, build more affordable housing, protect America’s standing on the world stage, and prepare our economies and communities for the changes brought on by Artificial Intelligence.

That’s why I’m in this race – and it’s why I’m asking for your support ahead of my campaign's first end-of-month deadline of the general election. The resources we raise now determine the strength of this campaign in the coming weeks. Every dollar and every grassroots donor makes a difference in this final sprint to Election Day.

[_**So please, if you’re ready to win this race and elect Democrats across Virginia who will fight to give working families their fair shot, chip in ahead of my campaign’s end-of-month fundraising deadline >>>**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137976054/642562016/1355166437?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_EOM1_260826_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwZjkxNDE4ZC03ZmExLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=evrVuHcWHq9KSV6yKg7m8BpQHNJtT2R7le4YuMOBqx0=)

The fight continues,

Mark Warner **Before you go:**

We’re asking people like you – who care deeply about our democracy and the future of our country – to join us in our fight to help Democrats win the midterms and bring accountability and transparency to Washington.

name: Heidi Ganahl
subject: The Mountain Minute: 8/26/2026
body:
What the Supreme Court did, and did not do, on Trump’s mail-ballot order
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Hi friends!
Want your full news breakdown? Listen to the Mountain Minute podcast [here](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), or watch on [YouTube](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) or [Rumble](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Here's a summary of today's top stories:
**🏔️ Here in Colorado...** A federal judge heard arguments on [Colorado's three-day gun purchase waiting period](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), with challengers calling it inconsistent with historical tradition and the state defending it as mirroring federal background-check timelines. A Denver audit found the $175.6 million 16th Street project suffered [an $18 million overrun and year-long delay](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) that bypassed City Council after a historic brick sewer was mishandled. And the Supreme Court lifted an injunction on Trump's mail-voting order, though a separate order still blocks USPS enforcement for November, [leaving Colorado's mail-ballot rules unchanged](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.); AG Phil Weiser called it a delay, not a defeat.
**🇺🇸 On the National Stage...** The Supreme Court ruled [Trump may enforce his mail-in voting order](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) for now while litigation continues in the 23 states that sued. Separately, [immigrant grocers sued NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) over his government-supermarket plan, arguing it threatens family-owned bodegas—a claim Mamdani rejects.
**🗣️ Commentary Spotlight...** Colleen Enos criticized Colorado's record on parental rights, citing an [ADF notice over a graphic Roaring Fork sex-ed curriculum](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) and DOJ guidance flagging the state's hostility to religious liberty. Nash Herman warned Initiative 195's graduated income tax would cause "bracket creep," pointing to [Prop FF as precedent](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). And C. J. Garbo examined [three federal gun-rights lawsuits against Colorado and Denver](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), arguing they test whether courts treat the Second Amendment as a real limit on government.
This is your Mountain Minute for Wednesday, August 26, 2026.
– Team RMV
---
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[What the Supreme Court did, and did not do, on Trump’s mail-ballot order](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
The Supreme Court handed the Trump administration a win Monday on mail-in voting, and the headlines said so. But for a Colorado voter, nothing has changed yet. The state remains set to send November ballots under existing rules, because a second court order the justices did not touch still blocks the part of the president’s plan most directly tied to how voters receive their ballots.
That gap between the headline and the effect is the story. The Court cleared one obstacle in Trump’s path. It did not rule that his election order is legal, and it did not change how Coloradans get their ballots this fall.
Colorado is not a bystander in the case. It is one of the plaintiffs that brought the suit, represented by Attorney General Phil Weiser, and one of eight states, plus the District of Columbia, with statewide mostly mail elections. So the question of who controls the mail ballot reaches further here than almost anywhere else.
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Three federal cases test whether Colorado treats gun rights as policy or as a limit on government](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY C. J. GARBO, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
_A federal judge weighs whether Colorado's mandatory waiting period on firearm purchases can survive the Supreme Court's history-based Second Amendment test._
* **A law with no historical roots, challengers argue:** Attorney Michael D. McCoy told the court that "cooling off"-style waiting periods didn't exist until the 1990s, arguing there's no historical tradition supporting Colorado's 2023 law and that any government-imposed delay on firearm acquisition is unconstitutional.
* **The state's defense leans on practicality:** Assistant Solicitor General Joseph G. Michaels countered that the challengers are effectively demanding a constitutional right to "immediate" gun acquisition — something impractical even at the founding — and noted federal law already builds in time for background checks.
* **The case turns on the Supreme Court's 2022 test:** Under the framework the Court established that year, judges must first determine whether the Second Amendment's text covers the regulation, then require the government to show the law is consistent with historical firearm regulations near the time of the amendment's adoption.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|

**ONLY ON ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE ⤵️**
**[DougCo’s charter proposal protects schools from competition, not choice](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**BY KIM GILMARTIN | COMMENTARY | AUGUST 24** _Douglas County has long been known as a community that values school choice, which is one reason a resolution recently advanced by the Douglas County School District (DCSD) Board of Education deserves much more attention than it has received._
__
**[A fire chief lost his free speech case. The day after, he published a book.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**BY SHAINA COLE | STATE | AUGUST 24** _Erik Holt read the opinion the morning it came down on July 7 at 9 a.m. Three federal judges had decided that when the former Florissant fire chief handed election surveillance footage to a criminal investigator examining alleged misconduct in the board’s election, he was doing his job, not speaking as a citizen._
____
__**[Davidson: Capitalism trusts you to choose. Socialism does not.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** **BY JAY DAVIDSON | COMMENTARY | AUGUST 24** _Only one economic system accounts for human nature. Economics is the study of human nature. It seeks to explain how individuals interact in the exchange of a medium of value: money, barter, services, etc. Psychology, social science, even philosophy also study human nature. Whereas these studies can affect us at different times, the economy constantly affects us._**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**__
