Power, Prosperity, Peace
| Friends, We need politicians who answer to their constituents, not wealthy donors or corporations. This is the bare minimum for a healthy democracy. Yet here we are, in a country where the wealthy can donate unlimited amounts to super PACs who represent special interests. Corporations can form PACs and use them to donate to candidates. Knowledge is power and you can use [this resource](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/7BI0urCWrc4M2ahnVJdaJzyPbdHIGrTX/click?signature=3d979d4de17bbef49fe6499490611dec5835a502&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.opensecrets.org%2F) to see where your elected officials get their campaign funding. You can also track how your Representative and Senators are voting by using [this link](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/7BI0urCWrc4M2ahnVJdaJzyPbdHIGrTX/click?signature=b37c115e5a7073a4bc2c6ab5d2ce5a081a093bba&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.congress.gov%2F) to search issues or specific bills. Using these resources, we can connect campaign funding to key issues:
* Weapons manufacturers to foreign policy
* The prison industrial complex to criminal justice and immigration policies
* Fossil fuel companies to climate change policy
* Private equity to housing (and much more!)
* Pharmaceutical and insurance companies to our healthcare

Paige believes the solution to getting the things everyday Americans need - things like Medicare for All, affordable housing and childcare - is to get big money out of politics. Because if a politician is funded by special interests, what is the likelihood that they will truly deliver for everyday Americans? Paige's opponent says she is fighting for a fair deal for Granite Staters which "[requires taking on corporate special interests to lower costs for Granite Staters](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/7BI0urCWrc4M2ahnVJdaJzyPbdHIGrTX/click?signature=11e1562f8be7981459f090f64a6fba0e66c3dbc1&url=https%3A%2F%2Fmaggiefornh.com%2Fpriorities%2F)." Interestingly, in the 2024 and 2026 campaign cycles, she has taken money directly from special interest [PAC Real Estate Roundtable](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/7BI0urCWrc4M2ahnVJdaJzyPbdHIGrTX/click?signature=84d6e8a9d8f7ad10c9d0cd8027aab6bbdbeee46e&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.fec.gov%2Fdata%2Freceipts%2F%3Fdata_type%3Dprocessed%26committee_id%3DC00797670%26committee_id%3DC00815753%26committee_id%3DC00878454%26contributor_name%3DC00033779) (an organization that includes prominent real estate owners and which wrote to Joe Biden in 2022 to urge greater federal impact on [return to office work for federal employees](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/7BI0urCWrc4M2ahnVJdaJzyPbdHIGrTX/click?signature=e55d99768aa7caf19a4bd42fefcffe2e20d5b539&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.costar.com%2Farticle%2F350893718%2Fus-real-estate-firms-urge-federal-government-to-bring-workers-back-to-the-office)). She took $5000 directly from [AIPAC](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/7BI0urCWrc4M2ahnVJdaJzyPbdHIGrTX/click?signature=dd433a965bd25e8c9f432904b624de519fa05b5d&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.fec.gov%2Fdata%2Freceipts%2F%3Fdata_type%3Dprocessed%26committee_id%3DC00878454%26two_year_transaction_period%3D2026%26line_number%3DF3-11C) this campaign cycle. She has taken notable amounts of money associated with [ Blackstone and Bain Capital ](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/7BI0urCWrc4M2ahnVJdaJzyPbdHIGrTX/click?signature=24e11299d34993af437ef3a93908aba5723b6aeb&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.opensecrets.org%2Fprofiles%2Fmaggie-goodlander%2Fus_congress%2Forganizations%3Fcycle%3D2026%26display%3Dcandidate%26mpid%3D1347687)(totaling over $100,000 between both election cycles). Paige's opponent also makes a point of expressing her dedication to New Hampshire. Yet the state that has made the most donations to her campaign is [New York](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/7BI0urCWrc4M2ahnVJdaJzyPbdHIGrTX/click?signature=60cfd2e88e0b2e95115eedbee4e4cf905bd1d719&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.fec.gov%2Fdata%2Fcommittee%2FC00878454%2F%3Ftab%3Draising). 14% of her contributions come from in-state. Paige is a working-class mom, a registered nurse and a sitting State Representative. She had a humble upbringing in New Hampshire. She returned to New Hampshire in 2018, well before her state or federal congressional aspirations began. The state that has made the highest donations to her campaign is [New Hampshire](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/7BI0urCWrc4M2ahnVJdaJzyPbdHIGrTX/click?signature=8355d0ec5f26e9e911624996ef036e7d02796ce6&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.fec.gov%2Fdata%2Fcandidate%2FH6NH02261%2F%3Ftab%3Draising), with about 31% of donations coming from in-state. The[ majority ](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/7BI0urCWrc4M2ahnVJdaJzyPbdHIGrTX/click?signature=6750e3fda8b0d6f374d7df83c310f0d8ea21da5f&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.fec.gov%2Fdata%2Fcandidate%2FH6NH02261%2F%23total-raised) of Paige's contributions are from individual donors (over 99%) with a small percent of total amount raised coming out of her own pocket (about .008%). Paige won't be bought or influenced. She is not beholden to corporations or special interests. Instead, her dedication is to Medicare for All, making life more affordable for everyday people and making this country a place where everyone can thrive. This campaign is gaining traction. We can win the 9/8 election. But we need your help. The more people who know about Paige, the higher her chances of winning are. Please share this email and this campaign. [Share the Movement](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/7BI0urCWrc4M2ahnVJdaJzyPbdHIGrTX/click?signature=43b169213dc1de9f939a54fa8b8bc3c35b020d12&url=https%3A%2F%2Flinktr.ee%2FPaigeForNH) Together, we will make a real difference this election season. In Solidarity, Team Paige

In a stunning innovation in constitutional avoidance, the _**Constitution State**_ has discovered that you don't need to repeal the Second Amendment if you simply replace it with a loading screen.
HARTFORD, CT -- The State of Connecticut has reportedly solved the thorny problem of gun violence without passing a single new firearms ban, proving that the most powerful weapon in modern governance isn't legislation--it's a broken server.
In a masterclass of bureaucratic Taekwondo, Connecticut officials have allegedly forced every licensed gun dealer to use the state's mandatory background check system, which has been performing with the reliability of a 1998 printer connected to the wrong Wi-Fi.
"We absolutely support the Second Amendment," said Connecticut's theoretical spokesperson, who would answer questions if anyone could get through. "We're just having... technical difficulties. Since... checks notes... four months ago. And next month. And probably forever."
It's the governmental equivalent of being stood up by the person who insisted they really, really wanted to meet you.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4498145e-41f4-422e-9391-ca0a11ff91dc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**The "Technically Legal" Ice Cream Truck**
Here's how the genius works: You can't explicitly ban ice cream without outraging voters. So instead, you mandate that all ice cream sales must pass through a single state-run freezer. Then--whoops--you accidentally unplug the freezer. The Constitution doesn't mention a right to functioning freezers, now does it?
Gun dealers in Connecticut report that transactions are now stuck in a state-run purgatory, suspended in digital carbonite while buyers and sellers stare awkwardly at each other across the counter, wondering if they should just start bartering in livestock.
"It's brilliant," said one Constitutional scholar we definitely made up. "Connecticut looked at gun bans and thought, 'Too obvious.' Then they looked at background checks and said, 'What if we just... kept those?' But then someone in IT accidentally created a permanent system failure, and suddenly it's not a ban--it's just 'user error.'"
**Bar Economics**
The comparisons is to taking away a bar's credit card machine to put AA out of business. Because of course the bar is still 'open'. You can still walk in, breathe the air, and legally own money. You just can't buy anything, because someone from the government unscrewed the credit card reader and took it to Albany for "routine upgrades."
That's Connecticut logic ®: The right to bear arms remains fully intact, provided you don't need to actually complete a transaction, own ammunition, or exist in a timeframe where the DESPP website loads.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b463fada-9ade-4de0-a543-a8a8a0adb056?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
"I tried to buy a shotgun three weeks ago," said one Connecticut resident, probably. "The dealer submitted my background check on a Tuesday. When the system finally responded, it was spring. My daughter had graduated college. I had developed a gluten sensitivity." "I got mugged in New Haven."
**The DMV Model, But Make It Deadly**
It's worth noting that states have long understood this principle with the DMV: Why ban driving when you can simply ensure the line moves slower than geological time? The genius of the DMV model is that citizens get so exhausted that many voluntarily give up the right entirely, deciding instead to live as hermits and trade car keys for goats, four wheels for e-bikes.
Connecticut has simply applied that user-hostile design philosophy to a Constitutional right. It's the bureaucratic equivalent of making someone run a marathon where the finish line moves backward every time you get close, and also all the water stations just show you a "404 Error."
"Is this intentional?" asked a constitutional law professor from an adjacent state that shall remain nameless (let's call it "the sensible one"). "Well, intent is notoriously hard to prove. But if I told my plumber my toilet was broken four months ago and he kept saying he was 'upgrading the pipes,' and then I found out he was secretly pro out house and a toilet abolitionist... I'd probably start connecting dots."
**A Right By Any Other Name Is Not a Right**
The cornerstone of this satirical but legally appalling situation is the distinction between de jure and de facto. Connecticut has not banned firearms, which is wonderful news for anyone who wants to take a photograph of their Second Amendment right and frame it, use it as a decorative coaster, or simply remember fondly the days when rights came with functionality.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/bc91fc1e-a8d4-45a9-8cf7-4c7ecf76c7ea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
It's like having a gym membership to a building with no doors. You still have the membership. The membership is real. It's just not unusable, and the state owns the only set of keys.
"Maybe they'll fix it next week," said one optimistic dealer. "And maybe the Winchester 1873 will come back in stock. And maybe pigs will apply for concealed carry permits." He was laughing, but it was the kind of laugh that comes with a side of nervous eye twitch when payroll is due.
**The Department of Redundancy Department**
For those keeping score, Connecticut is a "point-of-contact" state, meaning dealers cannot simply call the federal NICS office like dealers in freer states. No, no--Connecticut needs to run it through its special system. The state system. The special, magical, apparently cursed state system that exists for... reasons. Reasons that definitely have nothing to do with creating an additional layer of control that can be tightened, loosened, or simply unplugged depending on the political weather.
It's the administrative embodiment of a parent saying, "I'm not saying you can't go to the party, I'm just saying we need to talk about your grades for the next seventy-two hours."
Should any Connecticut residents actually wish to exercise their Second Amendment rights, state officials recommend patience, meditation, and perhaps reincarnating in a state where IT infrastructure is treated with the same urgency as potholes.
Because nothing says "constitutional governance" quite like a digital loading bar that replaces due process with a rainbow wheel of eternal delay. Did I mention it's the _**Constitution State**_?
\---
Legal Disclaimer: This article is satirical. The Second Amendment is real. Connecticut's alleged commitment to making it accessible appears to exist primarily in the theoretical realm, alongside unicorns, functional government websites, and the belief that the phrase "we're working on it" and "we're here to help" are ever uttered in good faith.

If you’ve ever pulled a 53-foot trailer through a blinding rainstorm, you know two things: you don’t panic, and you don’t let off the gas. Right now, this Georgia Senate race is in an absolute dead heat. Neck-and-neck. A complete dogfight. subject: This is more than just a number on a whiteboard
body:
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=1825%2E1086043%2EcFp3RV)
Peter, I want to share why setting goals matters to our campaign.
When we set a fundraising target, it isn’t just a number on a whiteboard.
**It’s a plan** -- a way to help sustain our work, fight back against Trump’s attacks on our progress, and make sure Dan Cox and his MAGA allies don’t get to undo it in November.
Every dollar we raise brings us closer to a Maryland where no one is left behind. _When we hit our goal together, it shows the strength of this movement._
**[That’s why we’re setting a $50,000 end-of-month goal for our re-election campaign to hit before August 31st. Can you make a donation of any amount today to help us close that gap?](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260826-2.ho6mPQ&refcode=em-20260826-2&t=2&akid=1825%2E1086043%2EcFp3RV)**

body:
Last month’s Weekend of Action was Ground Truth’s biggest weekend yet, and this time, we’re going even bigger.
#
Hi there,
Z here, Voter Contact Director at Swing Left! I wanted to reach out with some exciting news:
**Ground Truth volunteers have now officially had 15,000 substantive conversations with voters this cycle!** That is no small feat. Our conversations with voters average up to 9-10 minutes long, giving volunteers the time to actually listen to voters and gather the detailed, rich insights that campaigns can use to sharpen their messaging, connect with voters more effectively, and win.
But we have a lot of work to do to hit our goal of having 500,000 conversations by Election Day. Over the next few weeks, this work is going to multiply, and if you want to have an impact to help Democrats win this November, **we need your help now** —starting with our upcoming Weekend of Action this Saturday and Sunday, August 29th and 30th.
Last month’s Weekend of Action was Ground Truth’s biggest weekend yet, and this time, we’re going even bigger. We want to hold 50 Ground Truth canvasses and 10 virtual phone banks to have an additional 3,500 conversations in just two days as we scale up this work.
**Right now we have 43 canvasses confirmed, and we still need more volunteers to help us make them a success:**
[](https://act.swingleft.org/go/2308?utm_source=em20260826-2581&t=1&akid=2581%2E1562180%2E3ly572)
If you’d like to be a part of it, there are two different ways to take action:
1. [**You can join a canvass near you to talk with voters in the swing districts and states we need to win this November.**](https://act.swingleft.org/go/2308?utm_source=em20260826-2581&t=2&akid=2581%2E1562180%2E3ly572)

2. [**Or you can make calls from the comfort of your home to connect with voters in high-stakes districts nationwide.**](https://act.swingleft.org/go/499?utm_source=em20260826-2581&t=3&akid=2581%2E1562180%2E3ly572)

With less than 10 weeks until Election Day, every conversation we have now helps build the relationships and organizing power we’ll need to help Democrats flip the House and Senate. So please join us this weekend in whatever way works best for you!
Z Mooney
Voter Contact Director, Swing Left

**Since 2017, Swing Left has channeled the energy of grassroots volunteers and donors to elect Democrats, up and down the ballot, focusing on the most competitive races that can swing the national balance of power.** Right now, Swing Left is investing in grassroots organizing in key swing districts and initiatives across the country to flip the House and win the Senate and critical states in 2026. [**If you’d like to help support our work, you can make a donation using this link.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_sl_footer?refcode=em20260826-2&t=4&refcode2=2581_1562180_3ly572&akid=2581%2E1562180%2E3ly572)

Less than 48 hours after a Supreme Court ruling opened the door to Trump’s attempt to make it harder to vote, I’ve filed a new lawsuit to protect mail-in voting ahead of the midterm elections.

**[If that’s all you need to hear, rush a donation right now to power our work. Your support funds each and every one of these critical lawsuits to hold Trump and his administration accountable.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137986563/642590441/2110272206?refcode=260826em_rb_vbmlawsuit&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MTI2MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxNGRiZDExYi05NGExLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=JsEjmqx6MYgCKjmjmVl63ovXHxdV4eTffjZxJ8TND04=)****

_First,_ Trump issued an illegal Executive Order that directed the USPS to send mail-in ballots only to voters on a list of eligible mail voters provided by the states.
_Then_ , the USPS adopted an illegal rule to implement that order and compile a list of enrolled mail voters.

_Now_ , under the current USPS rules, if an eligible voter isn’t on the federal government’s official voter list, or if a ballot doesn’t meet specific new requirements, USPS can refuse to deliver a ballot to an eligible voter.

**Let me clear: it is against the law for USPS to discriminate among users of the mail and reject mail. The Constitution gives states — not the Postal Service or the President — the authority to regulate elections, period. So today, I’ve filed a lawsuit — my 86th against the Trump administration since he was inaugurated last year — challenging this unlawful USPS rule that restricts voting. **

The right to vote is what our nation was founded on, and it is the cornerstone of a functioning democracy. Now, Donald Trump is so terrified of losing the midterms that he is taking unprecedented measures to restrict that right and interfere with our elections — but this fight is far from over.

_The facts and the law are on our side, and we will never stop fighting to protect the constitutional right to vote for every single Californian and American._

Hi team! It's me, Winnie!
Today is National Dog Day, so I'm taking a break from playing with my stuffed squirrels to let you in on a little secret.
I have a trick I use when I want dinner early. I beg my mom, Rachel. Usually she tells me it's not time yet.
But if my sister Susie joins me? Different story.
**We 've learned that if we organize and beg together, we can make real change and get fed a little early.**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/cf17918b-c96d-4c26-a13c-a75120be7630?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
My mom says that the same thing is true in politics.
**She 's working really hard to give our part of PA the representation we deserve, but she can't do it alone.**
She needs help from me and Susie, who provide kisses and cuddles after a long day on the campaign trail. And she needs help from you, too.
**[Will you chip in $20, $10, or whatever you can today to help mom win this really important race?](https://substack.com/redirect/cf17918b-c96d-4c26-a13c-a75120be7630?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

If two dogs can move dinner up by 20 minutes, imagine what all of us can do together.
Thanks for your support. Time for a nap!
- Winnie 🐾

When Vice President J.D. Vance paid his second visit to Maine, he was there in Brewer to bang the drum for Republican U.S. Senator Susan Collins' Senate race and ME-CD2 frontrunner Gov. Paul LePage - two household names vying for offices that could well determine whether President Donald Trump has a cooperative GOP Congress for his final two years in office.
Yet for Vance, tapped by President Trump to head the White House Fraud Task Force amid a nationally reckoning over welfare fraud committed disproportionately by noncitizens and immigrants, one question lingered in the minds of even the most diehard MAGA fans: When will the fraudsters get arrested? When will the thieves get justice?
The question is all the more pressing because of the brazenness of the fraud, with dozens of newly minted MaineCare businesses rapidly rising to tens of millions in annual billing as their CEOs acquire high-end homes and luxury vehicles. While some of these Medicaid moguls have had their funding cut off, dozens more continue to bill taxpayers with impunity, and no one has even hinted that jail time and restitution might be in the picture.
Detailed Medicaid data, released by the Trump Administration in January, tells a story of explosive cost growth in the very programs where fraud allegations are piling up -- cost growth that should have been glaringly obvious to any government official tasked with protecting the integrity of public benefit programs.
Home health care spending in Maine went from $42.6M in 2018 to $116M in 2024 -- an increase of 175 percent -- while the number of Mainers getting "home care" went from 2,488 to 3,192, an increase of just 28 percent. MaineCare has paid out $512.5 million during this period to provide help with daily household activities for fewer than 3,200 people.
Autism groups homes of also exploded in growth. From 2019 to 2024, according to federal data, 27 new autism group home companies were founded in Maine, at a cost of $473 million. Even more alarming, these MaineCare start-ups are billing at a mathematically improbable rate over the autism care providers that existed in the state prior to 2019.
Federal data shows that Maine had 48 firms billing under the T2016 code for autism residential services in 2018, for an annual total of $250.5 million. That works out to about $12,380 per month per patient. From 2018, as the flood of new group home operators entered the scene, nine of the older providers went out of business. The new group home operators proceeded to out-bill the older companies on a per-client basis by 32-47 percent, depending on the year. While the incumbent providers charged a monthly average of $19,896 per client in 2024, the 27 new firms averaged $28,450 per beneficiary per month. One of the most expensive of the new firms averaged $39,235 per client per month -- or $470,820 annually for a single patient.

So when the fraud is mathematically screaming out of the databases, why can't state or federal investigators stop the fraudsters from looting the treasury in a poor state like Maine?
A source in the District of Maine's U.S. Attorney Office, who requested anonymity to speak openly about challenges facing the Trump Administration's effort to combat systemic welfare fraud and foreign criminal cartels, said the volume of potential fraud cases and cases related to transnational criminal organizations has far exceeded the small office's capacity to properly investigate.
Compounding the problem is former U.S. Attorney Darcie McElwee, an ally of Democratic Gov. Janet Mills who was appointed by President Joe Biden, refused to prosecute most drug and welfare fraud cases, meaning President Donald Trump's U.S. Attorney, Andrew Benson, inherited almost no major fraud cases that were near completion.
"We're starting from scratch with an understaffed office, a state Attorney General who has prosecuted no new cases of fraud, and a state government that has turned a blind eye to unprecedented levels of welfare fraud and organized crime for eight years," the source said.
The source said there were at least seven major welfare fraud investigations in the District of Maine that are on hold due to a lack of resources and manpower.
"We could quintuple the number of lawyers and investigators working fraud and racketeering cases and everyone would still be working overtime," the source said.
Conditions in the U.S. Attorney's office align with what's known publicly and what sources have told the Maine Wire about the lack of effort by Maine Attorney General Aaron Frey and the Department of Health and Human Services to investigate and prosecute major Medicaid and Food Stamp fraud cases.
[Share The Robinson Report](https://substack..h4sP5_nUgvb7NiejGjV60qZWPSD6csNMFIQfTx-kuOY?)
McElwee's record on Medicaid fraud was anemic, relying primarily on cases that preceded her appointment. Most of the Medicaid fraud cases she handled involved individuals lying about their income to obtain benefits, as opposed to the multi-million dollar provider-side fraud cases now surfacing in places like Minnesota, California, New York, and Maine.
The largest provider case McElwee handled involved a therapist in Corinna who was given three years probation, a $2,500 fine, and ordered to pay $13,087.62 in restitution.
Separate from the situation in the U.S. Attorney's office, two individuals familiar with the state of Maine's fraud investigations under the Mills administration told the Maine Wire about a fraud investigation that exemplifies how DHHS and left-wing district attorneys have turned a blind eye to brazen benefits theft. Both individuals spoke on the condition of anonymity out of fear of retaliation by government agencies.
Together, they told the story of how Antoine R. Bikamba, 53, flitted around the small world of left-wing Portland area non-profits, allegedly stole multiple debit cards and EBT cards belonging to clients, was effectively caught red-handed but never prosecuted and instead went on to start an autism company that has billed MaineCare nearly $8 million.
Bikamba, according to both sources as well as other public records, worked for Preble Street as a caseworker, then at Spurwink as a Direct Support Professional (DSP), for the Greater Portland Immigrant Welcome Center board, and then for Shalom House.
During his time working for the Shalom House, the sources said, Bikamba was subcontracting for the Portland Housing Authority (PHA). During this time, his contract was terminated after he was accused of stealing and using a clients debit card and multiple EBT cards.
"He stole a Portland Housing Authority client's debit card and made unauthorized transactions with that client's debit card at an ATM," one source said. "Portland Housing Authority told that client that they needed to file a police report... You're telling me that you're telling a client to go file a police report when they have freaking case managers? Because they are an individual that is not capable of taking care of themselves."
The theft was never reported to the Portland Police Department.
A subsequent investigation into the use of an EBT card by an individual who had died led once again to Bikamba.
"Lo and behold, someone was also calling into the department, pretending to be the client at least 10 times after they had passed to follow up on their SNAP benefits, and when we did a reverse search on the phone number that was calling, it came back to Antoine Bikamba's phone number," the source said.
Further investigation found that Bikamba had attempted to call Maine DHHS regarding the EBT card benefits of multiple other individuals, the sources said.
That included the EBT card of an individual who was found wandering the streets of Portland in July of 2020 in a state of apparent dementia. The individual, a non-English speaking illegal alien from an unknown African country, was hospitalized at taxpayer expense for more than a year.
Eventually, Maine's Office of Aging and Disability Services (OADS) took custody of that individual, whose medical condition required 24/7 intensive long-term care, and secured a no-bid contract worth more than $800,000 to put them in a long-term care facility in Oakland. [That no-bid contract was the subject of a previous Maine Wire report last year.](https://substack.com/redirect/dfc2ff1a-d234-4eec-aee5-eb41f643afc9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
According to the sources, the entire investigation into Bikamba's alleged welfare fraud and identity theft were given to Cumberland County District Attorney Jackie Sartoris, a far left progressive who won office in 2022 thanks to $385,000 in campaign spending from George Soros-affiliated political groups.
"It was gift wrapped and packaged off to Jackie Sartoris's office, and the last we were aware, it was still sitting there," the source said.
Sartoris's office refused to respond to multiple inquiries about the status of Bikamba's case.
Bikamba, in a phone interview, said he was unaware of any case involving him and denied ever having used another person's EBT card benefits.
Multiple inquiries to the Maine DHHS regarding Bikamba went unanswered.

## Pastor Tony Moves from EBT Cards to Autism Group Homes
Bikamba, a self-described Rwandan migrant who sometimes goes by Pastor Tony, arrived in Maine in 2008. didn't have to scrounge for EBT cards for long. While the prosecution referral was collecting dust on Sartoris's desk, Bikamba was busy forming Green Leaf Residential Care, LLC, a multi-million-dollar MaineCare provider that operates autism group homes throughout Maine.
From 2022 to 2025, Bikamba collected $6.8 million in MaineCare payments, according to records obtained under the Freedom of Access Act.
In a phone interview, Bikamba acknowledged running the autism group homes, but he denied that he ever brought any disabled migrants to the state and denied ever improperly using another individual's EBT card.
"I'm not aware of that," he said.
Although Bikamba began billing MaineCare in 2022, state records show that his company was not licensed to provide residential care until Oct. 2025. State records show that Green Leaf operates group homes on Garland Road and Cardinal Way in Bangor, Hotel Road in Auburn, Holyoke Street in Brewer, and Hallowell Road in Durham. The same records show that Green Leaf underwent what DHHS refers to as a "desk review," wherein a government employee inspects the company over the telephone, and was found to have no deficiencies.
If Bikamba's wheels are any indication, business is booming.
Public records show he owns a 2016 Mercedes GLC and a 2021 Mercedes GLE. Prior to that he owned a BMW X5, an Audi Q7, and an Audi Q5. But before he tapped into the MaineCare cash flow, Bikamba relied on more humble wheels - a 2008 Nissan Rogue that he purchased in 2012 with Jocelyne Ininhazwe, the former CEO of the now-defunct Paradise Residential Services, an autism group home company that bills the same exact program as Green Leaf Residential.
While Green Leaf remains in business, Paradise's operations were terminated on an emergency basis earlier this year after state inspectors found serious deficiencies that threatened the health and well-being of their clients.
[[RELATED: Paradise Lost: How African Migrants Made Millions on Filthy Medicaid Homes Where Disabled Mainers Were Abused...]](https://substack.com/redirect/777bc68a-5348-4982-99b6-dc342de78512?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
From 2022 to 2026, Paradise managed to bill nearly $25 million.
Like Bikamba, Ininahazwe is an immigrant from Central Africa and, like Bikamba, she's a fan of German luxury vehicles, with both her and her son owning a Mercedes E-Series and a Mercedes G-Wagon.
In the phone interview, Bikamba said he and Ininahazwe are just friends, and he declined to comment on the remarkable coincidence that both of them struck it rich in Maine's autism group home industry.
Green Leaf Residential Care and Paradise Residential Services are just two examples of "New Mainers" running start-up MaineCare businesses that exploded in cost under the Mills administration with next to no scrutiny from regulators until the Trump administration and CMS Administrator Oz began bearing down on the state.
In response to an April Freedom of Access Act request for records related to Ininahazwe, Bikamba, and several of their associates in the autism group home industry, DHHS asked __ the _Maine Wire_ to pay more than $40,000 for records that would take more than one year to deliver.
"Given the scope of your request, the Department's initial, good faith, non-binding, estimate to retrieve, compile, and review the responsive records that are subject to FOAA will be $41,085.50 for 1,645.42 hours of work in which the estimated time to be completed in 411 days from the time a check is received," the agency said.

## Maine's Fraud Squad AWOL
Although the Maine DHHS claims that it refers cases of suspected fraud to the Attorney General's office, there's little evidence that Attorney General Aaron Frey treats the theft of millions of taxpayer dollars -- or the abuse and neglect of disabled Mainers -- with the same seriousness and alacrity that he does amicus briefs for [transvestites](https://substack.com/redirect/a387499a-f34d-4816-b021-37cd72fab3c2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in West Virginia or [symbolic lawsuits](https://substack.com/redirect/c3f3e21c-2f9b-4225-8f37-76b43d953990?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) against Exxon-Mobil.
Frey, a former Democratic lawmaker, was tapped by Democratic lawmakers to serve as AG in 2018. Since that time, his office has assisted with just three cases of Medicaid fraud -- and all of them related to the same federal conspiracy case that was investigated and built two years before he came into office.
That case, which resulted in guilty pleas from Abdirashid Ahmed, Garat Osman, and Nancy Ludwig, was spearheaded by the FBI and the Department of Homeland Security begining in 2016, when both President Donald Trump and Gov. Paul LePage were in office.
In a March letter to Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz, the Mills Administration said that Maine DHHS made four criminal referrals to the AG's office in 2021 -- all of which were declined. From 2022 to 2025, DHHS referred 18 cases for criminal prosecution but, as of Feb. 2026, only one resulted in a guilty plea.
Apart from cases that began before he took the job, there's no public record of Frey pursuing a single welfare or MaineCare provider fraud case -- even as total spending and fraudulent spending ballooned on his watch.
In the high-profile instance of Gateway Community Services, a migrant services agency that has been credible accused of defrauding the state as it billed roughly $5 million per year the entire time Frey was in office, the Attorney General actually awarded Gateway a $400,000 opioid grant _after_ whistleblower allegations were published by The Maine Wire and replayed throughout national media.
To date, Frey has announce no charges against anyone involved in Gateway's alleged fraud scheme, and Somali-American founder Abdullahi Ali has absconded to Kenya.
Although Mills initially brushed off Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz's critical audits of Maine's Medicaid mismanagement as political attacks, behind the scenes she and her allies were scrambling to create some semblance of fraud enforcement.
In August, following Administrator Oz's interview with The Maine Wire, DHHS issued a press release touting its enforcement actions, the majority of which involved canceling the provider agreements of businesses that never billed MaineCare in the first place.
Of the providers suspended by Mills and her DHHS Commissioner Sara Gagne-Holmes, only seven were actively billing MaineCare and account for more than $138 million in taxpayer spending, according to state and federal payment records.
Records released by the Mills administration revealed that, on the same day Mills blasted Oz as a "TV doctor," her administration issued the termination letters to Paradise Residential Services and Beyond Residential Care.
Felix R. Hagenimana, the founder of [Beyond Residential Care](https://substack.com/redirect/1245e6c5-ff55-4ba7-9f9e-56909bff6808?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), has also been accused by the Maine State Bar Association of using ChatGPT to file bogus asylum claims for nearly 1,500 central African illegal aliens - the same population from which most of the African-owned autism firms draw their non-English-speaking employees. Hagenimana, himself a Rwandan migrant, has denied the allegations in the Maine Bar complaint.
[[RELATED: Rwandan Immigration Lawyer Faces Bar Complaint After $13M Autism MaineCare Biz Axed...]](https://substack.com/redirect/1245e6c5-ff55-4ba7-9f9e-56909bff6808?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The same release touted by the Mills administration also include Gateway, which was suspended almost a year ago.
In all seven of the cases the Mills administration as pointed to as evidence of their tough stance on fraud, there have been no arrests, no orders of restitution, and no indications that taxpayers will ever be repaid.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/677474c9-8cb5-4c21-95e3-6c16ac906c05?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Beyond the financial fraud, state investigators described harrowing conditions of neglect, abuse, and rights violations at the group homes controlled by the two companies.
In a termination letter obtained under a Freedom of Access Act request, state officials said the two autism residential care providers were found violating the disability rights of autistic Mainers and putting their lives in immediate jeopardy, with homes described as filthy, dangerous, and understaffed.
In light of the U.S. Attorney of Maine's apparent lack of resources to confront widespread fraud within the home health care sector, but also the residential autism care industry, it's worth asking how many other lives are currently in jeopardy because the state hasn't effectively ensured that multi-million dollar Medicaid businesses are protecting Maine's disabled population.
In a comment to the Maine Wire, Oz reiterated his commitment to snuffing out fraud in the Pine Tree State.
"Fraud doesn't just waste taxpayer dollars -- it erodes trust in the programs millions of Americans rely on," said Oz.

Sources say Maine's depleted and partisan justice system has been AWOL for more than four years when it comes to fighting systemic Medicaid fraud. Aug 26 | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- When Vice President J.D. Vance paid his second visit to Maine, he was there in Brewer to bang the drum for Republican U.S. Senator Susan Collins' Senate race and ME-CD2 frontrunner Gov. Paul LePage - two household names vying for offices that could well determine whether President Donald Trump has a cooperative GOP Congress for his final two years in office. Yet for Vance, tapped by President Trump to head the White House Fraud Task Force amid a nationally reckoning over welfare fraud committed disproportionately by noncitizens and immigrants, one question lingered in the minds of even the most diehard MAGA fans: When will the fraudsters get arrested? When will the thieves get justice? The question is all the more pressing because of the brazenness of the fraud, with dozens of newly minted MaineCare businesses rapidly rising to tens of millions in annual billing as their CEOs acquire high-end homes and luxury vehicles. While some of these Medicaid moguls have had their funding cut off, dozens more continue to bill taxpayers with impunity, and no one has even hinted that jail time and restitution might be in the picture. Detailed Medicaid data, released by the Trump Administration in January, tells a story of explosive cost growth in the very programs where fraud allegations are piling up -- cost growth that should have been glaringly obvious to any government official tasked with protecting the integrity of public benefit programs. Home health care spending in Maine went from $42.6M in 2018 to $116M in 2024 -- an increase of 175 percent -- while the number of Mainers getting "home care" went from 2,488 to 3,192, an increase of just 28 percent. MaineCare has paid out $512.5 million during this period to provide help with daily household activities for fewer than 3,200 people. Autism groups homes of also exploded in growth. From 2019 to 2024, according to federal data, 27 new autism group home companies were founded in Maine, at a cost of $473 million. Even more alarming, these MaineCare start-ups are billing at a mathematically improbable rate over the autism care providers that existed in the state prior to 2019. Federal data shows that Maine had 48 firms billing under the T2016 code for autism residential services in 2018, for an annual total of $250.5 million. That works out to about $12,380 per month per patient. From 2018, as the flood of new group home operators entered the scene, nine of the older providers went out of business. The new group home operators proceeded to out-bill the older companies on a per-client basis by 32-47 percent, depending on the year. While the incumbent providers charged a monthly average of $19,896 per client in 2024, the 27 new firms averaged $28,450 per beneficiary per month. One of the most expensive of the new firms averaged $39,235 per client per month -- or $470,820 annually for a single patient. This Substack is doesn't get Medicaid funding. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber. | | | | | | | ---|---|--- | Aug 10 | So when the fraud is mathematically screaming out of the databases, why can't state or federal investigators stop the fraudsters from looting the treasury in a poor state like Maine? A source in the District of Maine's U.S. Attorney Office, who requested anonymity to speak openly about challenges facing the Trump Administration's effort to combat systemic welfare fraud and foreign criminal cartels, said the volume of potential fraud cases and cases related to transnational criminal organizations has far exceeded the small office's capacity to properly investigate. Compounding the problem is former U.S. Attorney Darcie McElwee, an ally of Democratic Gov. Janet Mills who was appointed by President Joe Biden, refused to prosecute most drug and welfare fraud cases, meaning President Donald Trump's U.S. Attorney, Andrew Benson, inherited almost no major fraud cases that were near completion. "We're starting from scratch with an understaffed office, a state Attorney General who has prosecuted no new cases of fraud, and a state government that has turned a blind eye to unprecedented levels of welfare fraud and organized crime for eight years," the source said. The source said there were at least seven major welfare fraud investigations in the District of Maine that are on hold due to a lack of resources and manpower. "We could quintuple the number of lawyers and investigators working fraud and racketeering cases and everyone would still be working overtime," the source said. Conditions in the U.S. Attorney's office align with what's known publicly and what sources have told the Maine Wire about the lack of effort by Maine Attorney General Aaron Frey and the Department of Health and Human Services to investigate and prosecute major Medicaid and Food Stamp fraud cases. ? McElwee's record on Medicaid fraud was anemic, relying primarily on cases that preceded her appointment. Most of the Medicaid fraud cases she handled involved individuals lying about their income to obtain benefits, as opposed to the multi-million dollar provider-side fraud cases now surfacing in places like Minnesota, California, New York, and Maine. The largest provider case McElwee handled involved a therapist in Corinna who was given three years probation, a $2,500 fine, and ordered to pay $13,087.62 in restitution. Separate from the situation in the U.S. Attorney's office, two individuals familiar with the state of Maine's fraud investigations under the Mills administration told the Maine Wire about a fraud investigation that exemplifies how DHHS and left-wing district attorneys have turned a blind eye to brazen benefits theft. Both individuals spoke on the condition of anonymity out of fear of retaliation by government agencies. Together, they told the story of how Antoine R. Bikamba, 53, flitted around the small world of left-wing Portland area non-profits, allegedly stole multiple debit cards and EBT cards belonging to clients, was effectively caught red-handed but never prosecuted and instead went on to start an autism company that has billed MaineCare nearly $8 million. Bikamba, according to both sources as well as other public records, worked for Preble Street as a caseworker, then at Spurwink as a Direct Support Professional (DSP), for the Greater Portland Immigrant Welcome Center board, and then for Shalom House. During his time working for the Shalom House, the sources said, Bikamba was subcontracting for the Portland Housing Authority (PHA). During this time, his contract was terminated after he was accused of stealing and using a clients debit card and multiple EBT cards. "He stole a Portland Housing Authority client's debit card and made unauthorized transactions with that client's debit card at an ATM," one source said. "Portland Housing Authority told that client that they needed to file a police report... You're telling me that you're telling a client to go file a police report when they have freaking case managers? Because they are an individual that is not capable of taking care of themselves." The theft was never reported to the Portland Police Department. A subsequent investigation into the use of an EBT card by an individual who had died led once again to Bikamba. "Lo and behold, someone was also calling into the department, pretending to be the client at least 10 times after they had passed to follow up on their SNAP benefits, and when we did a reverse search on the phone number that was calling, it came back to Antoine Bikamba's phone number," the source said. Further investigation found that Bikamba had attempted to call Maine DHHS regarding the EBT card benefits of multiple other individuals, the sources said. That included the EBT card of an individual who was found wandering the streets of Portland in July of 2020 in a state of apparent dementia. The individual, a non-English speaking illegal alien from an unknown African country, was hospitalized at taxpayer expense for more than a year. Eventually, Maine's Office of Aging and Disability Services (OADS) took custody of that individual, whose medical condition required 24/7 intensive long-term care, and secured a no-bid contract worth more than $800,000 to put them in a long-term care facility in Oakland. According to the sources, the entire investigation into Bikamba's alleged welfare fraud and identity theft were given to Cumberland County District Attorney Jackie Sartoris, a far left progressive who won office in 2022 thanks to $385,000 in campaign spending from George Soros-affiliated political groups. "It was gift wrapped and packaged off to Jackie Sartoris's office, and the last we were aware, it was still sitting there," the source said. Sartoris's office refused to respond to multiple inquiries about the status of Bikamba's case. Bikamba, in a phone interview, said he was unaware of any case involving him and denied ever having used another person's EBT card benefits. Multiple inquiries to the Maine DHHS regarding Bikamba went unanswered. Pastor Tony Moves from EBT Cards to Autism Group Homes Bikamba, a self-described Rwandan migrant who sometimes goes by Pastor Tony, arrived in Maine in 2008. didn't have to scrounge for EBT cards for long. While the prosecution referral was collecting dust on Sartoris's desk, Bikamba was busy forming Green Leaf Residential Care, LLC, a multi-million-dollar MaineCare provider that operates autism group homes throughout Maine. From 2022 to 2025, Bikamba collected $6.8 million in MaineCare payments, according to records obtained under the Freedom of Access Act. In a phone interview, Bikamba acknowledged running the autism group homes, but he denied that he ever brought any disabled migrants to the state and denied ever improperly using another individual's EBT card. "I'm not aware of that," he said. Although Bikamba began billing MaineCare in 2022, state records show that his company was not licensed to provide residential care until Oct. 2025. State records show that Green Leaf operates group homes on Garland Road and Cardinal Way in Bangor, Hotel Road in Auburn, Holyoke Street in Brewer, and Hallowell Road in Durham. The same records show that Green Leaf underwent what DHHS refers to as a "desk review," wherein a government employee inspects the company over the telephone, and was found to have no deficiencies. If Bikamba's wheels are any indication, business is booming. Public records show he owns a 2016 Mercedes GLC and a 2021 Mercedes GLE. Prior to that he owned a BMW X5, an Audi Q7, and an Audi Q5. But before he tapped into the MaineCare cash flow, Bikamba relied on more humble wheels - a 2008 Nissan Rogue that he purchased in 2012 with Jocelyne Ininhazwe, the former CEO of the now-defunct Paradise Residential Services, an autism group home company that bills the same exact program as Green Leaf Residential. While Green Leaf remains in business, Paradise's operations were terminated on an emergency basis earlier this year after state inspectors found serious deficiencies that threatened the health and well-being of their clients. [[RELATED: Paradise Lost: How African Migrants Made Millions on Filthy Medicaid Homes Where Disabled Mainers Were Abused...]]() From 2022 to 2026, Paradise managed to bill nearly $25 million. Like Bikamba, Ininahazwe is an immigrant from Central Africa and, like Bikamba, she's a fan of German luxury vehicles, with both her and her son owning a Mercedes E-Series and a Mercedes G-Wagon. In the phone interview, Bikamba said he and Ininahazwe are just friends, and he declined to comment on the remarkable coincidence that both of them struck it rich in Maine's autism group home industry. Green Leaf Residential Care and Paradise Residential Services are just two examples of "New Mainers" running start-up MaineCare businesses that exploded in cost under the Mills administration with next to no scrutiny from regulators until the Trump administration and CMS Administrator Oz began bearing down on the state. In response to an April Freedom of Access Act request for records related to Ininahazwe, Bikamba, and several of their associates in the autism group home industry, DHHS asked the Maine Wire to pay more than $40,000 for records that would take more than one year to deliver. "Given the scope of your request, the Department's initial, good faith, non-binding, estimate to retrieve, compile, and review the responsive records that are subject to FOAA will be $41,085.50 for 1,645.42 hours of work in which the estimated time to be completed in 411 days from the time a check is received," the agency said. | | | | ---|---|--- | Aug 10 | Maine's Fraud Squad AWOL Although the Maine DHHS claims that it refers cases of suspected fraud to the Attorney General's office, there's little evidence that Attorney General Aaron Frey treats the theft of millions of taxpayer dollars -- or the abuse and neglect of disabled Mainers -- with the same seriousness and alacrity that he does amicus briefs for in West Virginia or against Exxon-Mobil. Frey, a former Democratic lawmaker, was tapped by Democratic lawmakers to serve as AG in 2018. Since that time, his office has assisted with just three cases of Medicaid fraud -- and all of them related to the same federal conspiracy case that was investigated and built two years before he came into office. That case, which resulted in guilty pleas from Abdirashid Ahmed, Garat Osman, and Nancy Ludwig, was spearheaded by the FBI and the Department of Homeland Security begining in 2016, when both President Donald Trump and Gov. Paul LePage were in office. In a March letter to Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz, the Mills Administration said that Maine DHHS made four criminal referrals to the AG's office in 2021 -- all of which were declined. From 2022 to 2025, DHHS referred 18 cases for criminal prosecution but, as of Feb. 2026, only one resulted in a guilty plea. Apart from cases that began before he took the job, there's no public record of Frey pursuing a single welfare or MaineCare provider fraud case -- even as total spending and fraudulent spending ballooned on his watch. In the high-profile instance of Gateway Community Services, a migrant services agency that has been credible accused of defrauding the state as it billed roughly $5 million per year the entire time Frey was in office, the Attorney General actually awarded Gateway a $400,000 opioid grant after whistleblower allegations were published by The Maine Wire and replayed throughout national media. To date, Frey has announce no charges against anyone involved in Gateway's alleged fraud scheme, and Somali-American founder Abdullahi Ali has absconded to Kenya. Although Mills initially brushed off Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz's critical audits of Maine's Medicaid mismanagement as political attacks, behind the scenes she and her allies were scrambling to create some semblance of fraud enforcement. In August, following Administrator Oz's interview with The Maine Wire, DHHS issued a press release touting its enforcement actions, the majority of which involved canceling the provider agreements of businesses that never billed MaineCare in the first place. Of the providers suspended by Mills and her DHHS Commissioner Sara Gagne-Holmes, only seven were actively billing MaineCare and account for more than $138 million in taxpayer spending, according to state and federal payment records. Records released by the Mills administration revealed that, on the same day Mills blasted Oz as a "TV doctor," her administration issued the termination letters to Paradise Residential Services and Beyond Residential Care. Felix R. Hagenimana, the founder of , has also been accused by the Maine State Bar Association of using ChatGPT to file bogus asylum claims for nearly 1,500 central African illegal aliens - the same population from which most of the African-owned autism firms draw their non-English-speaking employees. Hagenimana, himself a Rwandan migrant, has denied the allegations in the Maine Bar complaint. [[RELATED: Rwandan Immigration Lawyer Faces Bar Complaint After $13M Autism MaineCare Biz Axed...]]() The same release touted by the Mills administration also include Gateway, which was suspended almost a year ago. In all seven of the cases the Mills administration as pointed to as evidence of their tough stance on fraud, there have been no arrests, no orders of restitution, and no indications that taxpayers will ever be repaid. | | ---|---|--- Beyond the financial fraud, state investigators described harrowing conditions of neglect, abuse, and rights violations at the group homes controlled by the two companies. In a termination letter obtained under a Freedom of Access Act request, state officials said the two autism residential care providers were found violating the disability rights of autistic Mainers and putting their lives in immediate jeopardy, with homes described as filthy, dangerous, and understaffed. In light of the U.S. Attorney of Maine's apparent lack of resources to confront widespread fraud within the home health care sector, but also the residential autism care industry, it's worth asking how many other lives are currently in jeopardy because the state hasn't effectively ensured that multi-million dollar Medicaid businesses are protecting Maine's disabled population. In a comment to the Maine Wire, Oz reiterated his commitment to snuffing out fraud in the Pine Tree State. "Fraud doesn't just waste taxpayer dollars -- it erodes trust in the programs millions of Americans rely on," said Oz. "When credible instances of fraud emerge, taxpayers and beneficiaries deserve to see swift action," he said. "We need all stakeholders including state leaders in Maine to move with urgency and work aggressively with federal partners to root out fraud, protect taxpayer dollars, and ensure Medicaid is there for the people it was meant to serve." disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY VOTEVETS, VOTEVETS
body:
Stars and Stripes exists for the troops. They fight for the First Amendment. They deserve better than propaganda.
#
Peter, it’s time to talk about _Stars and Stripes_.
That’s the military newspaper printed specifically for the troops. It’s existed since 1861 and been in continuous print since the Second World War. It operates underneath the Department of Defense, but has always had its own editorial independence.
As Supreme Allied Commander in World War II, Dwight Eisenhower himself fought for that independence. That set the tone, and in 1980 Congress created an ombudsman position to ensure the paper operates without censorship or influence from the Pentagon.
That independence has been broadly respected under both Republican and Democratic administrations... until this year.
In March, Hegseth banned outside syndicated content and the funny pages. Yes, the comics. The ombudsman protested, and Hegseth fired her. Over the last few weeks _Stars and Stripes_ published original reporting on the conditions aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln. Hegseth wasn’t happy about that, and installed an active-duty Naval public affairs officer as “military deputy” to the publisher to keep him in line.
The publisher announced his retirement in protest, but before he could leave, Hegseth fired him. Hegseth also fired the editor-in-chief and a reporter who covered the Lincoln for “insubordination.” This level of intervention is absolutely unprecedented in the history of the paper.
_Stars and Stripes_ exists for the troops. They fight for the First Amendment. They deserve better than propaganda.
It’s time for Congress to do their damn job and conduct serious oversight on this abuse of _Stars and Stripes'_ independence. This paper is congressionally authorized, and Hegseth literally fired the ombudsman Congress created to ensure its independence.
[**It’s time to raise some hell. We’re asking you to sign our petition to save _Stars and Stripes_. Congress won’t do anything until we make them, so we’ve got to make a lot of noise. ### **Tell the AI & Data Center Committee: Support a Moratorium**

#### _The Artificial Intelligence and Data Center Committee meets August 31._
---
| |

— [Join Vern in his efforts to get North Dakota’s leaders to do the right thing. Write to members of the AI and Data Center Committee.](https://us.list-manage.com/mQczd3bWT3Y?e=37dda778f5&c2id=cdbf6368064ed4acbe3dc3fec7c073dc)
---
| | “North Dakota's data center boom is moving fast — faster than the rules meant to protect landowners and rural communities. Right now, it's the Wild West. North Dakotans deserve straight answers about who benefits from decisions being made on their behalf.” -Vern Thompson

* Public officials signing non-disclosure agreements (NDA’s) is just plain wrong and should be banned.
* A one year moratorium would level the playing field, encourage local control and give communities time to do research, give and gather public input, and pass ordinances.

Tell the AI and Data Center Committee to support these two common sense proposals. **Use our quick and easy tool to write to the committee before August 31** ➡️ [https://actionnetwork.org/letters/write-the-ai-committee?source=direct_link&](https://us.list-manage.com/6c6TGxZJWzW?e=37dda778f5&c2id=cdbf6368064ed4acbe3dc3fec7c073dc)

* North Dakota Data Center Overview, with an environmental engineer
* Review of the Responsible Hyperscale Development Framework, with Vern Thompson
* Public comments

Join TOP this coming **Tuesday, September 1, at 9 a.m. outside commissioners court** as we call out this deliberate move to weaken the power of voters of color across Tarrant County. For more details, contact Jet at [**jwashington@organizetexas.org**](mailto:jwashington@organizetexas.org). **Championing Fair Legal Representation in Bexar County ** **Power in numbers: San Antonio TOP members showed up in force at Bexar County Commissioners Court on Tuesday to speak up and advocate for budget funds to protect the county's MAC (Managed Assigned Counsel) program as well as Public Defender’s Office** , better ensuring fair legal representation for county residents, no matter their income. Nearly $2 million in this funding was on the chopping block. An official commissioners court vote is expected in the coming days. Bexar County's MAC goes beyond just legal defense. It provides critical support services, including access to mental health resources and on-site attorneys. This holistic approach aims to reduce unnecessary jail time and yield better outcomes for all involved. To get involved in TOP's Right2Justice campaign efforts, contact Dr. Doshie Piper at [_**dpiper@organizetexas.org**_](mailto:dpiper@organizetexas.org).
**End Non-Safety Traffic Stops + Mass Surveillance in Texas** Every day, thousands of Texans are pulled over for minor, non-safety issues. These stops draw working people into unnecessary police contact with zero public safety benefit. At the same time, Automated License Plate Readers (ALPRs), like Flock Safety, are expanding across our state. They create massive tracking databases that monitor where you drive, work, worship, and seek medical care. **👉🏾 Sign the petition:[Tell Texas officials to end non-safety traffic stops and Flock surveillance.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137987427/642593277/-731476291?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNVE8vMS80NTY0MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkYzA3ODU4My05N2ExLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=mf7ZwZYAhqZHP7b6TL510CaD9EYkUp4_gnBUQVyrz6I=&emci=b4306a1b-81a1-f111-9b33-0022482a9f1d&emdi=dc078583-97a1-f111-9b33-0022482a9f1d&ceid=227997)**

I have never had any desire to be a politician. I am doing this because I am answering President Donald Trump's call to serve and want to stand up for South Carolina and fight for his agenda. Like Lindsey, I am a hard worker with a servant's heart. We grew up in the back of a bar and liquor store, in one room. Our parents worked hard every day to make ends meet - there was no time for sickness and few vacations, because if the doors weren't open, no money was coming in. What I've spent my life doing is serving South Carolina - including running a state agency with 130 employees and a $90 million budget. We turned it from a struggling organization into a national model helping people find work and live independently. We made sure all spending was reasonable, allowable, and necessary. I fought against duplication of services, knowing it wasted taxpayers' dollars. I'm a mother, a grandmother, and a wife, and now South Carolina's first female United States Senator, I know how to bargain shop, and I look for the buy-one-get-one-free sales at the grocery store. I just bought a new pair of shoes to walk around the U.S. Capitol off the clearance rack at the Shoe Warehouse. I cut my own grass with a push mower, and yes, I know how to use a weed eater. # FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
**August 26, 2026**
## DAN COX ACCEPTS OCTOBER 6 MPT DEBATE WITH WES MOORE, CALLS FOR TWO ADDITIONAL DEBATES
**ANNAPOLIS, MD** — Republican gubernatorial nominee Dan Cox today accepted Maryland Public Television's proposed **October 6, 2026 debate with Gov. Wes Moore** and called on Moore to agree to at least two additional debates before Election Day. The MPT debate is proposed as an in-studio, televised forum with questions from a panel of independent reporters and moderators. With mail-in ballots scheduled to begin going out September 21, Cox thanked MPT while arguing Maryland voters should have multiple opportunities to hear directly from both candidates. “I am honored, on behalf of the people of Maryland, to accept the debate with Wes Moore,” Cox said. “But Marylanders deserve more than one debate—and an opportunity to hear from both candidates before and while voting is underway.” Cox challenged Moore to participate in **at least two additional debates** , proposing Maryland colleges and universities as possible hosts, including Bowie State University, Morgan State University, Coppin State University and the University of Maryland. “What is he afraid of? Let's let the people hear from both candidates,” Cox said. “I welcome the opportunity to debate our different visions for Maryland—including my vision of lowering taxes and fees, making Maryland more affordable, reopening and bringing online new electric plants, expanding energy options, lowering crime and building the Key Bridge along with Maryland's bright future.”
### ###

| | | Today, we’re supposed to celebrate Women's Equality Day. But I think we’re all well aware that the state of equality for women in America right now is... not good.

We know just by paying attention to the news and rhetoric coming out of this administration that women’s rights and autonomy are under attack. But we also have solid evidence that women’s equality, which was and still is a fight in progress, is actively waning. Look at last month’s job report: **In July, women accounted for 100% of jobs lost in the U.S. economy. **

_Let that sink in. While men actually gained 9,000 jobs, women lost 32,000. And 165,000 women exited the workforce entirely, all while the number of men in the labor force stayed steady._

This administration wants to tell you the economy is strong. But for who?

The number one reason women leave the workforce is caregiving. And we know exactly how to fix this: universal child care! Republicans in Congress and Donald Trump want to say that we don’t have the money. Well, that’s a lie. It’s always been a policy choice made by people who don't see women's economic participation as a priority.

This administration has spent the last year and a half actively making life harder for women across the board: attacking reproductive rights and bodily autonomy, dismantling diversity programs, making it harder for women to vote, and targeting their livelihoods. Every single one of those is a policy choice — and every single policy you can find laid out in the pages of Project 2025.

**This year’s Women's Equality Day is an urgent call to action to fight back against this administration, and to make sure we don’t cede any more ground in this fight by delivering a giant Blue Wave in the midterms. **

| | Before I ever cast a vote in Congress, I raised my right hand and swore to support and defend the Constitution against all enemies, foreign and domestic. I first took that oath in 1993, as a 17-year-old at the Naval Academy. I took it again as an officer. Again as a commander. And twice more on the floor of the House. Nowhere in that oath does it say “unless it's politically inconvenient.” [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137988450/642596920/-507177811?refcode=EM_BS_LUR_260826_FR_Jan6_A0_na_U1_X1_M1&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDA3OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0NGQwMjllNi05YWExLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=TLQGOD7m8YHtIn2ptRi-BcmShSxVU08DlhG_jr1H5Rw=) Three days after I was sworn in for my second term, I was evacuated from my office because a pipe bomb was found outside. I watched Capitol Police get beaten with flagpoles while the Commander-in-Chief did nothing for 187 minutes. Someone had to put the truth on the record, under oath, in permanent ink. So I did. I joined the January 6th Committee. I was representing one of the most competitive districts in America.
People told me I’d lose my seat in Congress. _They were right._
They also said that it would end my career. **They were wrong.** I have never once regretted the choice. But look where we are now: the plotters walked free. Their enablers run Washington. They continue to deny what I saw with my own eyes that day. That's why I'm not giving up the fight. clean_body: | | Before I ever cast a vote in Congress, I raised my right hand and swore to support and defend the Constitution against all enemies, foreign and domestic. I first took that oath in 1993, as a 17-year-old at the Naval Academy. I took it again as an officer. Again as a commander. And twice more on the floor of the House. Nowhere in that oath does it say “unless it's politically inconvenient.” = Three days after I was sworn in for my second term, I was evacuated from my office because a pipe bomb was found outside. I watched Capitol Police get beaten with flagpoles while the Commander-in-Chief did nothing for 187 minutes. Someone had to put the truth on the record, under oath, in permanent ink. So I did. I joined the January 6th Committee. I was representing one of the most competitive districts in America. People told me I’d lose my seat in Congress. They were right. They also said that it would end my career. They were wrong. I have never once regretted the choice. But look where we are now: the plotters walked free. Their enablers run Washington. clean_body: This is absolutely insane, friend. Thankfully, Florida made a change.| | | Friend – Florida just did something no other state in America has done. Governor Ron DeSantis directed the Department of Children and Families to change our TANF state plan. Cash assistance is now banned for spending on inappropriate and luxury items like: ❌ Drugs, tobacco, and vaping products❌ Porn❌ Psychic services ❌ Video games and theme park tickets❌ Tattoos and spa visits Friend, TANF money exists to help struggling families cover food, housing, and basic necessities. It was never supposed to be a blank check. Florida already blocks EBT purchases at casinos, gambling facilities, and adult entertainment venues. Now the state is going further, working with our EBT vendor to block these purchases at the transaction level, the same standard already used to stop benefits from funding soda, candy, and junk food. This is common sense. This is accountability. And it's exactly the kind of reform the Left will attack... because they'd rather defend a broken system than fix one. Florida became #1 by doing what other states are too afraid to do. Conservative leaders, from the Governor's office to the legislature, built this success. They need our support to defend it. A controversial initiative launched by Obama—and handsomely funded
under Biden—to end a fabricated pandemic of “diaper disparity”
by providing needy families with government-subsidized diapers is
quietly being kept alive by the Trump administration. It is known as
Diaper Distribution Demonstration and Research Pilot (DDDRP) and it is
funded by a Health and Human Services (HHS) division known as
Administration for Children and Families (ACF) Office of Community
Services (OCS). Under both Obama and Biden, the questionable program
received a steady stream of taxpayer dollars, and the money continues
flowing under Trump albeit with less fanfare and press releases in an
apparent effort to avoid scrutiny.

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately.
